title: Research on Causal Robustness Enhancement Methods and Out-of-Distribution Generalization for Deep Classification Models
authors: Xiaodong Wang; Ling Jiang
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 6th International Conference on Computer Science and Management Technology
arch_detail: ResNet-50 backbone for all methods; generative model (diffusion) for counterfactual background-replacement samples
train_data_note: ImageNet-9 (background shift) and Waterbirds; no training set sizes reported
augmentation_type: counterfactual data augmentation via generative foreground-preserving background replacement
effect_size_notes: Paper reports approximate OOD Top-1 gains (12-16% vs standard, 6-8% vs CF-Aug) but no formal effect size; no ID accuracy reported so no gap derivable
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; sensitivity metrics S_out/S_rep are intervention robustness, not coherence
repr_analysis_finding: Measures representation/output sensitivity under background-replacement interventions: Standard S_out=0.243 S_rep=0.317, CF-Aug S_out=0.172 S_rep=0.205, CRO S_out=0.071 S_rep=0.089
relevance_sigma_justification: Tests causal-robustness training against OOD/spurious-correlation failure on ImageNet-9 and Waterbirds, quantifying OOD accuracy and sensitivity to background interventions, but does not address compositional generalization or the sigma-trap structural mechanism.
relevance_alignment_justification: Robustness to background/texture spurious correlations bears on reliable behavior under distribution shift, but the paper makes no explicit link to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Counterfactual quality depends on foreground-background separation and generative model accuracy, adding noise in complex scenes; causal sensitivity regularization adds computational overhead; real-world confounders are more diverse and harder to model explicitly.
open_questions_text: More automated and causally interpretable counterfactual generation; extend framework to detection, segmentation, and weakly supervised or self-supervised learning.
other_metrics_reported: Sensitivity metrics S_out/S_rep under background-replacement interventions
notes: Full CRO (counterfactual augmentation + sensitivity regularization + invariance constraints); OOD Top-1 66.2%

title: Feature-granularity-based spurious correlation and causal analysis in CNNs Exploring Feature Granularity to Uncover Spurious Correlations
authors: Xiaodong Wang; Gaiqun Zhang
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 2nd International Conference on Internet of Things and Cloud Computing Technology
arch_detail: Pretrained ResNet50 classifier over 1000 ImageNet classes; analysis method = superpixel segmentation, foreground-background separation, and linear regression on superpixel features
train_data_note: Uses pretrained ResNet50; ILSVRC2012 (ImageNet) validation set as sample dataset; no training described
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; feature contributions are quantified via linear-regression coefficients, not a coherence/compositionality measure
repr_analysis_finding: Identifies spurious correlations (e.g., category 'Bow tie' predicted from facial features although absent from the image); filling face/clothing regions via a generative model significantly decreased all top-3 category probabilities
relevance_sigma_justification: Discusses OOD generalization failure driven by spurious correlations (facial features causing 'Bow tie' prediction) but reports no OOD experiment or accuracy numbers; interpretability/analysis method only.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; paper targets CNN interpretability and spurious-correlation analysis for image classification deployment.
limitations_text: Stresses that a sufficiently large random sample size L is crucial for robust regression coefficients; notes models relying on non-causal features generalize poorly to OOD data and face interpretability limits in regulated deployment.
open_questions_text: Future work: optimize training methods to reduce reliance on non-causal features and design more interpretable, stable model frameworks for robustness on OOD data.
other_metrics_reported: Linear-regression main-effect coefficients (beta) and interaction terms (rj) per superpixel block; top-3 class probabilities before/after generative inpainting

title: Don't Blind Your VLA: Aligning Visual Representations for OOD Generalization
authors: Nikita Kachaev; Mikhail Kolosov; Daniil Zelezetsky; Alexey K. Kovalev; Aleksandr I. Panov
venue: Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
task_custom_name: VLA robotic manipulation (Simpler-based benchmark)
arch_detail: OpenVLA-style VLA models (pretrained VLM encoder-decoder) with action fine-tuning; vision teachers C-RADIOv3-ViT-L, DINOv2-ViT-L/G, Theia, SigLIP; normalized-sphere projection + teacher-embedding alignment
train_data_note: VLA action fine-tuning; linear-probe evaluation on reduced ImageNet-100 (top-1 accuracy); OOD eval on Simpler-based benchmark
schema_coherence_notes: Linear probing measures visual information retention, not a representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy
repr_analysis_finding: Naive action fine-tuning degrades VLM visual representations (linear-probe top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-100 drops vs the pretrained VLM); projecting mid-level VLA features onto a normalized sphere and aligning with teacher embeddings mitigates degradation and improves OOD generalization; attention maps analyzed
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies OOD generalization failure in VLA models: action fine-tuning degrades visual representations and generalization across Semantic/Vision/Execution axes, and visual alignment mitigates it. Does not address compositional generalization or the training-dynamics/schema-coherence mechanisms of the sigma-trap.
relevance_alignment_justification: Concerns capability preservation and OOD robustness of embodied robotic agents, tangentially relevant to goal misgeneralization in agentic AI, but contains no safety, alignment, or value-learning analysis.
limitations_text: Linear-probe evaluation uses a reduced ImageNet-100 due to computational constraints; probing without per-layer tuning so differences reflect representations only
other_metrics_reported: task success rate per environment (mean+/-SD over 128 seeds); linear-probe top-1 accuracy (ImageNet-100)
notes: Standard SFT (naive action fine-tuning), no visual alignment; success rates mean+/-SD per environment over 128 seeds (e.g., Carrot 0.49+/-0.02, Instruct 0.74+/-0.02); no single ID/OOD scalar attributable

title: Mitigating Dynamic Graph Distribution Shifts via Mixture of Variational Experts
authors: Qianyu Song; Chao Li; Yeyu Yan; Hui Zhou; Zhongying Zhao; Qingtian Zeng
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026
task_custom_name: Link prediction on continuous-time dynamic graphs
arch_detail: MoVE: Mixture of Variational Experts over a dynamic GNN backbone; hierarchical variational encoder extrapolates latent pseudo-environments, MoE with alignment and diversity-regularization losses; baselines ERM, IRM, CaNet, TGAT, TGN, GraphMixer, DyGFormer, FreeDyg, DIDA, SILD
train_data_note: Dynamic graphs: Amazon-Review, Reddit, UN Trade, UN Vote (real-world, continuous-time); also COLLAB and YELP in sensitivity analyses; train/test temporal splits
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; SDs over runs given as +/- in AP%
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; alignment loss is a training objective, not a measured proxy
relevance_sigma_justification: Addresses OOD generalization under distribution shifts for dynamic graph link prediction via invariant learning, but the failure mode is temporal/environmental distribution shift, not compositional generalization, and no compositional structure or schema coherence is examined.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the invariant-representation objective targets OOD robustness on graph link prediction, with no discussion of alignment or safety implications.
limitations_text: Primary limitation is the implicit interpretability of learned pseudo-environments, whose semantics remain implicit; authors defer more explainable representations to future work.
open_questions_text: Development of more explainable representations of the pseudo-environments; the paper leaves this for further exploration.
notes: Train 98.75 +/-0.24 AP%, Test 95.46 +/-0.24 AP%; ERM baseline Test 67.98 +/-0.72

title: Causal Disentangled Recommendation against User Preference Shifts
authors: Wenjie Wang; Xinyu Lin; Liuhui Wang; Fuli Feng; Yunshan Ma; Tat-Seng Chua
task_custom_name: Recommendation under user preference shifts (Yelp, Book, Electronics)
arch_detail: Temporal VAE; MLP encoder g_phi and decoder with FC layers f_theta1/f_lambda; learnable matrices W_z/W_x for sparse influence; hidden dims of e_t/z_t/g_phi tuned in {200,300,400}; g_phi widths [200]/[400]/[800]/[800,500]
train_data_note: Three recommendation datasets (Yelp, Book, Electronics); user interaction sequences split into chronological environments; preference assumed stable within each short period
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy (probing, CKA, RSA, compositionality score) measured; KL/Euclidean analysis is a case-study alignment check, not a coherence metric
repr_analysis_finding: Euclidean distance between learned user representations tracks KL divergence of category-level interaction distributions across consecutive environments, showing CDR captures preference shifts in user representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Frames user preference shift as an OOD generalization problem via causal-graph environment modeling and temporal distribution shifts, but is distant from compositional generalization and the sigma-trap thesis; no treatment of training dynamics, flatness, or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper concerns robust recommendation quality under user preference shifts only.
limitations_text: Category-level preference is non-trivial to recover from pure interaction data; performance drops when parameters grow (g_phi widened from [800] to [800,500] hurts); hidden sizes must be carefully tuned to balance representation ability and over-fitting
open_questions_text: Explore more inference strategies to capture temporal patterns (current third strategy partially considers shifts but loses temporal patterns); incorporating item category into recommender models to help disentanglement
other_metrics_reported: Recall@10; NDCG@10
notes: No quantitative main-table results in excerpt; only qualitative ablations (multi-objective loss coefficients, category number C, hidden sizes) and case study

title: Abstraction Alignment: Comparing Model-Learned and Human-Encoded Conceptual Relationships
authors: Angie Boggust; Hyemin Bang; Hendrik Strobelt; Arvind Satyanarayan
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
task_custom_name: MLM specificity prediction (S-TEST); ICD-9 clinical coding case study
arch_detail: Evaluates bert-base/large, roberta-base/large, gpt-2 on S-TEST occupation/location/birthplace specificity tasks; abstraction alignment methodology builds abstraction graphs of human concepts and measures how much model uncertainty they explain
train_data_note: Pretrained LMs evaluated on S-TEST dataset; clinical coding case study uses MIMIC-III with ICD-9 codes
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; quantitative results are A@10 and subgraph-preference probabilities
schema_coherence_notes: Alignment is measured at the behavior/confidence level against human abstraction graphs, not via a representation-level coherence proxy over model internals
repr_analysis_finding: Models show strong preference for specific answers when evaluated over full abstraction graphs (bert-large prefers a specific answer on over 80% of instances), contradicting prior two-answer metrics; gpt-2 has lowest accuracy/specificity but highest preference for correctness
relevance_sigma_justification: Positions learned abstractions as informing a model's ability to generalize to new data, but all evaluations are in-distribution specificity benchmarks (S-TEST, ICD-9 coding); no compositional or OOD generalization measurements are made.
relevance_alignment_justification: Directly targets human-AI alignment: abstraction alignment quantifies how much of a model's uncertainty is explained by human-encoded conceptual relationships, is framed against societal and regulatory alignment demands, and provides experts audit tools to locate where model behavior diverges from human abstractions; it does not, however, address goal misgeneralization or safety-critical failures.
open_questions_text: Experts hypothesized abstraction alignment could improve model generation by selecting the most specific concept above a confidence threshold instead of the most probable (often overly specific and incorrect) answer; generated new hypotheses for specificity analysis.
other_metrics_reported: A@10 (accuracy at 10); subgraph preference P(s,g), P(s-down, s-up), P(s-relation, t); expert evaluation studies

title: Evading the Simplicity Bias: Training a Diverse Set of Models Discovers Solutions with Superior OOD Generalization
authors: D. Teney; E. Abbasnejad; S. Lucey; A. Van den Hengel
venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
arch_detail: ResNet-18 feature extractor (highly optimized); collections of 64 models with a penalty on alignment of input gradients
train_data_note: PACS (4 domains: art, cartoon, photo, sketch; leave-one-out DG); VLCS used for zero-shot cross-dataset transfer
effect_size_notes: Raw deltas (84.48 vs 85.14 on PACS; 82.9 vs 84.2 best-single-model) reported as mean differences only; no formal effect size reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; gradient-alignment penalty acts on input gradients, not a coherence measure
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates OOD generalization failure (the sigma-trap): attributes it to the SGD simplicity bias latching on spurious features, then shows a gradient-alignment regularizer plus model selection evades it, improving PACS domain-shift accuracy (82.9->84.2 best single model) and VLCS transfer; however it targets domain shift rather than compositional splits.
relevance_alignment_justification: Robustness to spurious correlations and domain shift matters for reliable deployed models, but the paper makes no connection to AI alignment, safety frameworks, or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: No guarantee a robust predictor is found; number of models and regularizer strength are key hyperparameters; too few models entangle robust and spurious features, too many fragment robust solutions; approach requires a separate model selection stage.
open_questions_text: Future work: encourage learning a 'basis' of elemental predictors via sparsity/complementarity and search for optimal combinations, resembling disentanglement but operating on ERM-optimized predictors.
other_metrics_reported: AUC (VLCS horse/person zero-shot detection, averaged over two classes)
notes: PACS leave-one-out, 64 independent models, no regularizer; mean accuracy +/- std over five runs (Table 3)

title: Data Distributional Properties As Inductive Bias for Systematic Generalization
authors: F. del Rio; A. Raymond-Saez; D. Florea; R. T. Icarte; J. Hurtado; C. B. Calderon; A. Soto
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
task_custom_name: Multi-attribute prediction (color/shape/size/material) on synthetic object-rendered images with textual attribute sequences
arch_detail: Multi-modal language model taking image plus textual attribute sequence as input; hidden size ablated 32-256; systematic generalization evaluated by holding out latent attribute combinations
train_data_note: Synthetic dataset of rendered objects with latent attributes (color count 8/27/64/125/216); diversity, burstiness, and latent intervention manipulate training distribution; Dtest-ID vs Dtest-OOD splits
augmentation_type: latent intervention (random alteration of a latent factor during training); burstiness restricts latent values per input
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; headline results are accuracy deltas (89% absolute OOD gain from diversity) and Pearson correlations of p-scores with OOD performance
schema_coherence_notes: Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between latent attributes in the training distribution is strongly predictive of OOD generalization; lower NMI induces parallelism in neural representations (input features coded in parallel neural vectors)
repr_analysis_finding: Representation parallelism (p-scores) strongly correlates with OOD performance on the shape task: AVG r=0.73 (p=1.88e-9), DIV r=0.76 (p=7.17e-4), BURST r=0.69 (p=5.5e-3), LI r=0.73 (p=3.45e-5)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies systematic (compositional) generalization failure, the sigma-trap: baseline models learn shape-color combinations as features so OOD accuracy collapses (shape 0.6% OOD), while data distributional properties (diversity, burstiness, latent intervention) and representation geometry (NMI, parallelism) predict and promote OOD generalization.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment or safety; the work concerns inducing systematic generalization via data properties and representation geometry, with no discussion of goal misgeneralization or safety implications.
other_metrics_reported: NMI between latent attributes; p-score (representation parallelism); Pearson correlations of p-scores with OOD performance
notes: OOD accuracy collapses to 0.6%: model learns shape-color combinations as features rather than systematic generalization (Table 2/3)

venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
task_custom_name: Multi-attribute prediction (color/shape/size/material) on synthetic object-rendered images with textual attribute sequences
arch_detail: Multi-modal language model taking image plus textual attribute sequence as input; hidden size ablated 32-256; systematic generalization evaluated by holding out latent attribute combinations
train_data_note: Synthetic dataset of rendered objects with latent attributes (color count 8/27/64/125/216); diversity, burstiness, and latent intervention manipulate training distribution; Dtest-ID vs Dtest-OOD splits
augmentation_type: latent intervention (random alteration of a latent factor during training); burstiness restricts latent values per input
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; headline results are accuracy deltas (89% absolute OOD gain from diversity) and Pearson correlations of p-scores with OOD performance
schema_coherence_notes: Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between latent attributes in the training distribution is strongly predictive of OOD generalization; lower NMI induces parallelism in neural representations (input features coded in parallel neural vectors)
repr_analysis_finding: Representation parallelism (p-scores) strongly correlates with OOD performance on the shape task: AVG r=0.73 (p=1.88e-9), DIV r=0.76 (p=7.17e-4), BURST r=0.69 (p=5.5e-3), LI r=0.73 (p=3.45e-5)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies systematic (compositional) generalization failure, the sigma-trap: baseline models learn shape-color combinations as features so OOD accuracy collapses (shape 0.6% OOD), while data distributional properties (diversity, burstiness, latent intervention) and representation geometry (NMI, parallelism) predict and promote OOD generalization.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment or safety; the work concerns inducing systematic generalization via data properties and representation geometry, with no discussion of goal misgeneralization or safety implications.
other_metrics_reported: NMI between latent attributes; p-score (representation parallelism); Pearson correlations of p-scores with OOD performance
notes: Altering color hue randomly during training gains up to 15% OOD accuracy over baseline (Table 6)
experiment_label: Shape task; latent intervention jitter 0.05, 216 colors

title: Complexity Control Facilitates Reasoning-Based Compositional Generalization in Transformers
authors: Z. Zhang; P. Lin; Z. Wang; Y. Zhang; Z. -Q. John Xu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
task_custom_name: Key+Anchor arithmetic compositional task (addition over anchors with noise tokens)
arch_detail: GPT-2 model for main experiments; two-layer single-head transformer for mechanism analysis; parameter initialization scale controlled by rate gamma (std (1/din)^gamma) and weight decay coefficient 0.01 default
train_data_note: Key+Anchor arithmetic: training samples (key, a1, a2) with noise tokens; ID test on seen anchor pairs, OOD test on unseen anchor pairs; also validated on image-generation and NLP tasks
schema_coherence_notes: No coherence/compositionality score computed; PCA/TSNE clustering and attention masking are representational analyses, not a coherence proxy
repr_analysis_finding: PCA/TSNE of output embeddings shows Phase-1 models entangle anchor-pair representations while Phase-2/3 form well-separated clusters; masking key-token and anchor circuits isolates each token's contribution; reasoning-based solutions exhibit lower complexity bias via neuron condensation
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates the sigma-trap: transformers show good ID but poor OOD compositional generalization (Phase 2). Shows complexity control (init scale, weight decay) decides whether models learn reasoning rules or memorize mappings, and dissects internal mechanisms via attention masking, PCA/TSNE, and neuron-condensation complexity analysis.
relevance_alignment_justification: Relevant to alignment via interpretability: distinguishing genuine compositional reasoning from memorized mappings and revealing internal circuits informs capability assessment and goal-misgeneralization risk, though the paper carries no explicit safety or alignment framing.
open_questions_text: Critical open questions: whether transformers genuinely learn compositional primitives within the data or primarily memorize input-output mappings; whether their errors on compositional tasks are systematic or reflect a deeper lack of reasoning structure
other_metrics_reported: commutativity probability on unseen anchor pairs (c,d)/(d,c); neuron condensation complexity metrics; ID/OOD test accuracy (figures)
notes: GPT-2 on Key+Anchor compositional task, weight decay 0.01, init rate gamma varied; phase transitions by ID/OOD accuracy reported only in figures

title: Handling Out-of-Distribution Data: A Survey
authors: L. Tamang; M. R. Bouadjenek; R. Dazeley; S. Aryal
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
arch_detail: Survey spanning CNN, RNN, Transformer, MLP, GNN, and diffusion methods across vision, NLP, and LLM domains; no single architecture evaluated
train_data_note: No training runs; reviews detection/measurement/mitigation methods for covariate and concept shift across many datasets and domains
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured; survey does not run experiments
relevance_sigma_justification: Systematically reviews detection, measurement, and mitigation of covariate and concept/domain shifts, the broad OOD generalization failure space that subsumes the sigma-trap, though it provides no experiments on compositional generalization or training dynamics.
relevance_alignment_justification: Highlights safety-critical failures under distribution shift (medical diagnosis, autonomous driving) and high-confidence incorrect outputs in open-world settings, but does not engage AI alignment or goal misgeneralization directly.
limitations_text: Covariate vs semantic shift dichotomy is overly simplistic for practice; in real applications shifts occur simultaneously and are intertwined, so segregated handling may be inefficient or insufficient.
open_questions_text: Calls for a holistic framework that handles both covariate and semantic shifts simultaneously under one cohesive framework; urges a model that performs well under all shift types.
other_metrics_reported: Catalogues evaluation metrics used across surveyed works: AUC, AUROC, AUPR, FPR/FPR95, Accuracy, F1, NMI, OSCR, IoU, misclassification error, BWT/FWT, perplexity
notes: Survey with no experiments; single placeholder sub-experiment emitted per contract (no quantitative results to report)

title: The Many Faces of Robustness: A Critical Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: D. Hendrycks; S. Basart; N. Mu; S. Kadavath; F. Wang; E. Dorundo; R. Desai; T. Zhu; S. Parajuli; M. Guo; D. Song; J. Steinhardt; J. Gilmer
venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
arch_detail: ResNet-50 baselines; ResNeXt; self-attention variants; WSL pretraining with 1000x labeled data; DeepAugment+AugMix augmentation method
train_data_note: ImageNet-R: 30,000 test images of renditions (paintings, embroidery, etc.); SVSF: storefronts w/ location/year/camera metadata; DFR: DeepFashion2 shifts in occlusion/orientation/zoom/scale; Real Blurry: 1,000 blurry images of 100 ImageNet classes
augmentation_type: DeepAugment+AugMix diverse data augmentation
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; only directional findings (e.g., DeepAugment+AugMix on ResNet-50 gives approx 19-point ImageNet-C accuracy increase; larger models help on Real Blurry/ImageNet-C/ImageNet-R but not DFR)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly evaluates OOD generalization across four real-world distribution shifts (style, blur, geography, camera operation) and arbitrates robustness hypotheses (e.g., texture bias), showing no method consistently improves robustness; but no compositional splits or sigma-trap-specific analysis.
relevance_alignment_justification: Frames robustness evaluation as groundwork for systems that 'robustly generalize in safety-critical settings', a safety-adjacent motivation, but does not engage with alignment, goal misgeneralization, or agentic safety.
open_questions_text: Future research must study multiple distribution shifts simultaneously since no evaluated method consistently improves robustness; community should evaluate future methods on multiple shifts (e.g., at least ImageNet-C and ImageNet-R).
notes: No point estimates in excerpt; only directional intervention results across ImageNet-C/-R, SVSF, DFR, Real Blurry Images

title: A System-Level Analysis of Cross-Domain Generalization Failure in Audio Deepfake Detection
authors: S. Oyucu; B. Arslan; S. Sagiroglu
task_custom_name: Audio deepfake detection (REAL vs FAKE binary classification)
arch_detail: Five hybrid architectures: CNN-LSTM, TCN, TCN-LSTM, Conformer, TCM-Conformer; each combined with four feature extractors (MFCC, Wav2Vec 2.0, HuBERT, HeAR)
train_data_note: Four acoustic domains: ASVspoof 2019 (LA), ASVspoof 2021 (DF), DEEP-VOICE (RVC voice conversion), In-the-Wild; 320 cross-domain train-test configurations
repr_analysis_finding: t-SNE of feature spaces: genuine/fake clusters well-separated in-domain but interleaved and positionally shifted under cross-domain transfer; In-the-Wild shows the most fragmented structure; feature-space shift identified as the dominant failure mechanism
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly documents the sigma-trap: in-domain accuracy up to 99.98% collapsing to 5.55% (below chance) under cross-domain shift across 320 configurations, with architecture-invariant degradation, single-class bias (Recall~1.000), and within-benchmark-family drops of 18.5pp; a quantitative portrait of OOD generalization failure, though on acoustic domains rather than compositional tasks.
relevance_alignment_justification: Deepfake detection supports security and information-integrity applications (voice authentication, fraud prevention) and the paper emphasizes deployment reliability, but it does not discuss AI alignment, safety mechanisms, or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Paper explicitly acknowledges study limitations (Section V) and notes that class-imbalanced test partitions can coincide with numerically high accuracy, making recall the more diagnostic metric.
open_questions_text: Directions for future research identified: develop domain-invariant features and explicit alignment mechanisms rather than increasing architectural complexity alone.
other_metrics_reported: Recall (near-total fake prediction, Recall~1.000 under single-class bias); inference latency 0.001-0.052 ms/sample; throughput ~27,000-361,000 samples/s
notes: CNN-LSTM with Wav2Vec 2.0, trained on ASVspoof 2021, evaluated on ASVspoof 2019: 71.26% -> 52.72% (drop of 18.5 percentage points, reported directly)

title: Spatial-DiT: Generalizable 3D Visuomotor Policy for Cross-Object Manipulation via Multi-Scale Spatial Fusion
authors: Z. Junjie; W. Jin; L. Xiaofei; Z. Haiyun; L. Guodong
task_custom_name: Robotic manipulation (pick-and-place, water pouring)
arch_detail: Spatial-DiT: Multi-scale Pyramid Encoder (MPE) + Multi-scale Fusion (MSF) over point clouds, Diffusion Transformer (DiT) for multimodal action generation, Delta 6D Pose action space; baselines: Diffusion Policy, IDP3, ResNet-50, PointNet
train_data_note: 25-object dataset (15 training types); pouring task uses 200 human demonstration trajectories recorded in Cartesian SE(3)
train_regime_other: Behavior cloning / imitation learning; diffusion policy training
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; comparisons are descriptive success rates
schema_coherence_notes: Feature-clustering analysis measures geometric discriminative power, not representation-level coherence/compositionality
repr_analysis_finding: Feature clustering experiment under strong texture interference: Spatial-DiT MPE features form tight geometry-based clusters (intra-class 0.28, inter-class 2.45, DR 8.75), outperforming ResNet-50 (DR 1.41) and PointNet (DR 5.00), confirming texture-invariant geometric feature extraction
relevance_sigma_justification: Studies zero-shot OOD generalization in robotic manipulation (unseen instances, unseen categories, cross-embodiment): 2D shortcut-learning policies fail under texture/color shift while 3D geometric features generalize (88.3% average success). Speaks to shortcut-driven OOD failure but not compositional generalization or training dynamics.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an embodied manipulation generalization paper.
limitations_text: Performance drops below 40% in complex semantic scenarios with visually similar distractors; policy struggles with fine-grained semantic disambiguation and requires high-level cognitive guidance to resolve logical/semantic conflicts
other_metrics_reported: Feature discriminative power: intra-class distance 0.28, inter-class distance 2.45, DR 8.75 (Table I); cross-embodiment pouring success 18/20 (xArm6), 17/20 (Kenbei); complex-mode success 8/20, 7/20; positional error ~1 cm
notes: Success rate 95.0% over 20 trials

task_custom_name: Robotic manipulation (pick-and-place, water pouring)
arch_detail: Spatial-DiT: Multi-scale Pyramid Encoder (MPE) + Multi-scale Fusion (MSF) over point clouds, Diffusion Transformer (DiT) for multimodal action generation, Delta 6D Pose action space; baselines: Diffusion Policy, IDP3, ResNet-50, PointNet
train_data_note: 25-object dataset (15 training types); pouring task uses 200 human demonstration trajectories recorded in Cartesian SE(3)
train_regime_other: Behavior cloning / imitation learning; diffusion policy training
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; comparisons are descriptive success rates
schema_coherence_notes: Feature-clustering analysis measures geometric discriminative power, not representation-level coherence/compositionality
repr_analysis_finding: Feature clustering experiment under strong texture interference: Spatial-DiT MPE features form tight geometry-based clusters (intra-class 0.28, inter-class 2.45, DR 8.75), outperforming ResNet-50 (DR 1.41) and PointNet (DR 5.00), confirming texture-invariant geometric feature extraction
relevance_sigma_justification: Studies zero-shot OOD generalization in robotic manipulation (unseen instances, unseen categories, cross-embodiment): 2D shortcut-learning policies fail under texture/color shift while 3D geometric features generalize (88.3% average success). Speaks to shortcut-driven OOD failure but not compositional generalization or training dynamics.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an embodied manipulation generalization paper.
limitations_text: Performance drops below 40% in complex semantic scenarios with visually similar distractors; policy struggles with fine-grained semantic disambiguation and requires high-level cognitive guidance to resolve logical/semantic conflicts
other_metrics_reported: Feature discriminative power: intra-class distance 0.28, inter-class distance 2.45, DR 8.75 (Table I); cross-embodiment pouring success 18/20 (xArm6), 17/20 (Kenbei); complex-mode success 8/20, 7/20; positional error ~1 cm
notes: 2D baseline; success rate 30.0% over 20 trials

title: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Improving Domain Generalization in Image Classification
authors: S. Addepalli; A. R. Asokan; L. Sharma; R. V. Babu
venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
arch_detail: Student ViT-B/16 ImageNet-1K init; teacher CLIP ViT-B/16 (VLM); VL2V-ADiP align-distill-predict
train_data_note: DomainBed DG benchmarks: OfficeHome, PACS, VLCS, TerraIncognita, DomainNet; 5000 iters (15000 DN), Adam lr 5e-5
train_regime_other: black-box VLM distillation (align, distill, predict) + fine-tuning
effect_size_notes: Avg-OOD reported across DG benchmarks; per-benchmark in sub_experiments
schema_coherence_notes: No schema coherence proxy; representation alignment between VLM and student is measured via distillation losses
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures OOD (domain) generalization gap in image classification and tests an intervention (VLM distillation) that improves OOD accuracy while retaining ID performance; measures one sigma-trap component but does not address flatness, schema coherence, or compositional failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment framing; robust OOD generalization in a safety-adjacent sense (deployment under distribution shift) but not connected to alignment failure or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Assumes black-box access to VLM teacher; gains depend on teacher quality; tested on image classification only; fixed seed 0 for main results with 3 re-runs for a subset.
notes: Avg-ID 73.97, Avg-OOD 75.48 (Table 3, fixed seed 0); DG benchmark average

title: Roses are Red, Violets are Blue… But Should VQA expect Them To?
authors: C. Kervadec; G. Antipov; M. Baccouche; C. Wolf
venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
task_custom_name: Visual Question Answering (GQA-OOD benchmark)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: head/tail answer frequency (alpha) within question groups
arch_detail: LXMERT (BERT-based multimodal); compared with Q.Prior LSTM, LSTM, BUTD (Faster R-CNN+LSTM), MCAN, BAN4, MMN; bias-reduction variants RUBi, RUBi+QB, LM, BP applied to BUTD
train_data_note: GQA-OOD benchmark: distribution shifts tailored to question groups with highly imbalanced answer distributions (head alpha>1.2, tail alpha<0.7); testdev split
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; head-tail confusion percentages reported (LXMERT confuses 25% of answers at alpha=1.2, 42% at alpha=0.3)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy; analysis is at the behavioral level (head/tail answer distributions, reasoning-label estimation)
relevance_sigma_justification: Studies OOD generalization failure in VQA under head/tail answer-frequency shifts, showing models exploit dataset biases rather than reason (Clever Hans effects), but the shift is label-frequency based, not compositional, and no compositional structure is analyzed.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment or safety; the work targets benchmark evaluation and bias exploitation in VQA with no discussion of alignment implications or goal misgeneralization.
open_questions_text: Authors conclude future efforts on model capacity to answer open questions (query type) should be fruitful and provide recommendations for future research directions on infrequent concepts.
other_metrics_reported: acc-head; head/tail confusion; overall accuracy on VQA2, GQA, VQA-CP2 for cross-benchmark comparison
notes: acc-all 54.6%, acc-tail 48.0%, acc-head 55.5% (Table 3a); confuses head/tail answers for 25% of questions at alpha=1.2 up to 42% at alpha=0.3

title: General Greedy De-Bias Learning
authors: X. Han; S. Wang; C. Su; Q. Huang; Q. Tian
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
task_custom_name: Biased-MNIST digit classification; Adversarial SQuAD question answering; VQA-CP v2 / GQA-OOD visual question answering
arch_detail: Base model ResNet-18 (Biased-MNIST); BiDAF base model for Adversarial SQuAD; VQA base models for VQA-CP v2/GQA-OOD. Biased models: SimpleNet-1x1 (background-color input), bg (ground-truth background image), self-ensemble (GGDse). Greedy training of biased + base models
train_data_note: Biased-MNIST with spurious background-color bias at rho_train=0.999; SQuAD train/val with adversarial AddSent/AddSentOne splits; VQA-CP v2 train 438,183 / test 219,928 samples
schema_coherence_notes: Per-class accuracy heatmaps (Fig. 3) analyze which correlations the model captures, but no representation-level coherence proxy is measured
repr_analysis_finding: Per-class accuracy matrices (diagnostic heat-maps) show vanilla ResNet-18 captures spurious background-color correlation while GGD relies little on background color
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses OOD generalization failure driven by spurious correlations: greedy de-bias training of biased plus base models improves OOD accuracy on extremely biased data (68% vs roughly 6x lower baseline on Biased-MNIST rho=0.999) across vision, QA, and VQA, but it is not about compositional generalization and no training-dynamics or schema-coherence analysis is given.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a robustness/de-bias learning method paper with no safety discussion.
limitations_text: GGD sometimes over-estimates the bias level and degrades on in-distribution test; GGDgs ID accuracy is significantly lower than baseline ResNet-18; GGDse gs is unstable in later training stages with large variance; the variance is reduced by Curriculum Regularization (lambda_t schedule)
open_questions_text: A better biased model that can access word-level similarity may achieve better Adversarial SQuAD performance without extra training data; self-ensemble GGDse shown as more flexible when task-specific bias models are unavailable
other_metrics_reported: F1 on Adversarial SQuAD (OOD) and SQuAD v1 (ID)
notes: Table I: GGD1crk 68% OOD accuracy on unbiased test (rho_test=0) under rho_train=0.999, over 6x the baseline model; mean of 4 repeated experiments under different random seeds

title: Three approaches to facilitate invariant neurons and generalization to out-of-distribution orientations and illuminations
authors: Sakai, A.; Sunagawa, T.; Madan, S.; Suzuki, K.; Katoh, T.; Kobashi, H.; Pfister, H.; Sinha, P.; Boix, X.; Sasaki, T.
task_custom_name: Object recognition under OOD orientations and illuminations (modified MNIST, modified iLab, CarsCG, MiscGoods)
arch_detail: DNN with batch-normalization layers and a last ReLU layer; concrete architecture (CNN/MLP depth, width) not specified in excerpt
train_data_note: Four datasets: modified MNIST, modified iLab, CarsCG (3D rendered cars), MiscGoods (controlled orientations/illuminations); results aggregated across InD data diversity levels; no sizes in excerpt
effect_size_notes: No absolute accuracies or effect sizes in excerpt; only relative improvement frequencies and win counts
schema_coherence_proxy_other: SI score (selectivity and invariance of intermediate-layer neurons)
schema_coherence_notes: SI score of last ReLU layer correlates with OoD accuracy (Pearson r = 0.891); P(SI increase): late-stopping 50.0%, tuned BN 83.3%, invariance loss 83.3%; no absolute SI values in excerpt
repr_analysis_finding: Individual intermediate-layer neurons become invariant to orientations/illuminations as OoD accuracy improves; SI-score increases precede OoD accuracy gains (P(acc increase | SI increase): late-stopping 83.3%, tuned BN 80.0%, invariance loss 100.0%); t-SNE shows category clustering consistent with neural invariance
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies OOD generalization failure under novel orientations and illuminations and identifies a representation-level mechanism (invariant, selective neurons) driving OoD gains, linking a schema-coherence-style neural measure (SI score) to generalization with causal-ordered evidence; highly relevant to the sigma-trap's OOD-failure plus schema-coherence components, though the shift is covariate rather than compositional.
relevance_alignment_justification: Frames poor OoD generalization as a barrier to safe and fair AI applications and studies neural invariance as a basis for it, but does not engage with alignment, goal misgeneralization, or value specification.
limitations_text: Authors note the SI score may not precisely capture the emergence of selectivity/invariance, so another mechanism may underlie OoD gains when the SI score does not increase; paper is limited in answering whether the approaches generalize beyond orientations/illuminations and how they relate to biological learning.
open_questions_text: Whether the three approaches extend to OoD factors beyond orientations/illuminations; how they relate to biological learning systems; novel mechanisms to explain OoD gains when the SI score does not increase.
other_metrics_reported: SI score (selectivity and invariance)
notes: P(OoD accuracy increases)=75.0% (9/12); P(SI increases)=50.0% (6/12); P(OoD acc increase | SI increase)=83.3% (5/6); no absolute accuracies

title: A two-stage co-adversarial perturbation to mitigate out-of-distribution generalization of large-scale graph
authors: Wang, Y.; Xue, H.; Wang, X.
task_custom_name: graph node classification on large-scale graphs (ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-proteins, ogbn-products, Pubmed, Yelp)
arch_detail: GNN backbones GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT with public implementations; CAP = two-stage co-adversarial perturbation (alternating weight and feature perturbation, T=3 steps); mini-batch subgraph sampling (NS, Cluster, SAINT)
train_data_note: OOD induced by mini-batch subgraph sampling: training subgraphs differ vastly in size/structure from test graphs; Yelp has over 700,000 nodes; standard splits for ogbn-* and Yelp, 60/20/20 random node split (10 runs) for Pubmed
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; reports raw deltas (e.g., CAP avg improvement up to 1.0%; +2.5% over GCN+FLAG on ogbn-proteins; CAP lifts test performance by avg 0.99% with Cluster sampling)
repr_analysis_finding: Examined weight and feature loss landscapes: GNNs get trapped in sharp local minima, causing suboptimal OOD generalization; CAP alternately smooths weight and feature loss landscapes
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets OOD generalization failure in GNNs via sharp-minima analysis and co-adversarial training on large-scale graphs, empirically quantifying OOD improvements, though the shift type is sampling-induced rather than compositional or schema-driven.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, goal misgeneralization, or societal impact; purely a graph OOD generalization method paper.
other_metrics_reported: ROC-AUC (ogbn-proteins, Yelp); test performance of best validation epoch
notes: Test accuracy (Acc), mean +/- SD over 10 runs

title: Invariant Graph Transformer for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Liao, T.; Zhang, Z.; Sun, Y.; Hu, C.; Li, J.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
task_custom_name: Graph classification under distribution shift (GOOD-Motif, GOOD-HIV, GOOD-SST2, GOOD-Twitter, DrugOOD)
arch_detail: GOODFormer: graph Transformer with entropy-guided invariant subgraph disentangler, evolving subgraph positional/structural encoder, and invariant learning module; baselines: Graphormer, GraphGPS, EXPHORMER, GNN+ERM/IRM/VREx, DIR, GREA, GIL, GSAT, CIGA, iMoLD, CAL+
train_data_note: GOOD benchmarks: GOOD-Motif (basis/size splits), GOOD-HIV (scaffold), GOOD-SST2 (length), GOOD-Twitter (length), DrugOOD (assay)
schema_coherence_notes: Invariant-subgraph discovery is evaluated via Precision@10 against ground-truth subgraphs (a structural identifiability check), not a representation-level coherence proxy
repr_analysis_finding: Invariant subgraph identification on GOOD-Motif basis split: GOODFormer Precision@10 = 0.698 +/- 0.069 vs DIR 0.203, GSAT 0.396, CIGA 0.247; qualitative visualizations of learned invariant subgraphs (Figure 2)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses OOD generalization failure on graphs: shows existing graph Transformers fail under distribution shift (e.g., EXPHORMER 46.44 vs GOODFormer 81.97 on GOOD-Motif basis) and proposes invariant subgraph learning to close the gap; theoretical justifications provided; graph-domain focus rather than compositional NLP.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an OOD generalization method and benchmark evaluation paper.
other_metrics_reported: ROC-AUC (GOOD-HIV, DrugOOD); Precision@10 for ground-truth invariant subgraph discovery; hyper-parameter sensitivity analyses
notes: Test-set accuracy 81.97 +/- 16.74 (reported as variance); +- values are variances

title: Producing plankton classifiers that are robust to dataset shift
authors: Chen, C.; Kyathanahally, S.P.; Reyes, M.; Merkli, S.; Merz, E.; Francazi, E.; Hoege, M.; Pomati, F.; Baity-Jesi, M.
task_custom_name: ZooLake plankton image classification (dark-field lake plankton, species recognition)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: Hellinger distance (feature space) for compositional shift; dy class-distribution shift
arch_detail: BEsT: ensemble of BEiT vision transformers with targeted augmentations, geometric ensembling, rotation-based test-time augmentation; MobileNet compared (92% ID, 77% OOD)
train_data_note: ZooLake dark-field images of lake plankton; 10 manually-annotated deployment days as OOD test cells
augmentation_type: Targeted augmentations for OOD robustness; rotation-based test-time augmentation; geometric ensembling
effect_size_notes: Drops reported as absolute accuracy differences (e.g., MobileNet 92% ID to 77% OOD); no formal effect sizes
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy of the trained models; shift quantification uses handcrafted CV descriptors and PCA in input space
repr_analysis_finding: PCA over 67 computer-vision image descriptors with Hellinger distance to quantify distributional vs compositional dataset shift and pinpoint image features (e.g., blurriness, cropping) that degrade classification; input-space analysis, not model internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies generalization failure under dataset shift (the sigma-trap): documents ID-to-OOD accuracy drops (e.g., MobileNet 92% to 77%), decomposes shift into distributional vs compositional components via Hellinger distance, and builds a three-step diagnostic pipeline yielding BEsT (83% OOD); empirical and systematic, though limited to one plankton dataset and deployment shift rather than compositional splits.
relevance_alignment_justification: Applied ecology monitoring paper on plankton classifier robustness; no connection to AI alignment, safety frameworks, or goal misgeneralization.
other_metrics_reported: Per-class precision/recall/F1; macro and micro F1; NMAE; Bray-Curtis dissimilarity; abundance quantification bias
notes: MobileNet nominal test accuracy 92% vs 77% OOD on deployment test cells (example of ID-to-OOD drop)

title: MiMu: mitigating multiple shortcut learning behavior of transformers
authors: Zhao, L.; Liu, Q.; Chen, W.; Chen, L.; Sun, R.; Hou, M.; Wang, Y.; Wang, S.; Ren, P.; Zhou, J.
arch_detail: BERT-base-uncased (NLP: hidden 768, AdamW lr 2e-5-5e-5, batch 64, 20 epochs, max len 128); ViT-Large-Patch16-224-in21k (CV: hidden 1024, SGD lr 1e-3-1e-4, batch 64, 90 epochs); MiMu adds self-calibration and self-improvement (random attention mask + adaptive attention alignment)
train_data_note: NLP: MNLI (matched/mismatched), HANS, QQP, PAWS (duplicate-label shortcut); CV: IN-9-W and IN-200-W with background/watermark shortcuts (Rand-B, Rand-W, Rand-B+W, IN-B, IN-R, IN-R+W)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; improvements reported as accuracy deltas (e.g. +9.2% Hans, +6.79% Rand-B+W, +3.78% IN-R+W)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Saliency maps reveal diverse and unknown shortcuts (watermark or background) relied on by ViT-Large; MiMu aligns target-model attention weights to a calibrated source model via adaptive attention alignment without post-hoc supervision
relevance_sigma_justification: Addresses OOD generalization failure from shortcut (spurious correlation) learning in Transformers across NLP and CV, showing models rely on multiple shortcuts and proposing MiMu to mitigate them, but the failure mode is spurious-correlation robustness, not compositional generalization, and no compositional structure is analyzed.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment or safety; the work targets robustness of Transformers to shortcut learning with no discussion of alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization.
other_metrics_reported: top-1 accuracy (CV); ECE calibration scores on MNLI (Fig 6); accuracy on PAWS duplicated/non-duplicated subsets
notes: Table 5: MNLI d-m 0.832, d-mm 0.838, Hans 0.707; text: +9.2% on Hans, +0.4% on mismatch vs ERM without hurting IID

title: Measuring and Improving Compositional Generalization in Text-to-SQL via Component Alignment
authors: Gan, Y.; Chen, X.; Huang, Q.; Purver, M.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2022 - Findings
task_custom_name: Text-to-SQL semantic parsing (Spider / Spider-SS / Spider-CG)
arch_detail: RAT-SQL family (RATSQLG, RATSQLB, RATSQL) with/without NatSQL and with sentence-split training subscript (S); GNN baseline; BERT-based relation-aware transformer encoder; RATSQLB(S) required LR 7.444e-04->1e-04 and BERT LR 3e-06->1e-05
train_data_note: Spider-SS: Spider split into clause-aligned sub-sentences (NatSQL normalization); Spider-CG: compositional recombinations (substitution CG-SUB, appending CG-APP); every sub-sentence seen during training yet OOD recombinations fail
augmentation_type: Clause-level synthetic example generation: Spider-SS segmentation and Spider-CG composition (substitution and appending of sub-sentences); (S) models trained on segmented Spider-SS data
effect_size_notes: Paper reports relative OOD degradation of 10-30% on CG-APPT/CG-APPD but no absolute OOD accuracy in excerpt
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; sub-sentence/SQL clause alignment is a data-construction property, not a measured representation metric
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures the core sigma-trap phenomenon: models degrade on Spider-CG OOD compositional recombinations (about 10-30% drop) even though every sub-sentence appeared in training, and shows clause-level segmentation training (Spider-SS) improves compositional generalization (RATSQLG(S) best on all eval sets), with a dedicated limitation discussion; it does not connect to training dynamics, flatness, or schema-coherence theory.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a text-to-SQL compositional generalization measurement and method paper.
limitations_text: Spider-SS/Spider-CG based only on Spider (English text-to-SQL), no verification on other languages/datasets; about 5% of NatSQL cannot be converted to correct SQL; method may not be compatible with original models (RATSQLB(S) hyperparameters not workable; GNN performance degraded on SpiderD and CG-SUBD)
other_metrics_reported: Execution match (Table 2, NatSQL conversion eval); difficulty distribution (easy/medium/hard/extra hard) analysis; split-algorithm similarity (deviation <=1/2 tokens, >90%)
notes: Table 5, exact match on Spider dev set 72.7%

title: Accurate Classification of Pathological Whole-Slide Images for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Sun, K.; Huang, K.; Huang, J.; Zhou, M.; Yu, G.
task_custom_name: whole-slide image classification via multi-instance learning (CAMELYON16, TCGA-NSCLC, CRC)
arch_detail: Transformer-based multi-instance learning (MIL) for whole-slide images; proposed IntraWR (intra-WSI rearrange) and InterWR (inter-WSI rearrange) distribution alignment strategies embedded in the framework
train_data_note: CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC public datasets; private CRC dataset with 5-fold cross-validation plus external validation on slides from other medical centers
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured; distribution alignment operates on patch distributions, not internal representations

relevance_alignment_justification: Robust OOD classification for clinical diagnosis is safety-relevant in deployment, but the paper makes no explicit AI alignment or goal-misgeneralization connection.
open_questions_text: Future research could focus on extending the IntraWR/InterWR methodology to other medical image analysis tasks and optimizing its applicability across a wide range of pathological data.
other_metrics_reported: accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 (Table 4, Fig 7); 5-fold CV fold-level AUCs and box-plot quartiles on CRC
notes: AUC 0.959; accuracy 0.884, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.863 (Table 4)

title: I2CD: An Invertible Causal Framework for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning via Disentangle-Compose-Disentangle
authors: Yuan, Z.; Wang, Z.; Pan, Y.; Luo, A.; Li, W.; Wu, X.; Xu, C.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
task_custom_name: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL): MIT-States, UT-Zappos, C-GQA
arch_detail: Frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 with adapters in transformer layers; invertible net: 12 ActNorm+Affine-Coupling+Shuffling blocks; 3-layer MLP projections (hidden 512)
train_data_note: CZSL datasets MIT-States, UT-Zappos, C-GQA; Adam batch 32; lr 1e-5 (MIT-States, C-GQA) / 2e-5 (UT-Zappos); CSP-style augmentation
augmentation_type: CSP-style data augmentation (Nayak, Yu, Bach 2023)
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported or derivable; statistical significance claimed without test statistics
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy metric reported (e.g., probing, CKA, disentanglement score); correlation coefficient 0.975 is a design choice of the invertible net, not a measured coherence value
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) via compositional zero-shot learning on unseen attribute-object compositions, using causal disentangle-compose-disentangle and intervention to shrink the seen-unseen gap; but framed as a CV disentanglement method without a general theory of OOD failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; CZSL is a visual compositional generalization task with no alignment discussion.
limitations_text: Contextuality (context-dependent visual manifestation of states) acknowledged as an open challenge not addressed; contextual relationships between objects and states noted as beyond the current scope
open_questions_text: Investigate contextual relationships between objects and states in future work
other_metrics_reported: Best seen accuracy (S), best unseen accuracy (U), harmonic mean (HM) of seen/unseen accuracies, AUC of seen-unseen curve; closed-world and open-world settings
notes: Table 3 Full: S=50.6, U=54.1, HM=40.0, AUC=23.3; gap = S-U

title: Grounded Graph Decoding Improves Compositional Generalization in Question Answering
authors: Yu Gai; Paras Jain; Wendi Zhang; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Dawn Song; Ion Stoica
arch_detail: Sequence encoder with attention + grounded graph decoder (Grounded Graph Decoding, 0.3M params); grounding attention over input retains syntax; ablations: graph decoding only and syntax-aware graph decoding; baselines LSTM+attn, Transformer, Universal Transformer, Evolved Transformer, T5, T5-11B
train_data_note: CFQ benchmark; MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits maximize compositional divergence between train and test; main results obtained without tuning on development sets to avoid test leakage
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (a core sigma-trap phenomenon) on CFQ MCD adversarial splits via grounded graph decoding, achieving 98.6% on MCD1, and includes an analysis of why only one syntactic composition type (conjunctive queries) limits MCD2/MCD3 performance; no connection to training dynamics or flatness.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a compositional generalization method for semantic parsing question answering.
limitations_text: Grounded Graph Decoding incorporates only one type of syntactic composition (conjunctive 'A and B' queries) and cannot completely solve MCD2/MCD3; domain-specific intermediate representations (LIR/RIR) that ease the task are complex to apply to real-world datasets like CFQ; error analysis shows conjunctive structures mainly help MCD1.
open_questions_text: Complement Grounded Graph Decoding with pre-training-based approaches; incorporate more complex syntactic structures beyond conjunctive queries to further boost accuracy.
notes: Table 1; 98.6% accuracy, MCD1 without dev-set tuning

arch_detail: Sequence encoder with attention + grounded graph decoder (Grounded Graph Decoding, 0.3M params); grounding attention over input retains syntax; ablations: graph decoding only and syntax-aware graph decoding; baselines LSTM+attn, Transformer, Universal Transformer, Evolved Transformer, T5, T5-11B
train_data_note: CFQ benchmark; MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits maximize compositional divergence between train and test; main results obtained without tuning on development sets to avoid test leakage
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (a core sigma-trap phenomenon) on CFQ MCD adversarial splits via grounded graph decoding, achieving 98.6% on MCD1, and includes an analysis of why only one syntactic composition type (conjunctive queries) limits MCD2/MCD3 performance; no connection to training dynamics or flatness.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a compositional generalization method for semantic parsing question answering.
limitations_text: Grounded Graph Decoding incorporates only one type of syntactic composition (conjunctive 'A and B' queries) and cannot completely solve MCD2/MCD3; domain-specific intermediate representations (LIR/RIR) that ease the task are complex to apply to real-world datasets like CFQ; error analysis shows conjunctive structures mainly help MCD1.
open_questions_text: Complement Grounded Graph Decoding with pre-training-based approaches; incorporate more complex syntactic structures beyond conjunctive queries to further boost accuracy.
notes: Table 3 ablation; syntax-aware encoder, no grounding, 32.7%

title: Towards Understanding the Relationship between In-context Learning and Compositional Generalization

train_data_note: Meta-ICL: train on all few-shot problems derivable from the dataset (shuffled instance order and shuffled labels); datasets SCAN (MCD splits), COGS, GeoQuery (TMCD)

title: Compositional Generalization in Semantic Parsing: Pre-training vs. Specialized Architectures
authors: Daniel Furrer; Marc van Zee; Nathan Scales; Nathanael Schärli
arch_detail: MLM pre-trained T5 variants (small-NP, small, base, large, 3B, 11B, 11B-mod with intermediate SPARQL representation) vs specialized archs: LSTM+A, Transformer, Universal Transformer, Evolved Transformer, CGPS, NSEN; hyperparameter tables for CGPS, Evolved Transformer, NSEN
train_data_note: CFQ and SCAN with DBCA MCD splits; pre-training = masked language modeling (T5); T5-11B-mod uses intermediate SPARQL representation (group subjects/objects, sort alphabetically)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; significance claims (pre-training vs non-pretrained) stated without test statistics in the excerpt
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; analyses operate on data splits (DBCA) and input/output lengths
relevance_sigma_justification: Systematic quantitative study of compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap): 13 architectures from RNN to transformer and neurosymbolic families evaluated on SCAN and CFQ MCD splits with accuracy-vs-compound-divergence curves, showing pre-training outperforms SCAN-inspired specialized architectures and all models fail (0 accuracy) beyond training length.
relevance_alignment_justification: No alignment or safety discussion; indirect relevance through robust compositional generalization of large pre-trained language systems, framed as language understanding capability rather than safety.
limitations_text: Pre-training decreases SCAN length-split accuracy by 8.5% on average; no gains and 0 accuracy on inputs beyond max training length with or without pre-training; specialized architectures gains from SCAN do not transfer to CFQ
notes: MCD mean 14.9 +-1.2 (95% CI); Keysers et al. baseline

title: Representational Homomorphism Predicts and Improves Compositional Generalization In Transformer Language Model
authors: Zhiyu An; Wan Du
task_custom_name: Adapted SCAN (noise injection, primitive coverage manipulations)
arch_detail: Small decoder-only Transformers trained from scratch; depth ablated 1-10 layers; layer-wise MSE-based Homomorphism Error metric using linear, bilinear, and MLP operators; no pretraining (to avoid data spoilage)
train_data_note: Adapted SCAN with controlled training set primitives (1 vs 2+ primitives) and randomly inserted noise tokens (0-15)
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; effects summarized via paired t-tests (p=1.1e-4, p=0.001, p=0.023) and R2=0.73 regression
schema_coherence_notes: Homomorphism Error (HE) measures deviation from compositional homomorphism between linguistic expression algebra and hidden-state space (layer-wise MSE); baseline modifier HE ~0.002 MSE at 0 noise tokens rising to ~0.012 at 15 noise; HE-regularized training significantly reduces HE (paired t-test p=1.1e-4)
repr_analysis_finding: HE predicts OOD compositional generalization under noise injection (R2=0.73); model depth has minimal effect on HE or OOD accuracy; noise tokens increase modifier HE while sequence HE stays stable; HE-regularization reduces HE and improves OOD accuracy
relevance_sigma_justification: Core sigma-trap study: introduces Homomorphism Error, a representation-level metric of compositional structure failure, shows it predicts OOD compositional generalization (R2=0.73), and demonstrates that regularizing HE during training significantly improves OOD accuracy (p=0.023) on an adapted SCAN benchmark.
relevance_alignment_justification: Not an alignment paper, but diagnosing and controlling internal compositional structure of models (via a regularizable representational metric) is a step toward interpretability and steering relevant to understanding goal misgeneralization; no explicit safety discussion.
limitations_text: Experiments on synthetic data with precisely controlled compositional structure; real-world language adds semantic ambiguity, context dependence, and irregular constructions. Evaluation on relatively small Transformer models; behavior of homomorphism error in large-scale pretrained LMs remains open.
open_questions_text: Apply homomorphism error analysis to established compositional benchmarks using natural language; investigate how homomorphism error scales with model size and pretraining data; explore compositionally-aware architecture search and training procedures.
other_metrics_reported: Homomorphism Error (modifier and sequence HE, layer-wise MSE averaged over linear/bilinear/MLP operators); R2 of HE-OOD accuracy regression
notes: Mean OOD accuracy approximately 47% at 0 noise tokens; modifier HE ~0.002 MSE; 5 random seeds, mean and std reported

title: *-CFQ: Analyzing the Scalability of Machine Learning on a Compositional Task
authors: Dmitry Tsarkov; Tibor Tihon; Nathan Scales; Nikola Momchev; Danila Sinopalnikov; Nathanael Schärli
arch_detail: Seq2seq Transformer (Vaswani et al. 2017) trained 500k steps at fixed model size and fixed training steps (fixed compute)
train_data_note: *-CFQ suite derived from CFQ with 10x example pool (U-CFQ); train sizes 10,314 to 1,031,270; compound divergence splits (0.0-0.6); fixed compute (500k steps)
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; error rates with 95% CI over 5 replicas of 36 splits
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; analysis operates on data splits and error rates
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly examines compositional generalization failure on CFQ compound-divergence splits across training sizes at fixed compute, showing OOD error persists at all scales and rises with language scope - a core sigma-trap phenomenon - though focused on scaling limits rather than the failure mechanism itself.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a scaling analysis of semantic parsing with no safety discussion.
limitations_text: N-CFQ/half-N-CFQ augmentation results hard to interpret due to large domain overlap with B-CFQ; lower starting accuracies are an artifact of the larger example pool in the compound divergence splitting algorithm
open_questions_text: Whether ML can robustly solve NLU at the scale of arbitrary natural language across domains remains open; deeper investigation of N-CFQ blending side effects suggested
other_metrics_reported: Mean error rate with 95% CI over 5 replicas of 36 splits; scalability curves (error vs train size, log-log); plateau error rates for half-L-CFQ (~0.03), L-CFQ (~0.02), half-X-CFQ (~0.04), X-CFQ (~0.03)
notes: Err 0.979 (95% CI 0.976-0.982), 5 replicas x 36 splits

title: Hierarchical Poset Decoding for Compositional Generalization in Language
authors: Yinuo Guo; Zeqi Lin; Jian-Guang Lou; Dongmei Zhang
arch_detail: Hierarchical Poset Decoding (HPD): encoder-decoder with poset-based sketch prediction, phrase-table primitive prediction, and traversal path prediction; baselines: LSTM+Attention, Transformer, Universal Transformer (Keysers et al. 2020), Seq2Tree, CGPS; ablations replace sketch predictor or remove hierarchical mechanism
train_data_note: CFQ over Freebase, MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits; accuracy = % of examples correctly parsed to gold SPARQL meaning representations; SPARQL simplified via merging similar triples in one baseline block
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; mean MCD accuracy 69.0% stated directly for HPD, 56.7% for Seq2Tree-based sketch ablation
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; poset structure is an output-decoding constraint, not a measured representation property
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly attacks compositional generalization failure on CFQ MCD splits; hierarchical poset decoding enforces partial permutation invariance, improving mean MCD accuracy to 69.0% vs sub-20% seq2seq baselines, with ablations isolating the permutation-invariance and hierarchical mechanisms.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architectural decoding method for compositional generalization in semantic parsing.
limitations_text: Break-down analysis: sketch prediction fails on 8.7%/24.9%/25.2% of MCD1/2/3 test cases because the sequence encoder does not capture implicit syntactic structure; primitive prediction has low precision (34.4-35.0%) from a simple phrase table; traversal path prediction fails on 11.7%/15.5%/7.0% of cases due to many candidate paths.
open_questions_text: Future work: enhance the encoder with compositionality and build attention between encoder and hierarchical poset decoder; improve primitive prediction recall via contextual information; reduce the number of candidate primitives for traversal path prediction.
other_metrics_reported: Component-level metrics per split: Sketch Prediction accuracy (91.3/75.1/74.8); Primitive Prediction precision (34.4/35.0/34.1) and recall (99.9); Traversal Path Prediction precision/recall/F1 (e.g., 96.7/98.9/97.7 on MCD1)
notes: Hierarchical Poset Decoding with Seq2Seq-based sketch prediction; 79.6% on MCD1

title: Iterative Decoding for Compositional Generalization in Transformers
authors: Luana Ruiz; Joshua Ainslie; Santiago Ontañón
task_custom_name: Cartesian product dataset (Ontanón et al. 2021)
arch_detail: Transformer seq2seq with relative attention (radius r=8) and copy decoding variants; iterative decoding decomposes mapping into intermediate steps fed back as inputs until end-of-iteration token, with short/long intermediate input and row/token decoding scenarios
train_data_note: PCFG (Hupkes et al. 2020) random/productivity/systematicity splits; Cartesian product easy (ID) + hard productivity splits; CFQ MCD1
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (a core sigma-trap phenomenon) in transformers on PCFG productivity/systematicity, Cartesian product, and CFQ MCD1 splits, showing seq2seq transformers fail to learn unrolled iterations while iterative decoding largely closes the gap; no connection to training dynamics or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a decoding-method study for compositional generalization in sequence learning.
limitations_text: Iterative decoding underperforms seq2seq on CFQ MCD1 (32.5% vs 37.1%); it only generalizes to longer iterations that were unrolled during training (row-decoding fails when extra token pairs are added); PCFG iterative decoding test accuracy still below training accuracy.
notes: Table 2; seq2seq, ID test (up to 5 numbers/letters) 97.8%

title: Structural generalization in COGS: Supertagging is (almost) all you need
authors: Alban Petit; Caio Corro; François Yvon
arch_detail: Neural graph-based semantic parser extended with supertagging step (ILP valency constraints, companionship principle), argument identification as maximum matching, factor-graph weakly-supervised loss, incremental early stopping
train_data_note: COGS dataset; training on in-distribution data with incremental early stopping (freezes part of the network) to prevent overfitting
effect_size_notes: Paper reports a 23.9 point increase from 51.1 to 75.0 accuracy on Obj-to-subj PP attributable to the incremental early-stopping training procedure
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; supertagging accuracy is a pipeline-internal metric, not a representation analysis
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional (structural) generalization failure on COGS by adding supertagging with ILP valency constraints, matching-based argument identification, and incremental early stopping, reaching high accuracy on structural generalization cases where baselines score near zero - a targeted fix for the sigma-trap.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic parsing method paper with no safety discussion.
limitations_text: Cannot predict supertags unseen during training (meta-grammars could overcome this); ILP solver may be slow in more realistic settings; pipeline's local predictions cannot use argument identification scores to fix earlier errors
other_metrics_reported: Overall accuracy (mostly lexical generalization, 85.7% of test set); per-case structural generalization accuracies (Obj to subj PP, PP recursion, CP recursion); word-level supertagging accuracy with/without ILP
notes: Sentence-level exact match on structural generalization case; 1,000 test sentences; mean over 3 runs

title: When Can Transformers Ground and Compose: Insights from Compositional Generalization Benchmarks
authors: Ankur Sikarwar; Arkil Patel; Navin Goyal
task_custom_name: ReaSCAN (grounded navigation); gSCAN (GSRR splits); RefEx (novel grounded referring-expression task)
arch_detail: GroCoT: attention-only transformer, command + world-state embeddings concatenated, stacked multi-head attention blocks with residual connections, 36-way softmax over grid cells; a single self-attention layer with a single head generalizes on RefEx; learned positional embeddings only for three-attr-rel variant; LLM baselines: GPT-3, Codex (few-shot in-context)
train_data_note: RefEx: 90K train / 2.5K val / 2.5K test per variant; C2-deeper: 100K sampled train + 6,000 C2 test examples, 4,500 depth-3 test examples; ReaSCAN and gSCAN used for main experiments
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-coherence proxy measured (no CKA/RSA/compositionality score)
repr_analysis_finding: Linear probe of target location in encoder representations: near-perfect localization accuracy on A1/A2/B1/B2 (up to ~100) but near 0 on A3 and C1 and 23.4 on C2, identifying target identification as the main OOD challenge; layer 0 (input embeddings) and random-embedding baselines also probed
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly probes grounded compositional generalization (the sigma-trap): shows a simple attention-only transformer generalizes on ReaSCAN, gSCAN and RefEx novel attribute compositions, isolates target identification as the core OOD challenge, and shows the ReaSCAN C2 depth-generalization split is unfair, with transformers generalizing on an amended deeper split.
relevance_alignment_justification: No alignment or safety discussion; indirect relevance via mechanistic insight into when transformers compose (single attention head suffices) and LLM failure on grounded compositionality.
notes: Action seq accuracy 99.40 (default) / 99.26 (and->that is) / consistency 99.61; ground-truth target location provided

title: Revisiting the Compositional Generalization Abilities of Neural Sequence Models
authors: Arkil Patel; Satwik Bhattamishra; Phil Blunsom; Navin Goyal
arch_detail: Standard seq2seq models: LSTM and Transformer; LSTM capacity swept 6.7K-354K params; SCAN/Colors embedding analyses on LSTM (t-SNE, distance metrics)
train_data_note: SCAN: 13,185 base train + 9 extra isolated-primitive definitions = 13,194; Colors train sets with 0/10/20/100 extra primitives; COGS: train size fixed at 2,500, varying % of 129 example primitives
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported
schema_coherence_notes: No coherence/compositionality proxy of internal representations; only embedding geometry of isolated vs example primitives
repr_analysis_finding: t-SNE plots and Euclidean/Manhattan/Cosine distances show the isolated primitive embedding moves closer to example-primitive embeddings as more example primitives are added to the train set (LSTM on Colors)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets the sigma-trap: compositional generalization failure on SCAN/COGS one-shot primitive generalization, and shows the failure is largely a training-distribution artifact, with detailed empirical analysis (capacity, distributions, seeds, embedding geometry) explaining when standard seq2seq models do and do not fail.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an empirical analysis of compositional generalization in sequence models.
notes: Uniform train distribution, 100 primitives x 1000 examples per primitive: 93.7%; accuracies collapse to near 0 with 10 primitives (0.0-4.2%)

title: Compositional Generalization for Primitive Substitutions
authors: Yuanpeng Li; Liang Zhao; Jianyu Wang; Joel Hestness
task_custom_name: SCAN Primitive substitution (Jump, TurnLeft, SCAN-ADJ); few-shot learning (Lake et al. 2019); EN-FR compositional MT
arch_detail: Seq2seq with two representations (one generates attention maps, the other maps attended input words to output symbols) plus primitive and function entropy regularization; baselines: LSTM+Attn, GRU+Attn, pointer networks (Ptr-Bahdanau, Ptr-Loung); code at github.com/yli1/CGPS
train_data_note: SCAN Primitive substitution tasks (Jump, TurnLeft, SCAN-ADJ), SCAN Simple/Length, few-shot learning task from Lake et al. 2019, and English-French compositional MT task (Lake and Baroni 2018); in Jump, 'jump' appears only as a single command in training
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; improvements reported as baseline vs proposed accuracies (e.g., 14.0% to 98.8% on Jump)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; entropy reduction is a training objective, not a measured coherence metric
repr_analysis_finding: Attention map visualization shows each output position attends on the correct primitive input word (including replicated words), consistent with expected compositional parsing; primitive and function entropy regularization both contribute (ablation A-E on Jump/TurnLeft)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure on SCAN primitive-substitution splits, improving Jump accuracy from 14.0% to 98.8% via dual-representation attention with entropy regularization, with ablations isolating which components drive the compositional gain.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is a method paper for compositional generalization in NLP sequence tasks.
other_metrics_reported: Few-shot learning accuracy vs human performance (Lake et al. 2019); machine translation sentence accuracy; ablation study across 5 variants; attention map visualization
notes: Proposed method, mean +/- std; baseline L&B 14.0%
