title: A Neuroscience-Inspired Dual-Process Model of Compositional Generalization
authors: Alex Noviello; Claas Beger; Jacob Groner; Kevin Ellis; Weinan Sun
arch_detail: MIRAGE dual-process model: System 1 = meta-trained Transformer Neural Decomposer (single-step compositional decomposition); System 2 = Schema Engine (rule-based, prioritized schemas, episodic bindings); iterative refinement loop; baselines: vanilla Transformer and Transformer+SC_Library prompt
train_data_note: System 1 meta-trained to perform single-step decomposition on a stream of random grammars; evaluated task-agnostically (zero-shot) on all SCAN splits
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; the schema library is symbolic and interpretability is discussed qualitatively via stepwise traces
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly confronts the sigma-trap: systematic compositional generalization failure in deep learning. MIRAGE achieves >99% accuracy on all SCAN splits (including Length, Add prim, Template designed to foil seq2seq models) via a dual-process neuro-inspired architecture, with ablations isolating schema priorities, iterative refinement, and accurate schemas as causes of systematic behavior; offers a processing and interpretability account of why compositional failure occurs and how it can be overcome.
relevance_alignment_justification: Not an alignment/safety paper, but its externalized, stepwise-verifiable schema traces and cognitive-architecture framing speak to interpretability and transparency concerns that are adjacent to AI safety; no direct treatment of goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: MIRAGE relies on reliable extraction of a consistent grammar; robustness to noisy or incomplete schemas is not yet addressed; evaluation is limited to SCAN.
open_questions_text: Extend the schema extractor with probabilistic rule learning and active retrieval for noisy schemas; apply the architecture to more complex reasoning tasks; use its inspectable states to test neuroscientific hypotheses about HPC-PFC interactions during planning.
notes: Table 1; Simple split treated as ID, 99.50 +/- 0.30 SEM, 4 runs

title: Can Transformers Jump Around Right in Natural Language? Assessing Performance Transfer from SCAN
authors: Rahma Chaabouni; Roberto Dessì; Eugene Kharitonov
arch_detail: Vanilla Transformer with focused modifications: SAG (relative-position attention graph), convolution self-attention, fixed span, T5-style local attention with learned relative-position bias; fairseq setup with encoder/decoder normalize-before; ConvS2S-inspired localization
train_data_note: SCAN splits (jump etc.); low-resource FLoRes MT (ne-en, si-en, en-ne, en-si); newly introduced distribution-shifted compositional English-French translation task; noun-adjective order agreement dataset
effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; relative gains reported (13.1% BLEU low-resource, 14% COMP, 1.44% noun-adjective)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Softmaxed learned relative-position biases (bij) show many heads strongly prefer fixed local positions; several heads dominantly attend to particular positions; local attention linked to SCAN compositional generalization; some heads retain ability to look beyond span, explaining T5's edge over fixed-span
repr_analysis_layer: all encoder/decoder layers, e.g. encoder layer 0 head 7, layer 2 heads 3,7; decoder layer 2 heads 3,4,5
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates compositional generalization on SCAN, shows Transformer variants with localized attention (SAG+T5) jump from near-zero to ~60% SCAN-jump accuracy, and tests whether this capability transfers to low-resource and distribution-shifted MT — a direct empirical probe of when comp-gen competence matters.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a transfer/architecture analysis across SCAN and machine translation.
other_metrics_reported: BLEU on FLoRes dev-test (ne-en 8.40+/-0.02 vs Transformer 7.94+/-0.05 for SAG+T5; en-ne 5.01+/-0.10 vs 4.43+/-0.01) and on compositional En-Fr (41.43+/-0.29 vs 40.86+/-0.34); sig at p<1e-3 and p<0.05 respectively; noun-adjective SAG +1.44% relative
notes: Best SAG+T5 model on SCAN-jump ~60% (instance selected for attention-bias analysis); vanilla Transformer ~0%, focused modifications give large improvements

title: CNNs found to jump around more skillfully than RNNs: Compositional generalization in seq2seq convolutional networks
authors: Roberto Dessì; Marco Baroni
arch_detail: Out-of-the-box fairseq convolutional seq2seq: multi-layer CNN encoder-decoder with multi-layer attention; hyperparameter search over learning rate, layer dimensionality (128-512), layer count (6-10), kernel width (3-5), dropout (0-0.5)
train_data_note: SCAN splits: random (80/20), jump, around-right, length, turn-left; CNN tested on random, jump and around-right (length near 0%, turn-left near-perfect)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons are descriptive mean accuracies across seeds
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; error analyses are behavioral, not representational
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on SCAN's jump and around-right splits, showing a CNN far outperforms RNNs, and analyzes kernel width, multi-layer attention, and error structure to explain why the CNN still does not induce systematic compositional rules.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is an architecture comparison on a compositional generalization benchmark.
limitations_text: CNN's learned positional embeddings do not generalize beyond training lengths (length split near 0%); shallow CNNs cannot handle even the random split; self-attentive networks left untested as more cumbersome to train; CNN induces no rule-like systematicity; best LSTM has 1/4 the parameters of the best CNN.
open_questions_text: Future work: investigate which CNN aspects (kernel width, multi-layer attention) are crucial for compositional generalization; formulate a tighter CNN vs LSTM comparison under matched depth and parameter budgets.
other_metrics_reported: error proportions across command words; output-length error variance under kernel-width variation; attention-layer ablation accuracies
notes: Random split treated as ID; mean cross-seed accuracy 99.92% (13th of ~2.5K configurations)

title: SUBS: Subtree Substitution for Compositional Semantic Parsing
authors: Jingfeng Yang; Le Zhang; Diyi Yang
arch_detail: Seq2seq semantic parsers: LSTM and BART-large; method = subtree substitution data augmentation (exchanging subtrees whose roots share meaning functions, gold and induced tree variants); baselines: no augmentation, SCFG recombination (Jia and Liang 2016), GECA (Andreas 2019); code at github.com/GT-SALT/SUBS
train_data_note: GeoQuery: 519 training examples (50/100/200 in few-shot scaling study); SCAN: 12,180 original + 6,660 subtree-substitution augmented examples; 3,351 of the 4,476 SCAN test examples recovered by substitution (74.87%)
augmentation_type: subtree substitution data augmentation: exchange subtrees with similar semantic function roots across training examples (gold and induced parse-tree variants)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; improvements reported as absolute accuracy gains (21% LSTM, 3% BART on GeoQuery Query split) and as full accuracies (e.g., 0.88 BART+SUBS)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence metric; analysis focuses on augmented-data complexity rather than internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly attacks compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap signature) via compositional data augmentation on SCAN and GeoQuery, raising LSTM exact match from 0% to 100% on SCAN RIGHT and reaching new SOTA on GeoQuery compositional split; limited to data-side remedies.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is a data augmentation method for semantic parsing benchmarks.
other_metrics_reported: Augmented-data complexity statistics (avg/max exchanged segment, utterance, program lengths); training-data-size scaling (Table 4); convergence speed (updates to converge)
notes: BART-large with gold subtree substitution at full 519 training examples; exact match 0.88; new SOTA on GeoQuery compositional split

title: On graph-based reentrancy-free semantic parsing
authors: Alban Petit; Caio Corro
arch_detail: Graph-based span parser: CYK/ILP MAP inference with grammar constraints, constraint smoothing + conditional gradient solver; ~5 sentences/sec on GeoQuery; baselines: seq2seq, BERT2SEQ, BART, span-based SP

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic parsing methodology paper with complexity proofs and benchmark evaluations.
limitations_text: Parser speed is a downside (~5 sentences per second on GeoQuery); accuracy is still significantly worse on the split requiring generalization to longer programs.
open_questions_text: Extensions for ASTs containing reentrancies; cases where a single word anchors more than one predicate or entity; more general research on neural architectures that generalize better to longer sentences.

title: LAGr: Labeling Aligned Graphs for Improving Systematic Generalization in Semantic Parsing
authors: Dora Jambor; Dzmitry Bahdanau
arch_detail: LAGr graph-labeling parser: predicts node and edge labels for a multi-layer input-aligned graph using a shared Transformer encoder; PED (positional embedding downscaling) init; weakly-supervised variant with approximate MAP alignment via Hungarian matching (K candidates, noise sigma)
train_data_note: CFQ MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits + random split (used as in-distribution for tuning); COGS train/gen sets. Metric is graph accuracy (predicted vs true graph isomorphism), comparable to exact-match accuracy of prior work
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; LAGr changes output structure (graph labeling), not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on COGS and CFQ: LAGr graph-labeling raises CFQ MCD mean from ~18% seq2seq baselines to ~39% and beats all baselines on every MCD split, but does not study training dynamics, flatness, or representation-level schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic-parsing method paper concerned only with compositional accuracy.
limitations_text: Weakly-supervised LAGr does not always converge on the training set; runs not reaching 99.5% training graph accuracy (~12%) were discarded. Duplicate node labels in 3.7-5.7% of CFQ examples complicate alignment inference (fixes 2.7% hard article cases via cached alignment candidate). Lexicons not integrated.
open_questions_text: Future work: modify LAGr to condition edge predictions on node labels (based on error analysis); use a pretrained encoder; apply more advanced discrete optimization or amortized inference methods for alignment; lexicons can be integrated though not expected to help on COGS.
notes: ID = CFQ random split graph acc 99.5 (sd 0.2); OOD = mean MCD graph acc 38.2 (sd 2.7); per-split MCD1 65.2 (2.6), MCD2 26.4 (3.2), MCD3 23.0 (2.0); 8-11 runs

title: Compositional generalization through meta sequence-to-sequence learning
authors: Brenden M. Lake
arch_detail: Memory-augmented seq2seq (LSTM encoder-decoder + external memory + decoder attention; 'seq2seq recurrent' per excerpt); baselines: standard seq2seq RNN, syntactic-attention Transformer
train_data_note: SCAN; meta-training on episodes of 4 primitives sampled from 24 (plus direction variants in Exp 4.5); seq2seq training augmented with 20 extra primitive/action pairs; length split trains on ~17,000 instructions (<=22 actions)
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; raw accuracies with SD across 5 runs
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; external memory usage is analyzed only via lesion ablations of support loss and decoder attention
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies the sigma-trap: standard seq2seq models fail catastrophically on SCAN compositional splits (12.26% on the jump split), and meta seq2seq learning with memory augmentation restores near-perfect compositional accuracy, while length split still shows systematic generalization failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a purely cognitive-science-driven machine learning study of compositional learning.
limitations_text: Meta seq2seq learner lacks the truly systematic generalization needed to extrapolate to longer sequences (16.64% on the length split); standard seq2seq still fails on compositional splits.
notes: Exp 4.4, test on composed 'jump' instructions; 98.71% correct (SD=1.49), 5 runs

arch_detail: Memory-augmented seq2seq (LSTM encoder-decoder + external memory + decoder attention; 'seq2seq recurrent' per excerpt); baselines: standard seq2seq RNN, syntactic-attention Transformer
train_data_note: SCAN; meta-training on episodes of 4 primitives sampled from 24 (plus direction variants in Exp 4.5); seq2seq training augmented with 20 extra primitive/action pairs; length split trains on ~17,000 instructions (<=22 actions)
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; raw accuracies with SD across 5 runs
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; external memory usage is analyzed only via lesion ablations of support loss and decoder attention
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies the sigma-trap: standard seq2seq models fail catastrophically on SCAN compositional splits (12.26% on the jump split), and meta seq2seq learning with memory augmentation restores near-perfect compositional accuracy, while length split still shows systematic generalization failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a purely cognitive-science-driven machine learning study of compositional learning.
limitations_text: Meta seq2seq learner lacks the truly systematic generalization needed to extrapolate to longer sequences (16.64% on the length split); standard seq2seq still fails on compositional splits.
notes: Exp 4.5 baseline; 0.0% correct
experiment_label: SCAN around right split; standard seq2seq

title: Inducing Transformer's Compositional Generalization Ability via Auxiliary Sequence Prediction Tasks
authors: Yichen Jiang; Mohit Bansal
arch_detail: CGPS-Transformer: encoder-decoder Transformer with dual functional/syntactic + primitive/semantic embeddings and two auxiliary sequence prediction heads; decoder has 2 layers (L1/L2 vector ablations)
train_data_note: SCAN MCD splits (Keyers-style compound divergence). Few-shot variants: 418 (5%) and 836 (10%) of ground-truth auxiliary sequences; full command-action pairs = 8360 (~7947 extra beyond 418). No total train count stated for main runs
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported in excerpt; SCAN MCD has no ID split, so no gap computable
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; auxiliary sequences are data-side supervision, not a measured internal-coherence metric
repr_analysis_finding: Ablation of attention query vectors: using less-contextualized representations (decoder layer-1 intermediate/output vectors) as attention queries consistently beats final (L2) output vectors on MCD3; action-sequence accuracy tracks auxiliary-sequence prediction accuracy
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (sigma-trap): turns Transformer performance on SCAN from <=10% to 100% via auxiliary sequence supervision, shows compositionality is inducible with minimal data, and dissects which internal vectors preserve compositional structure; but does not analyze training dynamics, loss landscape, or alignment failure mechanisms.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; purely a language-model compositionality induction and architecture analysis paper.
limitations_text: Method developed on synthetic SCAN; unclear transfer to large-scale natural datasets; applying auxiliary sequences to natural language requires designing a heuristic to approximate the underlying grammar, which is infeasible in general.
open_questions_text: Whether/how a neural network can recognize compositionality in language as a first step in simpler settings; possibility of using small numbers of human-annotated auxiliary sequences to improve performance on large-scale natural datasets where automatic generation is infeasible.
notes: MCD1 test accuracy 97.8% with only 418 (5%) command-action pairs + auxiliary sequences

title: Laziness Is a Virtue When It Comes to Compositionality in Neural Semantic Parsing
authors: Maxwell Crouse; Pavan Kapanipathi; Subhajit Chaudhury; Tahira Naseem; Ramon Astudillo; Achille Fokoue; Tim Klinger
arch_detail: LSP (Lazy Semantic Parser): bottom-up, semi-autoregressive decoding built on pretrained T5-base, reusing the full language model; LSTM-encoder variant with random embeddings used for the GeoQuery experiment
train_data_note: CFQ (MCD1-3 splits), three Text-to-SQL datasets (ATIS, GeoQuery, Scholar) of Finegan-Dollak et al. 2018, and GeoQuery lambda-calculus; training set sizes not stated in excerpt
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure on the CFQ MCD splits and three Text-to-SQL benchmarks, attributing the failure to top-down autoregressive decoding and showing a bottom-up semi-autoregressive parser (LSP) significantly outperforms T5-base and LSTM, mitigating the sigma-trap at the decoding level without data augmentation.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a semantic-parsing architecture and decoding strategy paper.
limitations_text: Unordered n-ary relations (e.g., WHERE, and) can yield many valid logical forms per question, causing significant runtime issues; the method assumes the logical form is given as a graph, imposing an annotation burden absent in text-to-text systems such as fine-tuned LLMs.
notes: Exact-match accuracy on CFQ MCD1

title: Early-Warning Signals of Grokking via Loss-Landscape Geometry
authors: Yongzhong Xu
task_custom_name: Dyck-1 language depth prediction
arch_detail: Transformer encoder-decoder (SCAN); weight-decay grokking runs (lambda=1.0) vs no-weight-decay controls (lambda=0)
train_data_note: Grokking regime on small datasets: SCAN compositional splits and Dyck-1 depth prediction
effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; causal interventions accelerate grokking ~32% (SCAN) and ~50% (Dyck), reported as percentage changes in grokking time
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-coherence proxy; analysis is of weight-space geometry (loss-landscape curvature, PCA of weight trajectories), not data representations
repr_analysis_finding: PC1 de-concentration precedes grokking in Dyck but follows it in SCAN; spectral concentration (PC1 70-90%) specific to grokking runs vs diffuse 15-30% in no-weight-decay controls; attention projections show 70-85% PC1 concentration vs 40-60% for MLP weights
repr_analysis_layer: deepest layer; attention projections (WQ,WK,WV,WO) vs MLP weights
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly probes the dynamics of generalization on the SCAN compositional benchmark: grokking transitions (memorization to generalization) can be anticipated via loss-landscape curvature, so it speaks to when compositional generalization emerges, but it does not measure OOD gaps or generalization failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: Abrupt, hard-to-predict generalization transitions bear on deployment-time behavior and the commutator-defect early warning is a candidate monitoring signal, but the paper makes no explicit alignment or safety claims.
other_metrics_reported: Grok step, defect onset step, lead time and lead fraction, power-law exponents with R2, PC1 variance ratios, z-scores vs random-walk null, exec/random integrability ratios, intervention acceleration (32%/50%)
notes: 13 runs: 12 grok, 11 with detectable defect onset; lead-time power law alpha=1.18 (R2=0.990, n=11); advance warning windows 90-97% at slow learning rates; intervention accelerating non-commutativity speeds grokking ~32%

title: Sequence-Level Mixed Sample Data Augmentation

title: Does Data Scaling Lead to Visual Compositional Generalization?
authors: Arnas Uselis; Andrea Dittadi; Seong Joon Oh
task_custom_name: Controlled concept-combination benchmarks: PUG Shapes3D, dSprites, FunnySprites (introduced), Colored-MNIST, MPI3D
arch_detail: ResNet-50 trained from scratch as primary baseline; comparisons with ViT (patch 8/16, depth 4-8, width 384-512, heads 8/12, MLP 384-512); pretrained DINOv2 ViT-L, DINOv1 ResNet-50, DINO ViT-L, CLIP ViT-L; linear and 2-layer MLP [512,512] probes
train_data_note: Controlled concept-combination datasets with two concept dimensions (e.g., shape x color); training samples typically 60k (Table 2: 60x10^3), one ViT run at 120k; combination coverage varied 25-100%
schema_coherence_notes: Core thesis: linearly factored representations (concepts as additive components) enable compositional generalization; linear probe accuracy on FSprites at 93% observed combinations: intervention DINO ViT-Large 0.86 (linear) vs baseline ResNet-50 ImageNet 0.79 (linear); non-linear probes higher for DINO models
repr_analysis_finding: Linear probes show partial linearly-factored structure; non-linear (2-layer MLP) probes exceed linear for DINO ResNet-50/ViT-Large, indicating some compositional info not linearly accessible; ResNet-50 and CLIP ViT-L are more linearly separable for the evaluated concepts
relevance_sigma_justification: Central to the sigma-trap thesis: shows vision models fail compositional generalization under sparse concept combinations and memorize frequent pairs, demonstrates OOD generalization is driven by combination diversity rather than data scale, and identifies linearly factored representations as the structure enabling efficient compositional learning - directly linking schema coherence to compositional OOD performance.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; concerns vision-model compositional accuracy and dataset design only.
open_questions_text: Motivates stronger emphasis on constructing diverse datasets for compositional generalization and on representational structure that enables efficient compositional learning; notes partial presence of factored structure in pretrained models (DINO, CLIP) warranting further study.
other_metrics_reported: linear and non-linear (2-layer MLP [512,512]) probe accuracies on FSprites
notes: Colored-MNIST, 80% combinations (k/n 8/10), 60k training samples; OOD acc 95.1%

title: Towards Robust Out-of-Distribution Generalization Bounds via Sharpness
authors: Yingtian Zou; Kenji Kawaguchi; Yingnan Liu; Jiashuo Liu; Mong-Li Lee; Wynne Hsu
arch_detail: Theory built on two-layer ReLU random-feature models f(w,A,x)=(1/sqrt(m)) sum w_i sigma(x,a_i) with m hidden units and random features on the unit sphere; experiments on deep-learning ERM classifiers for WILDS-Camelyon17 and PACS; sharpness computed via Hessian of last FC layer; experiment backbone architectures not named in excerpt
train_data_note: WILDS-Camelyon17: 455,954 tumor/normal tissue slide images from 5 hospitals, one hospital assigned as test environment. PACS: 9,991 images of 7 objects in 4 styles (art painting, cartoon, photo, sketch), each environment used as test in turn (Gulrajani & Lopez-Paz setup)
effect_size_notes: No numeric accuracy or effect sizes in excerpt; sharpness-OOD accuracy relationship reported only via scatter figures (Figures 3, 5, 6)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; the paper analyzes loss-landscape sharpness (Hessian of last FC layer) vs OOD accuracy, not internal representation coherence

authors: Parikshit Bansal; Yashoteja Prabhu; Emre Kiciman; Amit Sharma
task_custom_name: text-matching item-to-item recommendation: Amazon products; AskUbuntu/SuperUser/Quora question recommendation

train_data_note: Amazon product-pair data and three forum question-recommendation datasets (AskUbuntu, SuperUser, Quora); sizes not stated in excerpt

relevance_alignment_justification: OOD robustness of deployed recommenders bears on reliability under distribution shift, but the paper has no safety or goal-misgeneralization framing; relevance to alignment is indirect.
limitations_text: Setting limited to short text-matching recommenders; results may not transfer to systems using longer descriptions or metadata; all experiments use offline data; OOD benefit depends on base model quality; under extreme shifts (Quora) the base model or OutReg is more suitable than ITVReg.

notes: AUC(0.05); in-distribution forum evaluation
experiment_label: AskUbuntu train, AskUbuntu eval (IID); NLI-DistilBERT, ITVReg

authors: Michael Zhang; Nimit S. Sohoni; Hongyang R. Zhang; Chelsea Finn; Christopher Ré

title: Fishr: Invariant Gradient Variances for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Alexandre Rame; Corentin Dancette; Matthieu Cord
task_custom_name: Also: linear toy dataset (Shi et al., 2021); main paper evaluates DomainBed (not in excerpt)
arch_detail: 3-layer MLP with ReLU, hidden dim 390, Adam (IRM hyperparameters); linear logistic regression for the toy dataset
train_data_note: Colored MNIST (IRM setup): binary digit classification, 2 train domains with green-label correlation 90% and 80%, reversed correlation (10%) at test; 501 epochs, batch size 25,000
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; mean +/- SD point estimates per method
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; analyses concern loss-landscape Hessians, not internal representation structure
repr_analysis_finding: Fishr aligns domain-level Hessians and gradient variances at convergence on Colored MNIST; with ERM the Frobenius distance between domain-level Hessians grows during training; Hessian norm (flatness) does not correlate with generalization
relevance_sigma_justification: Addresses OOD generalization failure by enforcing domain invariance of gradient variances (Fishr), with consistent gains over ERM on Colored MNIST and the DomainBed suite; not compositional generalization and no schema-coherence mechanism, so only indirectly relevant to the sigma-trap.
relevance_alignment_justification: Invariant learning for OOD robustness is upstream of safe deployment, but the paper makes no connection to AI alignment, goal misgeneralization, or safety.
limitations_text: Proper approximation bounds for using gradient covariance as a Hessian proxy are out of scope; full gradient covariance is computationally prohibitive (memory), so Fishr targets only the diagonal; methods compared under IRM-optimized hyperparameters
open_questions_text: Future work should investigate the diagonal variance approximation further or provide cheaper alternatives (e.g., K-FAC approximations) to reduce computational cost
other_metrics_reported: Train/test accuracy on the linear toy dataset (Shi et al., 2021) with learned weight vectors; Hessian distance, cosine similarity, and gradient-variance distance trajectories during training
notes: Table 6, Fishr (omega): no label flipping; ID = train domain acc, OOD = test with reversed color-label correlation

title: What Matters to You? Towards Visual Representation Alignment for Robot Learning
authors: Ran Tian; Chenfeng Xu; Masayoshi Tomizuka; Jitendra Malik; Andrea Bajcsy
task_custom_name: XMAGICAL (avoid/grouping) and Franka/Kuka robotic manipulation with preference-based rewards
arch_detail: RAPL: visual reward learned via optimal-transport feature matching on pre-trained visual representations (ImageNet, R3M, MVP, fine-tuned MVP backbones); RL policy trained with learned reward; baselines RLHF, TCC
train_data_note: Human preference feedback on videos; in-domain = videos from robot's own embodiment, cross-embodiment = videos from a different embodiment (e.g., short-stick X-Magical agent, Franka videos for Kuka deployment)
train_regime_other: preference-based reward learning from human feedback with optimal transport feature matching; RL policy optimization
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; success rates reported approximately and Spearman correlations between GT and learned rewards (Table 1)
schema_coherence_notes: Representation 'alignment' is measured via reward-space Spearman correlation, not a representation-level coherence proxy (no probing/CKA/RSA)
repr_analysis_finding: Average Spearman's rank correlation between ground-truth and learned visual reward trajectories across 100 video trajectories (Table 1); RAPL highest in all three tasks
relevance_sigma_justification: Addresses zero-shot OOD generalization (cross-embodiment transfer of learned visual rewards, +33% success under transfer) and robustness to spurious correlations (color distractor) in learned rewards, but does not address compositional generalization or model training dynamics.
relevance_alignment_justification: Core contribution is aligning robot reward/behavior with end-user preferences via human feedback, explicitly framed as eliminating behaviors 'misaligned with user preferences' caused by proxy-task fine-tuning and spurious correlations; a direct preference-based alignment study, though scoped to robot manipulation rather than AGI safety.
limitations_text: Only controlled simulation experiments; no real human feedback or robotic hardware validation.
open_questions_text: Strategic active-learning preference queries, robustness to noisy feedback, multi-modal (language) feedback, online visual reward fine-tuning from human feedback, crowd-sourced multi-human preferences.
other_metrics_reported: Policy success rates; average Spearman's rank correlation between GT and learned reward trajectories (100 video trajectories); sample efficiency of reward learning
notes: In-domain policy success rate approx 60%; RAPL comparable to ground-truth reward, outperforming RLHF and TCC

title: Diagnosing Generalization Failures from Representational Geometry Markers
authors: Chi-Ning Chou; Artem Kirsanov; Yao-Yuan Yang; SueYeon Chung
task_custom_name: OOD transfer learning to 9 datasets: Flowers102, Stanford Cars, Places365, Food101, Oxford-IIIT Pet, etc. (linear probe test accuracy)
arch_detail: 20 popular ImageNet-pretrained architectures from PyTorch official repository, each with two weight sets (v1/v2); exploratory experiments across diverse architectures, optimizers, and datasets
train_data_note: ImageNet-pretrained models (weights from PyTorch hub); v2 weights achieve higher ImageNet ID accuracy than v1; OOD transfer evaluated with linear probes on 9 downstream datasets
effect_size_notes: Derived: marker-based OOD-transfer prediction accuracy 73.02% minus ID-accuracy-based prediction 37.22% = +0.358 raw delta in prediction accuracy (92/126 correct predictions vs ID-accuracy baseline)
schema_coherence_notes: Prognostic markers are ID object-manifold geometry: effective manifold dimensionality (Deff) and utility (Psi_eff); reduced values (overcompression) predict weaker OOD generalization and overspecialization. No numeric marker values reported in excerpt; effective_rank used as closest vocabulary proxy for Deff
repr_analysis_finding: Object-manifold geometry analysis: low effective manifold dimensionality (Deff) and utility (Psi_eff) of ID representations forecast poor OOD generalization; with comparable ID validation accuracy, larger Deff/Psi_eff reflect richer task-relevant variability while excessive compression signals ID overspecialization; geometry predicted v1>v2 OOD transfer in 14/20 architectures despite v2's higher ID accuracy
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses anticipating OOD generalization failure: shows overcompression of ID object manifolds (low Deff/Psi_eff) predicts weaker OOD performance across diverse architectures, optimizers, and datasets, and beats ID accuracy as a transfer model-selection signal; a diagnostic biomarker framework for the sigma-trap, though not about compositional structure or training dynamics.
relevance_alignment_justification: Implicitly supports safe deployment by predicting OOD failures and improving model selection, and frames diagnostics as a complement to mechanistic interpretability for anticipating vulnerabilities, but contains no direct discussion of alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization.
open_questions_text: Strengthening theoretical foundations linking manifold overcompression to feature overspecialization; causal mechanisms and interventions (geometry-aware regularization, early stopping, robustness-oriented model selection); extending the diagnostic framework beyond vision to language, RL, and multimodal models; linking diagnostics to parameter transfer (Net2Net); parallels with neuroscience.
other_metrics_reported: Prognostic-marker prediction accuracy 73.02% (92/126) vs 37.22% for ID test accuracy as OOD-performance predictor, across 15 models x 9 OOD datasets; Neural Collapse and Participation Ratio markers also predictive; early fine-tuning dynamics differ by initialization (v1 sometimes faster learning)
notes: NOT model accuracy: 73.02% (92/126) is the accuracy of Deff/Psi_eff markers at predicting which v1/v2 weights transfer better on 9 OOD datasets, vs 37.22% for ID-accuracy-based selection; raw_delta=0.358 derived by extractor. 20 architectures, prediction verdicts: 14 v1>v2, 1 v2>v1, rest no clear verdict

title: Making Foresight Actionable: Repurposing Representation Alignment in World Action Models
authors: Lu Qiu; Yizhuo Li; Yi Chen; Yuying Ge; Yixiao Ge; Xihui Liu
task_custom_name: real-world robot manipulation with world action models (IRON-R01-1.11 humanoid); CLOSURE-style semantic/instance/attribute generalization splits
arch_detail: World Action Model with dual DiT: Cosmos-Predict2.5 video DiT (world model) + action DiT head; AGRA aligns video hidden states with frozen DINOv2 foundation-encoder semantic features via an MLP alignment projector
train_data_note: Real-world robot manipulation demonstrations (IRON-R01-1.11 humanoid); dataset sizes not stated in excerpt
effect_size_notes: OOD reported only as relative improvements (27%/32%/32%) over baseline; absolute OOD success rates not given, so no effect size derivable
schema_coherence_notes: AGRA aligns features toward DINOv2 semantic structure but no quantitative coherence/compositionality proxy is measured
repr_analysis_finding: Action-head cross-attention analysis shows the decoder ignores hand-object interaction regions despite plausible visual foresight; causal interventions show decisions are driven by task-irrelevant background; PCA shows DINOv2 features form spatially coherent structures while Cosmos features remain entangled with local appearance
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly diagnoses the action-grounding gap: plausible visual futures do not guarantee correct actions because representations are not organized for action decoding and attention drifts to task-irrelevant regions; AGRA's representation alignment improves ID and OOD (semantic/instance/attribute) generalization, targeting the sigma-trap's representation-mismatch failure mode in embodied control.
relevance_alignment_justification: OOD robustness of robot manipulation policies is safety-relevant for embodied deployment, and the paper shows task-irrelevant perturbations can corrupt actions; however, alignment/safety or goal-misgeneralization are not framed explicitly.
other_metrics_reported: object localization accuracy; affordance understanding
notes: In-distribution success rate 80% with AGRA representation alignment

authors: Manh Cuong Dao; Phi Le Nguyen; Thao Nguyen Truong; Trong Nghia Hoang
task_custom_name: Offline black-box optimization (Design-Bench style: TF-BIND-10, D'Kitty, Ant, Superconductor, Chembl)
arch_detail: Model-agnostic regularizer (IGNITE) on surrogate models; search baselines GA, REINFORCE, CbAS, BO-qEI; surrogate architecture not specified in excerpt

Epsilon=0.1 and eta_lambda=1e-3 chosen as optimal.

title: Temporal Representation Alignment: Successor Features Enable Emergent Compositionality in Robot Instruction Following
authors: Vivek Myers; Bill Chunyuan Zheng; Anca Dragan; Kuan Fang; Sergey Levine
task_custom_name: Robotic manipulation instruction following: BridgeData tabletop tasks + OGBench goal-conditioned locomotion
arch_detail: Real-world: ResNet visual encoder with CLIP embeddings, behavior cloning with Gaussian policy; OGBench: MLP state and goal encoders (64,64,64), latent dim 64; TRA adds time-contrastive successor-feature alignment loss
train_data_note: BridgeData tabletop manipulation (13 tasks, 4 scenes, 5-10 trials per task) and OGBench; tasks are compositionally OOD: each subtask's goal image lies in the training distribution but combinations are unseen
ood_metric_other: success rate (%) in OGBench environments; real-world results reported only as >40% relative improvement across 13 tasks
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; per-environment success rates with SD
schema_coherence_notes: No measured representation-level coherence proxy; TRA shapes representations via a temporal alignment loss but no probing/CKA/compositionality score is reported
repr_analysis_finding: Temporal alignment (NCE) loss over successor-feature state/goal representations enables compositional stitching; Theorem 1 proves compositional generalization error bound E[RR(pi;D*)] <= E[RR(pi;D)] + (alpha-1)/2alpha + (alpha-2)/2alpha*1{alpha>2}, tighter than worst-case and decreasing in alpha
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure in robot instruction following: tasks are compositionally OOD (subtasks in-distribution, compound combinations unseen) and temporal alignment of successor-feature representations yields >40% improvement across 13 tasks plus a proven bound showing compositional generalization error decreases with alignment strength.
relevance_alignment_justification: Robust compositional generalization in instruction-following robots is safety-relevant deployment behavior, but the paper makes no connection to AI alignment, goal misgeneralization, or safety.
limitations_text: TRA cannot counteract failures inherited from behavior cloning with a Gaussian policy; failure cases arise from inability to learn depth reasoning (early grasping or late release) and difficulty reconciling multimodal behavior
other_metrics_reported: OGBench success rate (%) over 7 environments (10 seeds, final 3 eval epochs averaged); real-world >40% compositional improvement across 13 tasks in 4 evaluation scenes
notes: OGBench GCBC baseline; compositionally-OOD stitch task

title: VLA^2: Empowering Vision-Language-Action Models with an Agentic Framework for Unseen Concept Manipulation
authors: Han Zhao; Jiaxuan Zhang; Wenxuan Song; Pengxiang Ding; Donglin Wang
task_custom_name: LIBERO simulation manipulation (custom OOD benchmark with novel object concepts)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: custom LIBERO benchmark with three difficulty levels: color changes, semantic reinterpretations (e.g., wine bottle -> Moutai), synonym substitutions (e.g., plate -> saucer)
arch_detail: VLA2 agentic framework wrapping OpenVLA (vision-language-action backbone) with external modules: web image/text retrieval, MMGroundingDINO object detection, lexical normalization (replace), transparent mask/color-mask injection, subtask planning and process verifier; evaluated in LIBERO simulation; baselines: OpenVLA-OFT, pi0, pi0-FAST (fine-tuned), Agentic Robot (RP)
train_data_note: Custom benchmark built on LIBERO simulation; novel objects and object descriptions (textures, synonyms, brand reinterpretations) introduced; no training performed for VLA2 itself, baselines fine-tuned on original LIBERO dataset
train_regime_other: agentic framework (no training); OpenVLA backbone augmented with retrieval, detection, lexical substitution and mask injection at inference
effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; paper reports relative SR improvements (44.2% on Hard vs standalone OpenVLA; average 20.2% across custom environments) and ablation deltas
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; framework-level interventions (retrieval, masks, lexical substitution) evaluated only via task success rate
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets OOD/concept generalization failure of VLA models on unseen object concepts (textures, descriptions, synonyms) via an agentic retrieval-and-grounding framework, framing the drop as generalization failure; embodied rather than compositional/semantic, and no link to training dynamics, flatness, or sigma.
relevance_alignment_justification: Concerns embodied agents operating in simulation with explicit focus on out-of-distribution concept handling; relevant to safe manipulation and robust autonomy but no engagement with alignment, oversight, or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Framework confined to relatively rigid procedural structures; no real-world experiments at this stage; extension to open-world real-world grasping evaluations is essential.
open_questions_text: Enhance VLA2 to achieve greater system autonomy and enable invocation of more external tools to handle a wider range of tasks; extend to open-world real-world grasping evaluations.
notes: Class 2 average SR 80.1% on in-domain LIBERO evaluation (fairest ID comparison within OpenVLA family); no performance degradation on in-domain tasks

title: Navigating High Dimensional Concept Space with Metalearning
authors: Max Gupta
task_custom_name: Few-shot Boolean concept classification from PCFG-generated logical statements
arch_detail: Gradient-based meta-learner Meta-SGD (learned initialization and step sizes; first- and second-order variants; K adaptation steps) vs vanilla SGD baseline on few-shot Boolean concept classification
train_data_note: Task distribution from a PCFG concept generator (extension of Goodman et al. 2008); featural dimensionality F in {8,16,32} (binary literals), compositional depth D in {3,5,7}; few-shot acquisition
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; relative accuracy improvements of Meta-SGD over SGD reported (+15.5% simple, +34.1% medium, +11.1% complex concepts), not absolute accuracies
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; analysis concerns optimization loss landscapes, not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies compositional versus featural complexity in few-shot concept learning: meta-learners are robust to increased compositional recursion (D=3 to D=7) but collapse under featural dimensionality (F=32), with loss-landscape analysis (roughness, local minima counts) explaining when compositional structure generalizes and when it fails.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a study of meta-learning optimization for few-shot concept acquisition.
limitations_text: Loss-landscape analysis is a local approximation (trajectories sampled in a small, locally convex region); findings may not extend to higher dimensions or more complex models.
open_questions_text: Whether compositional depth preserves loss-surface navigability in higher-dimensional settings and with more complex models deserves further investigation.
other_metrics_reported: Samples required to reach 60% accuracy (data efficiency); relative accuracy improvement vs SGD (+15.5% simple, +34.1% medium, +11.1% complex); loss trajectory roughness (std of discrete 2nd derivatives); local minima counts; trajectory geodesic length (90-99% reduction vs SGD); K=10 vs K=1 adaptation gains (5-8% simple, 15-20% complex)
notes: 2-3 literals: smooth quasi-convex landscape (roughness 0.0002, 0.3+/-0.1 local minima); Meta-SGD +15.5% accuracy vs SGD; K=10 vs K=1 gives modest 5-8% gain
experiment_label: Simple Boolean concepts; Meta-SGD vs SGD

title: Evaluating Reward Model Generalization via Pairwise Maximum Discrepancy Competitions
authors: Shunyang Luo; Peibei Cao; Zhihui Zhu; Kehua Feng; Zhihua Wang; Keyan Ding
task_custom_name: reward model preference evaluation (RewardBench2; open-domain prompt pool)
arch_detail: 10 LLM-based reward models re-evaluated; fine-tuning experiment uses ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1; LLM oracle judges ClaudeSonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GLM-4-Plus
train_data_note: Fine-tuning on 4500 oracle-annotated PMDC-selected preference pairs; prompt pool = 1000 questions with 5 candidate responses each
train_regime_other: fine-tuning reward model on PMDC-selected preference pairs
effect_size_notes: Extractor-computed: overall RewardBench2 gain = 0.599 (fine-tuned) - 0.568 (baseline) from Table 2
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly evaluates OOD generalization of reward models under distribution shift via pairwise maximum discrepancy selection from an open-domain prompt pool and uncovers systematic generalization failures - relevant to OOD generalization failure in alignment-critical components, though it is an evaluation-methodology paper rather than a study of compositional generalization mechanisms.
relevance_alignment_justification: Reward models are the core alignment signal in RLHF; the paper directly studies whether RMs generalize to unseen prompts and shifting distributions, uncovers systematic generalization failures (length bias, context insensitivity), and shows PMDC-guided fine-tuning improves alignment fidelity on RewardBench2, making it directly relevant to alignment reliability.
limitations_text: O(N^2) pairwise comparisons limit scalability to very large RM collections; LLM-oracle inherent biases (e.g., stylistic preferences) may affect evaluation fidelity (mitigated by high inter-judge agreement); prompt pool coverage of highly specialized or rapidly evolving domains remains limited
open_questions_text: Enhance oracle reliability through multi-judge ensembles; extend PMDC to multi-dimensional evaluation frameworks; scale the framework to larger model sets and prompt pools
other_metrics_reported: LLM judge agreement: 95.0% (Claude vs Gemini), 96.0% (Claude vs GLM), 94.5% (Gemini vs GLM); vs human oracle: 94.5%/92.5%/93.0%; annotation cost 10000->450 comparisons (95.5% reduction); Spearman ranking stability vs top-k; per-dimension RewardBench2 gains: Math +4.5%, Safety +7.1%, IF -1.6%, Focus -5.4%
notes: RewardBench2 overall 0.568; per-dimension: Factuality 0.534, Focus 0.642, Math 0.516, Precise 0.366, IF 0.780, Safety 0.570

title: Improving Latent Generalization Using Test-time Compute
authors: Arslan Chaudhry; Sridhar Thiagarajan; Andrew Lampinen
task_custom_name: Latent generalization: syllogism, reversal (strict/non-strict), category-as-subject/target fact recall
arch_detail: Finetuned decoder-only language model (exact model not named in excerpt); trained via RL from correctness feedback to produce long chain-of-thought (thinking); ICL condition as reference
train_data_note: Knowledge finetuning tasks (syllogisms, reversal facts, category-subject/target facts); OOD = holdout knowledge not trained on (no RL performed on it)
train_regime_other: Reinforcement learning from correctness feedback for long chain-of-thought (thinking)
augmentation_type: Train-time data augmentation (e.g., strings in forward and reverse directions); Augmentation and Augmentation+RL baselines
effect_size_notes: Qualitative claims (thinking resolves many latent generalization failures; above-chance on reversal via generate-and-verify; below ICL) without extractable effect sizes.
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; only behavioral accuracy metrics.
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies a generalization failure mode of finetuned LMs (latent generalization deficit, including the reversal curse) where in-weights knowledge fails to compose into logically implied OOD queries, and tests whether test-time thinking with RL-from-correctness closes the OOD gap versus augmentation baselines that fail OOD, though training sharpness and schema coherence are not examined.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work targets capability (deductive reasoning over in-weights knowledge) with no alignment or risk discussion.
other_metrics_reported: All F1, Train Recall, Heldout Recall, Primary Reference In Prediction, Pass@1 and Pass@16 at N=1 and N=16 (best-of-n sampling); thinking consistently outperforms Finetuning+RL and Augmentation+RL baselines, often matching ICL on ID and OOD; augmentation fails to generalize OOD similarly to plain finetuning; on pure reversal tasks thinking remains below ICL.

title: Frequency Bias and OOD Generalization in Neural Operators under a Variable-Coefficient Wave Equation
authors: Runlong Xie; An Luo

effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; mean relative L2 error per split and architecture
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured

relevance_sigma_justification: Studies OOD generalization failure of neural operators under structured distribution shifts (input frequency, coefficient smoothness), showing FNO's sharp error increase under unseen high-frequency inputs and a fundamental ID-vs-OOD performance gap; not compositional generalization and no training-dynamics or schema-coherence mechanism.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; focused purely on PDE surrogate model generalization.
other_metrics_reported: Mean relative L2 error across validation, ID, OOD-frequency, and OOD-smoothness splits; spectral error curves across sine modes for FNO and DeepONet
notes: Mean relative L2 error on ID split (lower is better) | rel-L2: id=0.198913

title: Predictable GRPO: A Closed-Form Model of Training Dynamics
authors: Rajat Ghosh; Datta Nimmaturi; Aryan Singhal; Vaishnavi Bhargava; Henry Wong; Johnu George; Debojyoti Dutta
task_custom_name: GRPO RL post-training on GSM8K; OOD eval on 8 math benchmarks (GSM-Plus, Math-500, AIME-2026, MetaMathQA, NuminaMath, OpenMath2, IMO-Bench, HMMT-2025)
arch_detail: GRPO RL post-training (LoRA rank 16, alpha 64) of decoder-only LLMs DeepSeek-7B, DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-1.5B, Nemotron-4B; paper's contribution is a closed-form reduced-order (stochastically-forced damped oscillator) model of GRPO training dynamics
train_data_note: GRPO on GSM8K; config: LR 1e-5, 2 epochs, batch size 4 (grad accum 4), temperature 0.8, KL beta 0.005, clip 0.2, LoRA r=16 alpha=64 on q,k,v,o,up,down,gate; OOD eval on 8 math benchmarks (pass@k)
train_regime_other: GRPO (group relative policy optimization) reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards; heavy-ball optimizer with momentum
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; key quantitative claim is closed-form trajectory fitting training reward to R2>=0.91 and group-size invariance of the mean trajectory (OOD transfer to eight math benchmarks)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; analysis is of training reward dynamics, not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Studies GRPO training dynamics via closed-form reduced-order modeling with OOD evaluation on eight math benchmarks, but its focus is optimizer dynamics and reward scaling laws rather than compositional or OOD generalization failure mechanisms.
relevance_alignment_justification: Provides diagnostics that separate reward hacking, advantage degeneracy, and policy concentration in RL post-training of LLMs — failure modes directly relevant to reward misalignment in RLHF-style training; scope is mechanism and scaling, with no treatment of AGI safety or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Stability threshold and overdamped-to-oscillatory transition only exercised in a softmax-bandit exact reduction (deep-network demonstration left to future work); reduction is local (linearization at fixed point) so it describes approach to saturation, not the global trajectory; curvature-scaling exponent K(M) inherited from empirical fits, not derived; within-group reward spread retains residual group-size dependence.
open_questions_text: Deep-network demonstration of the stability sweep; a model of residual group-size structure in within-group spread sigma_adv; treatment of the pre-linear phase; relating the fitted curvature-scaling exponent to lazy/NTK-regime slowdown to convert it into a predicted exponent.
other_metrics_reported: Closed-form fit R2>=0.91 to training reward; pass@1/pass@5 on 8 OOD math benchmarks; stability threshold K*eta*Kref>1-mu (Proposition 9); refresh-interval stability threshold; 1/G stationary fluctuation scaling; group-size invariance of mean trajectory
notes: OOD benchmark GSM-Plus (2400 examples), pass@1, base model (no GRPO): 25.64%

title: Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?
authors: Giacomo Camposampiero; Michael Hersche; Roger Wattenhofer; Abu Sebastian; Abbas Rahimi
task_custom_name: I-RAVEN / I-RAVEN-X analogical reasoning (Raven's progressive matrices, symbolic)
arch_detail: Large Reasoning Models (OpenAI o3-mini, DeepSeek R1) with test-time compute scaling; neuro-symbolic probabilistic abductive model ARLC (VSA-based) with entropy regularization
train_data_note: Symbolic I-RAVEN and I-RAVEN-X puzzles (10 panels per row vs 3, up to 100x more attribute values); I-RAVEN-X extended with confounding attributes and smoothened attribute distributions; no dataset sizes in excerpt
train_regime_other: no training for LRMs (prompting with test-time reasoning); ARLC trained with entropy-regularized probabilistic abduction
effect_size_notes: Paper directly reports 'o3-mini loses up to 69.6% accuracy' from standard I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X with uncertainty; converted from percentage to proportion
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies OOD/compositional generalization failure in large reasoning models: extending reasoning rules (I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X) plus perceptual uncertainty collapses o3-mini from 86.6% to 17.0% and R1 from 80.6% to 23.2% (near chance), while a neuro-symbolic model stays at 88.0% - a sharp quantitative demonstration of the generalization failure at the heart of the sigma-trap, though the uncertainty manipulation is synthetic.
relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment framing; relevance is indirect through reliability of large reasoning models under OOD conditions, which matters for trustworthy deployment, but the paper does not discuss safety, goal misgeneralization, or alignment mechanisms.
limitations_text: Three-bin discretization oversimplifies real perception modules which would distribute uncertainty more broadly; encoding uncertainty yields longer and less efficient LRM prompts that may impair reasoning; unimodal nature of LLMs/LRMs constrains evaluation to purely symbolic datasets, not extended to the visual domain
open_questions_text: Open-domain robust analogical reasoning models remain a mirage and need future investment; more thorough investigation of the simulated perceptual-uncertainty limitations is left to future work
other_metrics_reported: Reasoning tokens for o3-mini: 7209 (base) -> 18,589 (combined noise), 53,596 at high reasoning effort (accuracy 31.0%); arithmetic reasoning gains up to 65.4% for LRMs; random chance accuracy 12.5%; ARLC Pareto-frontier accuracy-cost scaling vs o3-mini
notes: 86.6% on I-RAVEN to 17.0% on I-RAVEN-X with perceptual uncertainty (paper reports 69.6% loss); 3.4x more reasoning tokens (7209->18589); high reasoning effort reaches 31.0% at 53,596 tokens

title: Systematic Generalization with Edge Transformers
authors: Leon Bergen; Timothy J. O'Donnell; Dzmitry Bahdanau
task_custom_name: CLUTRR relational reasoning (test k=2..10); CFQ dependency parsing
arch_detail: Edge Transformer: Transformer variant with 3D tensor edge states (vector per pair of input nodes) and triangular attention inspired by unification in logic programming, O(n^3) complexity; encoder-decoder version for CFQ semantic parsing; graph version for COGS; baselines: Universal Transformer, vanilla Transformer, Relation-aware Transformer, BiLSTM, LSTM+Lex, T5-small
train_data_note: CFQ: random-split training reduced from ~90K to ~20K examples to increase hyperparameter sensitivity; SPARQL queries >50 tokens filtered out; hyperparameters tuned on random split, compositional splits kept for testing. COGS: trained on graph representation of semantic parses
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; head-to-head MCD advantage vs baselines described in text (17-30% EM on MCD2/3 dependency parsing, ~3pp on CFQ, +9pp on COGS) without formal effect sizes
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; edge-state architecture analyzed behaviorally via ablations only
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets the sigma-trap: documents systematic generalization failure of Transformers, GNNs, and pretrained models on compositional benchmarks, then shows an edge-state + triangular-attention architecture (inspired by symbolic AI) recovers large OOD gains (CFQ MCD ~24.7%, COGS 87.4%, CLUTRR extrapolation), with ablations isolating the mechanism; focused on architecture, not training dynamics or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a model-architecture paper on systematic generalization in NLP and reasoning tasks.
limitations_text: O(n^3) computational complexity and memory footprint limit applicability: CFQ training requires filtering SPARQL queries >50 tokens and 1-2 days on 4 V100 GPUs, making larger hyperparameter search prohibitively expensive; hyperparameters for COGS were not tuned (taken from Ontanon et al. 2021).
other_metrics_reported: CFQ dependency parsing MCD3: EM 89.1 +-0.2, LAS 96.3 +-0.1 (10 runs); CLUTRR accuracy across test k=6..10; dependency-tree F1 mentioned for the dependency parsing setting; CFQ MCD per-split EM: MCD1 47.73+-3.63, MCD2 13.14+-2.12, MCD3 13.2+-1.38
notes: Table 3: mean exact match over MCD splits 24.69 +- 1.27 (SE), 5 runs; MCD1 47.73+-3.63, MCD2 13.14+-2.12, MCD3 13.2+-1.38

title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
authors: Thaddäus Wiedemer; Prasanna Mayilvahanan; Matthias Bethge; Wieland Brendel
task_custom_name: synthetic sprite-image reconstruction from latent factors (5-d component latents mapped to 64x64 RGB images)
arch_detail: Compositional model: component functions as 4 fully-connected layers followed by 4 upsampling-convolution stages, with soft pixel-wise sigmoid composition; contrasted with a monolithic non-compositional model matched in parameter count
train_data_note: Synthetic 64x64 RGB sprite images: two sprites overlaid on a black canvas with position, size, shape, color factors; training supports varied: random full-latent coverage, orthogonal support with two planes for the foreground, normal orthogonal support, uniform diagonal support
effect_size_notes: Table 1 (reconstruction MSE) values are not reproduced in the excerpt; only qualitative results are available
schema_coherence_notes: Paper analyzes compositional structure of the data-generating process theoretically but measures no representation-level coherence proxy empirically
relevance_sigma_justification: Foundational theoretical treatment of compositional generalization: derives sufficient conditions (compositional support, sufficient support, non-collapsed composition) on training support and architecture under which compositional generalization provably occurs, targeting exactly the sigma-trap failure observed even in models with explicit compositional priors; empirically shows failure localizes precisely where conditions are violated.
relevance_alignment_justification: Broader-impact discussion notes that better generalization could increase reliability and robustness but may amplify existing biases and hinder interpretability and certifiability; no direct safety or goal-misgeneralization analysis.
limitations_text: Only supervised regression with ground-truth latents studied (unsupervised setting left open); composition function assumed known; proof relies on the Jacobian of the ground-truth model and an initial-point technicality; guarantees hold only when the model perfectly matches ground truth on the training distribution.
open_questions_text: Extend to unsupervised identifiable representation learning; relax the initial-point condition via a self-consistency condition; learn unknown composition functions; extend error bounds beyond perfect training fit; relax conditions using inductive biases such as shift invariance.
other_metrics_reported: reconstruction MSE on ID test set (P) and entire latent space (Q)
notes: Single setup (sprite reconstruction, compositional vs monolithic model); no numeric values in excerpt; qualitative only

title: On Evaluating Multilingual Compositional Generalization with Translated Datasets
authors: Zi Wang; Daniel Hershcovich
task_custom_name: MCWQ-R (multilingual KBQA semantic parsing)
arch_detail: mBART50 and mT5 encoder-decoder transformers; ZX-Parse adds a trained aligning layer; mT5* setup freezes the pretrained encoder and trains a randomly initialized encoder-decoder
train_data_note: MCWQ-R: faithful rule-based translation of MCWQ (Wikidata questions, English/Chinese/Japanese) replacing neural-machine-translated MCWQ; MCD train/test splits with within-language and cross-lingual settings
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; cross-lingual vs within-language gaps reported as raw exact-match means
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; only t-SNE visualization of latent alignment
repr_analysis_finding: t-SNE shows latent representations of compositional utterances (especially English) remain distinct from natural MKQA utterances even after the ZX-Parse aligning layer, evidencing a domain gap, although the mechanism aligns representations across languages as intended
repr_analysis_layer: mBART50 embedding layers and ZX-Parse encoder (trained aligning layer)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap): it shows neural semantic parsers generalize compositionally within language but nearly fail cross-lingually on MCD splits (mT5-small ~0.1%), quantifies the OOD gap across three models, and diagnoses how translation-induced distributional shifts confound compositional evaluation; relevance is tempered by its focus on benchmark construction rather than training dynamics or mitigation.
relevance_alignment_justification: No direct treatment of AI alignment or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect, through compositional generalization and cross-lingual robustness as components of dependable generalization for deployed multilingual parsers.
limitations_text: Even rule-based translation suffers distributional divergence: train-test overlap analysis shows JA/ZH structurally 'simplify' the compositions (one structure per SPARQL fragment vs several in EN); neural-translated MCWQ contains systematic GT errors that models fit, inflating monolingual scores; MCWQ-R is restricted to Chinese and Japanese KBQA over Wikidata.
notes: Cross-lingual exact match on MCWQ-R: MCD1 JA 42.6+-1.7, ZH 43.0+-1.0; MCD2 JA 24.5+-1.6, ZH 27.0+-1.2; MCD3 JA 39.0+-2.9, ZH 43.2+-3.2; mean/SD of the six cells reported here (derived)

title: Compositional Generalization with Tree Stack Memory Units
authors: Forough Arabshahi; Zhichu Lu; Pranay Mundra; Sameer Singh; Animashree Anandkumar
task_custom_name: Equation verification (symbolic math, depth-based splits)
arch_detail: Tree-SMU: recursive neural network with differentiable stack memory units; baselines: LSTM, Transformer, Tree Transformer, Tree-RNN, Tree-LSTM
train_data_note: Depth-balanced equation verification dataset; ~40k train/validation equations of depth 1-7; large test set ~200k equations of depth 1-19 (~10k per depth), depths 8-19 unseen in training
repr_analysis_finding: t-SNE of learned representations: Tree-RNN representations are highly sensitive to irrelevant syntactic details (e.g., order of multiplication by 0) while Tree-LSTM and Tree-SMU cluster equivalent expressions; these representation variations propagate errors as expressions deepen
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization (zero-shot generalization to novel compositions) on math reasoning, evaluating models on four compositionality tests with a depth-based OOD split (depths 8-19) against strong baselines, and proposes a memory-augmented architecture to mitigate the generalization gap.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a model architecture and generalization-performance study on symbolic math.
other_metrics_reported: precision and recall on equation verification; stack-size ablation (stack usage vs equation depth); t-SNE visualization
notes: Train (depths 1-7) Acc 99.59; Validation 93.52±0.28; Test (depths 8-19) 79.57±0.16, Prec 80.56±2.11, Rcl 76.63±3.15

title: Simple and effective data augmentation for compositional generalization
authors: Yuekun Yao; Alexander Koller
arch_detail: Pretrained seq2seq T5 parser (BART also mentioned); backtranslation model used to map sampled MRs to sentences
train_data_note: COGS, CFQ (MCD1-3), GeoQuery (template/turnleft/length), SCAN (length) compositional splits; augmented data synthesized by sampling MRs from an induced grammar (P_train/P_test/P_uniform) and backtranslating them
train_regime_other: Grammar-based MR sampling + backtranslation augmentation; sampling distributions P_train (training), P_test (test, upper bound), P_uniform; integration via concatenation or pretraining on synthesized data
augmentation_type: MR grammar sampling + backtranslation; uniform rule weights vs training-distribution vs test-distribution sampling
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; SDs over seeds available in Table 16
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Perplexity curves over training show P_test-augmented models reach lowest test perplexity; analysis of why augmentation distribution matters, not a representation-level analysis
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap): shows augmentation distribution choice (training vs test vs uniform) determines whether semantic parsers generalize to OOD compositional splits, with per-split results across COGS, CFQ, GeoQuery and SCAN and analyses of why the training distribution fails.
relevance_alignment_justification: Purely a data augmentation method for semantic parsing; no connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Backtranslation model introduces noise into augmented training data (misses/alters structures, adds extra phrases); hyperparameters of the backtranslation model directly adapted from the parser without tuning; improving the backtranslation model could increase the method's benefit.

other_metrics_reported: Test-set perplexity over training steps; execution accuracy (GeoQuery); exact-match accuracy (COGS/CFQ/SCAN); breakdown by recursion depth and observed local structures

title: Unobserved Local Structures Make Compositional Generalization Hard
authors: Ben Bogin; Shivanshu Gupta; Jonathan Berant
task_custom_name: semantic parsing (COVR, Overnight, S2Q, ATIS)
arch_detail: Fine-tuned seq2seq T5, BART, T5-L, BART-L; LSTM decoder with copying mechanism + BERT-Base encoder variant
train_data_note: 5 semantic parsing datasets; compositional splits with no program overlap between train and test (template, MCD, and adversarial n-LS splits)
effect_size_notes: Paper reports raw EM differences between conditions (e.g., 74.9/45.8 absolute points on 2-LS-NOSIB vs template) but no formal effect size
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly characterizes when compositional generalization fails at the instance level: proposes unobserved local structures (n-LS) as the difficulty criterion, validates it across 5 semantic parsing datasets, and constructs adversarial compositional splits that collapse seq2seq model EM from ~94 to ~20 points; central to the sigma-trap analysis of compositional failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work concerns instance-level difficulty prediction and data sampling for semantic parsing.
other_metrics_reported: Decision-rule AUC (2-LS Transformer COVR 93.3, LSTM 80.0; Overnight syn/nat 84.6/67.9); 2-LS split EM COVR 32.8±43.6, Overnight 23.1±33.6; LSTM EM COVR 70.0, Overnight 50.8/20.5, S2Q 54.1, ATIS 64.4
notes: EM averaged across all created splits and 4 models (T5, BART, T5-L, BART-L); sd across models/splits

title: Compositional Generalization Requires Linear, Orthogonal Representations in Vision Embedding Models
authors: Arnas Uselis; Andrea Dittadi; Seong Joon Oh
task_custom_name: Compositional generalization in vision embedding models on dSprites / MPI3D / PUG-Animal (unseen concept recombinations)
arch_detail: Pretrained vision-language image encoders: OpenAI CLIP (ViT-L/14), OpenCLIP, MetaCLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINO(Dv3); evaluated as frozen encoders
train_data_note: Models are pretrained web-scale encoders (e.g., CLIP on LAION-400M); study itself does not train encoders
schema_coherence_proxy_other: projected R2 of linear per-concept factorization; within- vs across-concept cosine similarity (orthogonality); spectral SVD analysis of residuals
schema_coherence_notes: Measures how linearly and orthogonally representations decompose into per-concept components; e.g., within-concept cosine ~0.66-0.68 vs across-concept ~0.09-0.20 on dSprites, projected R2 ~0.22-0.68 varying by model/dataset; degree of linear factorization correlates with compositional accuracy
repr_analysis_finding: Representations show partial linear factorization into low-rank near-orthogonal per-concept factors; residual variance spread across many SVD components (not low-rank structured); within-concept similarity consistently exceeds across-concept similarity across models and datasets
repr_analysis_layer: image encoder embedding space (e.g., CLIP ViT-L/14)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in vision embedding models: formalizes necessary geometric conditions (divisibility, transferability, stability) for CG and empirically shows partial linear/orthogonal factorization correlates with compositional accuracy on unseen combinations, explaining when and why CG fails.
relevance_alignment_justification: Grounds the Linear Representation Hypothesis as a necessary consequence of compositional generalization, which is relevant to interpretability research; no explicit discussion of AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization.
other_metrics_reported: projected R2 vs compositional accuracy correlation across train fractions; within-/across-concept cosine similarity with SDs; residual spectral explained-variance-ratio (EVR)
notes: No clean per-configuration accuracy results in excerpt; results are representation-structure metrics (projected R2, orthogonality cosine similarities) over 3 seeds across models (CLIP/OpenCLIP/MetaCLIP/SigLIP/DINO) and datasets (dSprites, MPI3D, PUG-Animal).

title: When does compositional structure yield compositional generalization? A kernel theory
authors: Samuel Lippl; Kim Stachenfeld
task_custom_name: symbolic addition; context dependence; transitive equivalence/ordering (compositional toy tasks)
arch_detail: Kernel models with fixed, compositionally structured representations (theory object); empirical validation on convolutional networks, residual networks, and Vision Transformers; salience analysis of random-weight networks (0-20 layers, step/ReLU/leaky ReLU/rectified quadratic/Gaussian nonlinearities)
train_data_note: Compositional tasks built from component conjunctions (symbolic addition, context dependence, transitive equivalence/ordering); DSprites disentangled-representation models in appendix
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or quantitative accuracy results reported in the excerpt
schema_coherence_notes: Introduces representational salience S(k;C), a normalized metric of how strongly each component conjunction is encoded in the representation (computed from kernel similarities); analyzed qualitatively across depth and nonlinearity (Fig. 3), no numeric values given in the excerpt
repr_analysis_finding: Representational salience analysis shows deep random ReLU networks increasingly encode only the full conjunction (S(C;C) approaches 1 with depth), so very deep networks implement a look-up table memorizing training data without generalizing to novel component combinations; moderately conjunctive representations still suffer memorization leak and shortcut bias.
relevance_sigma_justification: Provides a formal kernel theory of when compositional structure fails to yield compositional generalization (the sigma-trap): it proves compositionally structured kernel models are restricted to conjunction-wise additive functions, identifies two concrete failure modes (memorization leak and shortcut bias) driven by training-data statistics, and shows when very deep networks memorize rather than generalize; relevance tempered by the absence of benchmark-scale empirical results in the excerpt.
relevance_alignment_justification: No direct treatment of AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect via understanding and remedying compositional generalization failure modes in deep learning models, which bears on dependable generalization.
limitations_text: Theory is restricted to kernel models with fixed, compositionally structured representations (treated as the best-case scenario for compositional generalization); extension to randomly sampled or learned representations is a conjecture with preliminary evidence (in expectation, and empirically on DSprites in the appendix).
open_questions_text: Whether learned disentangled representations are useful for downstream compositional generalization remains unclear; framework grounds research into learning mechanisms that implement compositional computations other than conjunction-wise additivity, and helps design hard benchmark tasks not solvable by kernel models.
notes: No quantitative results in the excerpt; theoretical analysis with qualitative empirical validation only

arch_detail: Syntax-guided Transformer encoder with dependency-parsing attention masking and weight sharing across the encoder; multimodal grounding over image cells; 1.9M parameters

effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; accuracy with std over 3 runs

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a multimodal grounding and generalization method paper.
limitations_text: Controlled synthetic datasets may not capture real-world complexity; performance tied to pre-trained parser accuracy (error propagation); hyperparameter search limited by computational constraints; failure on gSCAN splits D, G, and H (systematic output-sequence generalization).

notes: Avg over gSCAN splits (A,B,C,E,F,H plus D,G at 0.00); 60.49 +/-0.20 over 3 runs
