title: Diverse Demonstrations Improve In-context Compositional Generalization
authors: Itay Levy; Ben Bogin; Jonathan Berant
task_custom_name: SMCalFlow-CS (third semantic parsing dataset not named in excerpt)
arch_detail: Pretrained LMs for in-context learning: T5 (finetuned setup), Codex and GPT-3 (pure ICL setup); SBERT embeddings for utterance similarity
train_regime_other: in-context learning prompting (24 demonstrations) plus optional finetuning
effect_size_notes: No numeric accuracy values in the excerpt to derive an effect size from; qualitative claim that Cover-LS outperforms Top-K by a significant margin
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; structural coverage is measured in the prompt space, not the model's internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in semantic parsing under in-context learning: proposes diversity-based demonstration selection (Cover-LS) covering predicted output structures, shows it outperforms similarity-based Top-K across compositional splits, and ties hardness to unobserved local structures (ULS); limited to prompting methodology with no analysis of internal mechanisms.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an in-context-learning prompting methodology paper for semantic parsing.
limitations_text: Assumes diversity is obtained via different program structures and that recall matters more than precision in Cover-LS; does not predict whether a specific structure should be covered; does not consider more complex utterance features beyond words/symbols; retriever choice differs between NoFT and FT setups without a principled explanation
open_questions_text: Understand why different retrievers are preferred in different setups; consider both input utterances and programs for retrieval; improve gold-structure coverage with diversity-targeted beam search methods
other_metrics_reported: Prompt metrics for 24-demonstration prompts: symbol coverage, LS coverage, utterance similarity (SBERT cosine), number of unique LSs; ULS rate and T5 accuracy by test-example group (Fig. 4)
notes: No quantitative accuracy values in the excerpt; Cover-LS vs Top-K comparison reported only qualitatively and in figures

title: Exploring the Compositional Generalization in Context Dependent Text-to-SQL Parsing
authors: Aiwei Liu; Wei Liu; Xuming Hu; Shuang Li; Fukun Ma; Yawen Yang; Lijie Wen
task_custom_name: Context-dependent text-to-SQL (SParC-CG, CoSQL-CG)
arch_detail: Multiple parsers evaluated: STaR, RASAT, LGESQL, SCoRe, T5-3B; base models for p-align: SPIC (CONCAT) with BERT-Base/Large, LGESQL+ELECTRA-Large
train_data_note: Two constructed compositional benchmarks SParC-CG and CoSQL-CG, built by recombining modification patterns of SQL statements
effect_size_notes: Paper reports average QM-accuracy decreases on CG benchmarks directly (39.3 and 33.6 points) - captured in sub_experiments id_ood_gap
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; p-align operates on utterance-query alignment during training, not on internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Constructs two compositional-generalization benchmarks (SParC-CG, CoSQL-CG) and shows all current context-dependent text-to-SQL models degrade severely on CG splits (39.3 and 33.6 points on average), diagnosing the sigma-trap in a real database-querying setting; mitigation (p-align) is task-specific with no link to training dynamics or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a compositional generalization study of text-to-SQL parsers.
open_questions_text: Improving alignment between utterances and queries is proposed as a potential direction for future research on compositional generalization.
other_metrics_reported: Per-SQL-component QM accuracy (SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, etc.); error-type statistics (context info vs modification info errors); per-difficulty (easy/medium/hard/extra hard) and per-conversation-turn analyses
notes: Paper-reported average QM-accuracy decrease on SParC-CG vs development set (39.3 points), averaged over evaluated models

title: Improving Compositional Generalization Using Iterated Learning and Simplicial Embeddings
authors: Yi Ren; Samuel Lavoie; Mikhail Galkin; Danica J. Sutherland; Aaron Courville
task_custom_name: Molecular graph property prediction (ogbg-molhiv AUROC, ogbg-molpcba avg precision, PCQM4Mv2 MAE); controlled vision tasks with known latent factors
arch_detail: Standard GCN and GIN backbones (OGB defaults) with SEM (simplicial embedding method: linear transform + softmax-like discretizing operation) and SEM-IL (SEM + iterated learning with reset-and-relearn across generations); baseline+ adds an embedding layer for parameter fairness
train_data_note: OGB molecular datasets; half-split = train on half of training data less similar to validation/test sets; vision experiments (Figure 3) on datasets with known generating factors
train_regime_other: iterated learning: multiple generations of reset-and-relearn with simplicial embeddings under compressibility and expressivity pressures
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; differences reported as mean AUROC with SD across 5 seeds
schema_coherence_proxy_other: graph probing (linear head on frozen z predicting molecular substructure fingerprints)
schema_coherence_notes: Graph-probing AUROC averaged over 10 substructures (GCN, trained on molhiv): SEM-IL 0.878 vs baseline 0.801, Init.base 0.732; z of SEM-IL is more similar to ground-truth generating factors

title: Exploring Continual Learning of Compositional Generalization in NLI
authors: Xiyan Fu; Anette Frank
task_custom_name: C2Gen NLI (Continual Compositional Generalization in Inference)
arch_detail: Pre-trained language model (PLM) fine-tuned for NLI; exact backbone not specified in excerpt; continual learning across primitive inference stages S1/S2 then compositional inference (TaskCI)
train_data_note: C2Gen NLI: continual learning over primitive inference tasks (veridical 'ver', customary NLI 'nat') in stages S1/S2, then compositional inference; orders ver->nat and nat->ver; CGen NLI offline baseline; continual strategies ER-Res/ER-Buff/ER-Mir/AGEM/KD
train_regime_other: continual learning with experience replay
schema_coherence_notes: No coherence/compositionality proxy quantified; representation analysis is qualitative cluster-density visualization

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is purely about compositional NLI generalization under continual learning.

title: Layer-wise Representation Fusion for Compositional Generalization
authors: Yafang Zheng; Lei Lin; Shuangtao Li; Yuxuan Yuan; Zhaohong Lai; Shan Liu; Biao Fu; Yidong Chen; Xiaodong Shi
task_custom_name: CoGnition (German translation, CG-test)
arch_detail: Seq2seq Transformer (6 encoder + 6 decoder layers); LRF adds a fuse-attention module at each encoder and decoder layer (~12M extra parameters); variants LRF-Small, LRF-Rela, LRF-onlytop, Transformer-accu; RoBERTa-based and HPD baselines
train_data_note: CFQ with MCD splits (MCD1-3); CoGnition German translation dataset with CG-test set; results averaged over 3 random runs
effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; improvements reported as raw percentage-point deltas (e.g., -8.4% CTERInst, -12.6% CTERAggr, ~21% relative EM improvement over RoBERTa)
schema_coherence_notes: Representation entanglement (RE) is discussed as the failure cause and analyzed via attention visualizations, but no representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy metric is reported
repr_analysis_finding: Visualization of fuse-attention probabilities per layer shows LRF learns layer-specific fusion weights (e.g., lower layers concentrate on a few prior layers while higher layers attend more broadly), supporting the claim that shallow residual connections under-fuse earlier-layer information and cause representation entanglement; encoder-side fusion helps more than decoder-side.
repr_analysis_layer: fuse-attention modules at each of the 6 encoder and 6 decoder layers
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap): proposes LRF to fix representation entanglement in seq2seq Transformers, diagnoses the mechanism (shallow residual connections causing information forgetting and entanglement), and evaluates on CFQ MCD splits and CoGnition CG-test with clear quantitative gains (CFQ MCD-mean 43.4 -> 52.4; CTER -8.4% instance-level); relevance limited by its single-method focus and lack of training-dynamics or schema-coherence measurements.
relevance_alignment_justification: No direct connection to AI alignment or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect through improving compositional generalization, a capability related to robust generalization of deployed language models.
limitations_text: Improvements on CoGnition are moderate and LRF is worse than Dangle there, attributed to natural-language compositionality being more complex than rigid arithmetic-like operations; LRF adds ~12M parameters; task-optimized HPD still outperforms LRF on CFQ; simple accumulation (Transformer-accu) hurts performance.
other_metrics_reported: CTER (compatibility test error rate, instance- and aggregate-level) on CoGnition CG-test; fuse-attention probability visualizations
notes: Exact-match on CFQ MCD splits: MCD1 68.9, MCD2 43.4, MCD3 44.7, MCD-mean 52.4; averaged over 3 random runs

title: Block-Operations: Using Modular Routing to Improve Compositional Generalization
authors: Florian Dietz; Dietrich Klakow
task_custom_name: Synthetic algorithmic tasks (double-addition, logical rules/variable assignment); BPMNIST (block-permuted MNIST)
arch_detail: SMFR = Stack of Multiplexers and FNNs with gated residual connections implementing modular representation-preserving mappings (block-operations); Multiplexer enhances the FNN; grid sizes ~20k-500k params; BPMNIST ~4M params
train_data_note: Synthetic algorithmic task (double-addition) with OOD even/odd iterations; BPMNIST with 8 block permutations, one number held out per test permutation
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; accuracy and OODeven/OODodd metrics reported
schema_coherence_notes: No coherence proxy scored; modularity assessed qualitatively via routing-weight inspection and attention indicators
repr_analysis_finding: On BPMNIST, attention sharpness, permutation-undoing, and attention fairness tracked over training (good SMFR runs: high sharpness, learned to undo permutations); on double-addition, routing-weight inspection showed irrelevant inputs receive weight 0 and important ones 0.5, with learned interpolation B1=0.5*A1+0.5*A2 and FNNR gating weights approaching zero
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses the sigma-trap by attributing compositional generalization failure to static routing in neural networks; shows FNNs and Transformers only learn heuristic approximations while the SMFR learns the underlying atomic operations and generalizes perfectly OOD on algorithmic tasks.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; an architecture-level generalization paper.
limitations_text: Prior stability issue (softmax/sigmoid weights kept growing despite zero gradient) fixed via a regularization loss with threshold 20; regularization slows convergence but increases reliability
open_questions_text: Use the principles of block-operations to improve other existing architectures (future work)
other_metrics_reported: OODeven/OODodd accuracy by model-size category (Table 7); OOD accuracy over training (convergence behavior); attention sharpness, permutation-undoing, and attention fairness indicators on BPMNIST
notes: Perfect OOD generalization; 25 SMFR architectures achieved OOD accuracy 1.0 (Table 6)

title: Evaluating the Impact of Model Scale for Compositional Generalization in Semantic Parsing
authors: Linlu Qiu; Peter Shaw; Panupong Pasupat; Tianze Shi; Jonathan Herzig; Emily Pitler; Fei Sha; Kristina Toutanova
arch_detail: Encoder-decoder T5 fine-tuned or prompt-tuned (Small to 11B); decoder-only PaLM (8B-540B) with in-context learning (non-oracle and oracle exemplar retrieval via BM25/BERT and target overlap); also includes SMCalFlow-CS
train_data_note: Scale sweep of pretrained LMs applied to COGS, CFQ (Random/MCD1-3), GeoQuery (Std/Template/TMCD/Length), SMCalFlow-CS (8/16/32 cross splits); ICL exemplar counts reported per split (means ~12-59)
train_regime_other: fine-tuning all parameters, prompt tuning, and in-context learning of pretrained LMs
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured

open_questions_text: Improving retrieval for in-context learning is an important direction for future work; modeling the order of sub-structures in the target-overlap oracle could lead to further improvements.

title: Real-World Compositional Generalization with Disentangled Sequence-to-Sequence Learning
authors: Hao Zheng; Mirella Lapata
task_custom_name: Machine translation (CoGnition, ReaCT, IWSLT2014); semantic parsing (SMCalFlow-CS)
arch_detail: R-Dangle: Dangle variant with periodic re-encoding of source keys at interval, keys/values represented separately (R-Danglesep) or shared (R-Dangleshr); Transformer encoder-decoder; BART-large pretrained for SMCalFlow-CS; baselines Dangle, vanilla Transformer, BERT2SEQ, C2F, T5(+CSL)
train_data_note: ReaCT: compositional MT benchmark from IWSTL14 + 1.3M WMT candidates (filtered OOV); CoGnition; IWSLT2014 De->En; SMCalFlow-CS with 8/16/32 cross-domain examples added (avg target length 99.5, max 411)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured in excerpt
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in real-world machine translation and semantic parsing, extending the disentanglement-based Dangle model with interval-based re-encoding, and shows gains over Transformer/Dangle baselines on ReaCT, CoGnition and SMCalFlow-CS without sacrificing in-domain BLEU.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architecture/empirical study of compositional generalization in MT and semantic parsing.
open_questions_text: Finding a tradeoff between generalization and efficiency (re-encoding interval) left to future work, e.g., interval 40 yields 4x speed-up vs interval 10 at 50.3% accuracy on SMCalFlow-CS 16-C.
other_metrics_reported: compound translation error rate (instance-wise ErrRInst and aggregate ErrRAggr)
notes: CoGnition BLEU: ind-test 69.2, cg-test 59.4; ErrRInst 30.5, ErrRAggr 63.8; Table 4

task_custom_name: Machine translation (CoGnition, ReaCT, IWSLT2014); semantic parsing (SMCalFlow-CS)
arch_detail: R-Dangle: Dangle variant with periodic re-encoding of source keys at interval, keys/values represented separately (R-Danglesep) or shared (R-Dangleshr); Transformer encoder-decoder; BART-large pretrained for SMCalFlow-CS; baselines Dangle, vanilla Transformer, BERT2SEQ, C2F, T5(+CSL)
train_data_note: ReaCT: compositional MT benchmark from IWSTL14 + 1.3M WMT candidates (filtered OOV); CoGnition; IWSLT2014 De->En; SMCalFlow-CS with 8/16/32 cross-domain examples added (avg target length 99.5, max 411)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured in excerpt
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in real-world machine translation and semantic parsing, extending the disentanglement-based Dangle model with interval-based re-encoding, and shows gains over Transformer/Dangle baselines on ReaCT, CoGnition and SMCalFlow-CS without sacrificing in-domain BLEU.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architecture/empirical study of compositional generalization in MT and semantic parsing.
open_questions_text: Finding a tradeoff between generalization and efficiency (re-encoding interval) left to future work, e.g., interval 40 yields 4x speed-up vs interval 10 at 50.3% accuracy on SMCalFlow-CS 16-C.
other_metrics_reported: compound translation error rate (instance-wise ErrRInst and aggregate ErrRAggr)
notes: ReaCT BLEU: IWSLT14 36.0, cg-test 12.3 (significantly superior to Transformer by 0.9, Dangle by 0.5); Table 4

title: Improving Compositional Generalization with Latent Structure and Data Augmentation
authors: Linlu Qiu; Peter Shaw; Panupong Pasupat; Paweł Krzysztof Nowak; Tal Linzen; Fei Sha; Kristina Toutanova
task_custom_name: SMCalFlow-CS (calendar-domain semantic parsing)
arch_detail: Pre-trained T5 seq2seq model fine-tuned on original plus CSL-sampled synthetic examples; CSL is a generative model with an induced quasi-synchronous context-free grammar (QCFG) backbone and a parametric state-cluster model; compared with NQG-T5, LeAR, GECA, SpanBasedSP, C2F
train_data_note: SCAN, COGS, GeoQuery (template, TMCD, length splits), SMCalFlow-CS (8/16/32-shot compositional splits); T5 fine-tuned on original + CSL-sampled recombined examples
augmentation_type: example recombination via induced generative grammar (CSL); compared with GECA recombination
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; gains reported as accuracy points and relative improvements
schema_coherence_notes: Compositional bias is transferred via training-data augmentation, not via representation-level coherence proxies; no probing/CKA/RSA-style analysis
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses out-of-distribution compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) with a data-augmentation solution: induces a compositional grammar (CSL) from training data and recombines examples to transfer compositional bias to T5, achieving new state-of-the-art on GeoQuery and SMCalFlow-CS compositional splits and nearly solving SCAN; relevance tempered by its focus on a specific augmentation method rather than training dynamics or a general theory of failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No direct connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; indirect relevance through improving compositional generalization of deployed semantic parsing systems that must handle novel combinations in the wild.
limitations_text: CSL grammars can lack coverage (e.g., %XCSL as low as 6.6% for SMCalFlow-CS 8-C); T5+CSL-Aug. is slightly worse than prior models on SMCalFlow-CS single-domain splits, attributed to inherent ambiguity in remaining errors; GECA can over-generate incorrect examples; CSL sampling may not be biased toward target-relevant examples; QCFG limitations analyzed in appendix.
open_questions_text: Important direction: biasing CSL sampling towards examples most relevant to improving target-distribution performance; using pre-trained representations in CSL's parametric model; updating the parametric model with unlabeled target-distribution examples improves sample efficiency.
other_metrics_reported: Grammar coverage (%XCSL); CSL eval-set coverage 99.9% on COGS vs 64.9% for NQG; 90%+ runtime decrease in grammar induction for GeoQuery
notes: Exact match (All column, Table 2): T5 84.8, CSL 58.9, T5+CSL Ens. 86.9, Aug. 89.3; %XCSL 61.0; on covered inputs T5 93.1 -> Aug. 97.1, on non-covered 71.6 -> 76.9

title: Can LLM find the green circle? Investigation and Human-guided tool manipulation for compositional generalization
authors: Min Zhang; Jianfeng He; Shuo Lei; Murong Yue; Linhang Wang; Chang-Tien Lu
task_custom_name: ReaSCAN; GSRR (grounded compositional question answering)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: question complexity levels P1-P3; test splits A/B/C with C2 hardest
arch_detail: LLMs via in-context learning (Zero-Shot, Standard, CoT, PoT, proposed HTM with Python-interpreter tool generation); task-specific baselines MMLSTM, GCN, TRF, GroCoT
train_regime_other: in-context learning prompting (zero-shot/standard/CoT/PoT/HTM); no gradient training; baselines trained or finetuned
effect_size_notes: No formal effect size; paper claims outperforming existing methods on the most challenging split (C2) by 70%; HTM C2 95.8% vs GroCoT 27.3% and best ICL 20.6%
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; the LLM's compositional ability is probed indirectly by comparing performance on symbolic vs original semantic expressions
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure in LLMs (the sigma-trap): empirically shows prevailing ICL methods fail on complex compositional questions due to cumulative errors in long reasoning steps and intricate tool-making logic, and proposes human-guided tool manipulation (HTM) reaching 95.8% EM on the hardest ReaSCAN split C2 versus 27.3% for GroCoT; no analysis of training dynamics or representations.
relevance_alignment_justification: Relevant to LLM reliability under compositional distribution shift but the paper does not discuss alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; human-guided tool generation touches on oversight only in an engineering sense.
other_metrics_reported: Tool-generation validation pass rate (5/5 for HTM vs 0/5 purely automatic); ablation of code comments (C2 drops 12.8% to 83.0%); comparison of symbolic vs semantic expression performance
notes: EM avg over ReaSCAN splits; C2 = 27.3% (stated in text); GroCoT is the best smaller task-specific network

title: Multi-Sourced Compositional Generalization in Visual Question Answering
authors: Chuanhao Li; Wenbo Ye; Zhen Li; Yuwei Wu; Yunde Jia
task_custom_name: Visual question answering (GQA-MSCG, GQA, VQA v2)
arch_detail: Evaluates multiple VQA models: MAC, LCGN, MMN, BLIP-2, MiniGPT-4, LLaVA-1.5/1.6, CFR, Qwen-VL, PNP-VQA etc.; proposed retrieval-augmented training (RAG) framework with Dq/Dv retrieval databases applied on top of baselines

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a VQA compositional-generalization method and benchmark paper.
other_metrics_reported: Parameter sensitivity of retrieval weights wq and wv (best wq=0.6, wv=0.4); qualitative case analysis
notes: Level-1 LL (linguistic-linguistic novel compositions) split accuracy

title: NeSyCoCo: A Neuro-Symbolic Concept Composer for Compositional Generalization
authors: Danial Kamali; Elham J. Barezi; Parisa Kordjamshidi
task_custom_name: CLEVR-family vision-language reasoning: ReaSCAN, CLEVR-CoGenT, CLEVR-SYN, CLEVR-Ref, CLEVR-Puzzle, CLEVR-RPM
ood_difficulty_metric_name: CLEVR-SYN easy/medium/hard: number of replaced unseen synonym concepts per program (1 / up to 3 / all)
arch_detail: NeSyCoCo: LLM generates symbolic programs (dependency-augmented NL input), distributed word representations (GloVe-6B-300D, RoBERTa, SpaCy, one-hot tested) link linguistically motivated predicates to neural modules, soft composition of normalized predicate scores; baselines: MDETR, NSCL, LEFT, LLaVA, OpenFlamingo, ViperGPT, VisProg
train_data_note: Trained with CLEVR programs (GT and LLM-generated); CLEVR-SYN built by replacing concepts in CLEVR validation programs with unseen synonyms via regex substitution
train_regime_other: Neural module training with GT/LLM-generated programs; soft composition of normalized predicate scores; LLM program generation with syntactic parsing context
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; ID-OOD gap visible across CLEVR (99.7) vs CLEVR-SYN (92.1/81.2/73.4) but not reported as a gap number
schema_coherence_proxy_other: Pearson correlation (rho) between learned predicate scores of semantically similar (synonym) concepts; cosine similarity of predicate embeddings vs score correlation
schema_coherence_notes: Per-pair rho values (Table 6): left/left-of 1.00, large/huge 0.97, front/front-of 0.98, small/little 0.91; weak for ball/sphere -0.02 and brown/chocolate 0.20. Embedding cosine similarity correlates with score correlation (Fig 5).
repr_analysis_finding: Analysis of predicate-score space: substituted-concept scores correlate strongly with original predicate scores when embeddings are semantically close (cosine > 0.4); significant Pearson correlations (e.g., left/left-of p<0.01, large/huge p=0.01)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure in vision-language reasoning: NeSyCoCo composes primitive concepts via differentiable soft composition of normalized predicate scores from LLM-generated symbolic programs, achieves SOTA on ReaSCAN and CLEVR-CoGenT, and measures zero-shot generalization to novel synonym concepts (CLEVR-SYN easy/medium/hard) with per-split accuracy.
relevance_alignment_justification: Neuro-symbolic compositional reasoning for vision-language agents bears on robustness and interpretability relevant to AI safety, but the paper never discusses alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; relevance is indirect.
limitations_text: Method struggles with semantically similar but context-sensitive predicates (e.g., ball/sphere, brown/chocolate) not fully captured by frozen embeddings; generalization depends on high-quality embeddings (cosine similarity above ~0.4); 5 CLEVR-Puzzle errors attributed to incorrect annotations.
open_questions_text: Integrate NeSyCoCo into the DomiKnowS neuro-symbolic framework to make underlying neural models programmable instead of using a fixed neural architecture for predicates.
other_metrics_reported: Pearson correlation (rho) and p-values of predicate-score substitutions; cosine similarity of predicate embeddings; language-encoder ablation (SpaCy, RoBERTa, one-hot, GloVe-6B-300D) on CLEVR and CLEVR-SYN Easy
notes: CLEVR validation set, 99.7 +/- 0.02, average of 3 runs (Table 4)

title: Compositional Generalization via Forced Rendering of Disentangled Latents
authors: Qiyao Liang; Daoyuan Qian; Liu Ziyin; Ila Fiete
task_custom_name: synthetic 2D Gaussian bump generation (decode (x,y) coordinates into spatial image)
arch_detail: MLP decoder networks for coordinate-to-pixel generation; forced rendering via modular output-level embedding filters (one per disentangled input dimension) with low-rank regularization or factor-isolated data curation
train_data_note: Synthetic 2D bump/stripe datasets parameterized by image size N (2N stripes + 0-50 bumps); data requirement scales linearly in N with stripes training vs ~N^3 for bumps-only
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; results reported as data-scaling thresholds to 90% target accuracy and representational volume metrics
schema_coherence_notes: Volume metric (effective dimensionality of representation manifold) measured as a function of layer depth; representations remain smooth and uniform in OOD regions for the forced-rendering models, contrasting with re-entangling failure-mode models
repr_analysis_finding: Networks that fail OOD extrapolation re-entangle factors in later layers via manifold warping (volume metric collapse, memorization via data superposition); successful forced-rendering networks show early-layer stripe scaffolds that localize into bumps in downstream layers, with uniform smooth OOD representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Mechanistic analysis of why disentangled latents fail for compositional/OOD generalization (re-entanglement, manifold warping, memorization via superposition) plus an architectural/data intervention (forced rendering) that achieves zero-shot OOD composition; directly addresses the sigma-trap's compositional failure mechanism.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work targets disentangled representation learning and compositional generalization on a toy generation task.
limitations_text: Toy synthetic 2D bump setting limits scope; translation to large-scale models (diffusion, autoregressive, Transformers) and high-dimensional domains (vision, language) is an open next step; authors do not claim universal applicability and note interactive compositionality likely needs no one-size-fits-all solution.
open_questions_text: Scaling the principles to standard disentanglement datasets and naturalistic settings; whether modular embedding and low-rank factorization constraints retain utility at scale; need for new metrics and frameworks for partial and hierarchical compositional structures.

train_data_note: C-PRO task with 64 contexts of rule combinations; ANNs trained on 4 practiced contexts (stopping at 90% accuracy) then evaluated on novel contexts; pretraining on primitives/simple tasks
train_regime_other: primitives pretraining / simple task pretraining followed by standard training on C-PRO contexts
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; significance only via p-values (p<0.0001 for Vanilla vs pretrained comparisons)
schema_coherence_proxy_other: Parallelism Score (PS) - degree of abstract/parallel representations

repr_analysis_finding: Hierarchy of abstract representations: sensory-rule PS peaks in early layers, logic-rule PS in middle layers, motor-rule PS in late layers, converging with human fMRI cortical organization
repr_analysis_layer: ANN hidden layers (3-layer extended model); fMRI sensory/association/motor cortical systems
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies compositional generalization failure in ANNs (novel-context accuracy 28.79% vs 94.43% practiced) and shows pretraining-induced abstract representations restore human-like generalization, tying representation-level abstraction to the OOD gap at the core of the sigma-trap.

other_metrics_reported: Parallelism Score (PS); generalization inefficiency ratio; zero-shot generalization; sample efficiency (Combined model needs 4.23x fewer samples than Vanilla)
notes: Trained on 4/64 C-PRO contexts, stopped at 90% accuracy; practiced 94.37%, novel 28.79% (p<0.0001)

train_data_note: Ordered CommonGen built from CommonGen Concept Sets (4 concepts each); all 24 permutations per set form Ordered Concept Sets; 36 pretrained instruction-tuned LLMs evaluated
train_regime_other: instruction tuning (SFT / human-preference tuning) of pretrained LLMs
ood_metric_other: ordered coverage (Ordered Rate); Concepts Coverage; Diverse Rate

title: Differentiable Tree Operations Promote Compositional Generalization
authors: Paul Soulos; Edward Hu; Kate McCurdy; Yunmo Chen; Roland Fernandez; Paul Smolensky; Jianfeng Gao
task_custom_name: Tree-to-tree Lisp tasks: Active-Logical, Passive-Logical, CAR-CDR-SEQ, Logical-Passive
arch_detail: DTM: Differentiable Tree Machine = neural tree agent + differentiable tree interpreter (TPR-based, car/cdr/cons as precomputed matrix ops) + external tree memory; baselines: Transformer, Tree Transformer, LSTM, Tree2Tree LSTM
train_data_note: Synthetic tree2tree semantic parsing / language generation tasks; Active-Logical is the main analysis task
effect_size_notes: Paper reports mean accuracies across 5 random initializations; no effect sizes reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy (probing/CKA/compositionality score) reported; interpretability is via program-level operation traces, not representation geometry
repr_analysis_finding: Interprets inference as programs: Neural Tree Agent output traced over timesteps; at convergence operation/argument weights become one-hot (~94% correct operation sequence on CAR-CDR-SEQ); emergent cons-empty-tree operation found in Logical-Passive
relevance_sigma_justification: Core sigma-trap paper: DTM hits 100% OOD compositional generalization on lexical and structural splits while Transformer/LSTM baselines stay below 30% (mostly 0-19%), showing structure-aware differentiable operations eliminate the compositional failure mode on these tasks.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; interpretability angle is about debugging operation traces, not safety.
limitations_text: DTM requires input and output to be structured as trees and assumes the input and output languages share the same vocabulary; restricted to tree transformations; scaling to unbounded depth and lossy role-space compression left to future work.
open_questions_text: Extend to unbounded tree depth and lossy compression of the role space; investigate other tree functions (e.g., Tree Adjoining) and other data structures; translate between different vocabularies; scale to language modeling and pretraining.
notes: Predefined car/cdr/cons; ID = TEST IID 1.0±0.0; OOD lexical 1.0±0.0; 5 random initializations

title: Factorization Regret mediates compositional generalization in latent space
authors: John Schwarcz
task_custom_name: Cognitive Gridworld (stationary POMDP with latent variables and parametric interactions)
arch_detail: LSTM Classifier performing sequential inference over latent beliefs; Echo State (reservoir computing) RNN baseline; RCC (Representation Classification Chains): Classifier+Generator modules bootstrapping without shared gradients, trained via RL
train_data_note: Cognitive Gridworld POMDP; training episodes contain at most one testing variable (never the goal); testing episodes consist entirely of testing variables; teaching signals provided for a subset of training goal variables
train_regime_other: supervised training with optimal Bayesian belief as target; RCC embeddings learned via reinforcement learning (offline learning) from naturalistic feedback
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or numeric accuracies in excerpt; quantitative results appear only in figures
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; Factorization Regret is a task-level information-theoretic quantity (DKL between Joint and Naive Bayesian beliefs), not a model representation metric
relevance_sigma_justification: Formalizes compositional generalization over abstract latent variables with an information-theoretic measure (Factorization Regret) that explains accuracy gaps between architectures (Echo State matches Naive Bayes, Fully Trained LSTM matches Joint Bayes) and predicts a confident-wrong failure mode, directly addressing the mechanism of compositional generalization failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: Aims at goal-directed general intelligence and exposes a hallucination-like failure mode where confidence decouples from accuracy, but contains no explicit discussion of AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization.
other_metrics_reported: Factorization Regret (DKL between Joint and Naive Bayesian beliefs); confidence calibration / belief dynamics; relative accuracy ratios
notes: No quantitative results in excerpt (figures only). Fully Trained LSTM matches Joint Bayes; Echo State matches Naive Bayes accuracy; novel-combination generalization via RCCs

title: Swing-by Dynamics in Concept Learning and Compositional Generalization
authors: Yongyi Yang; Core Francisco Park; Ekdeep Singh Lubana; Maya Okawa; Wei Hu; Hidenori Tanaka
task_custom_name: SIM (structured identity mapping on Gaussian mixture with structured centroids)
arch_detail: 2-layer symmetric linear model (theory); 2-layer MLP with linear or ReLU activations for SIM experiments; text-conditioned diffusion model for validation
train_data_note: SIM: 5000 training samples per Gaussian cluster; d=64 by default; random rotation applied to train/test points; batch size 128, learning rate 0.1, 40 epochs
effect_size_notes: No accuracies or effect sizes reported in excerpt; results are loss/weight learning-dynamics curves
repr_analysis_finding: Tracks evolution of Jacobian entries (major/minor) over training: staged growth/suppression ('swing-by dynamics'); failure mode where a major entry is suppressed to 0 and the model is trapped generalizing only a subset of concepts, OOD loss converging to non-zero value
relevance_sigma_justification: Theoretically characterizes compositional generalization learning dynamics on a simplified identity-mapping task: staged growth/suppression of Jacobian entries, nonmonotonic (multi-descent) loss, and failure modes where the model is trapped into generalizing only a subset of concepts and never fully generalizes OOD. Speaks directly to why compositional generalization fails, though on a simplified synthetic setup with validation on diffusion models.
relevance_alignment_justification: No discussion of AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; contribution is a theoretical account of concept-learning dynamics in generative models.
limitations_text: Theory relies on assumptions D.4/D.5 (small equal-weight initialization, sufficient signal-strength distinctions) whose breakdown leads to failure modes; analysis limited to 2-layer symmetric linear model without bias terms; generalization to deeper networks, ReLU, or NTK regime left open.
open_questions_text: Systematically characterize behavior beyond the stated assumptions and conditions for OOD failure; generalize analysis to deep linear networks, two-layer ReLU networks, and NTK-regime models; investigate early-alignment of ReLU networks on the SIM task.
notes: No accuracies reported; results are learning-dynamics curves (loss and Jacobian entries). Validation experiments use text-conditioned diffusion models; SIM experiments use 2-layer linear/ReLU MLPs, SGD batch 128, lr 0.1, 40 epochs.

title: ExeDec: Execution Decomposition for Compositional Generalization in Neural Program Synthesis
authors: Kensen Shi; Joey Hong; Yinlin Deng; Pengcheng Yin; Manzil Zaheer; Charles Sutton
task_custom_name: Program synthesis by example (RobustFill and DeepCoder DSLs)
arch_detail: Transformer encoder-decoder trained from scratch with ExeDec execution decomposition (SubgoalModel + SynthesizerModel); baselines: plain Transformer, no-subgoal ablation, Latent Programmer; also few-shot LLM prompting

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a program-synthesis methods paper.
other_metrics_reported: Single-step subgoal/synthesizer/combined accuracy; per-CG-task results (Length-Generalization, Compose-Different-Concepts, Switch-Concept-Order, Compose-New-Operation, Add-Operation-Functionality)
notes: NoGen 95.5 / GenAvg 87.0; execution-decomposition subgoal training; end-to-end test accuracy

authors: Florian Redhardt; Yassir Akram; Simon Schug
task_custom_name: hyperteacher compositional task families
ood_difficulty_metric_name: fraction of tasks held out from training
arch_detail: ReLU MLP students (0.5M-10M params) trained on synthetic hyperteacher compositional task families with hypernetwork teacher; model-size scaling; transfer check with text-to-image diffusion models
train_data_note: Synthetic compositional task families (M modules, K components, hyperteacher); task encodings: identity, orthogonal, language, invertible NN, interval shuffle, fewshot; training support varied (compositional/connected/popular/unpopular modules)
schema_coherence_proxy_other: linear decodability (R2) of task constituents from hidden activations (task decoder)

repr_analysis_finding: Task constituents can be linearly decoded from hidden activations of models that compositionally generalize; task-decoder R2 correlates with compositional generalization across model sizes, task encodings and K components; also correlates with failures of text-to-image models to compose known concepts
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates compositional generalization (the sigma-trap): shows scaling data and model size alone yields compositional generalization on held-out task structures, proves MLP compositionality with linear neurons in module count, and links success to linear decodability of task constituents.
relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment or safety framing, but the analysis of composition failures in deployed text-to-image generation models touches on reliability of generative systems; otherwise a basic-science scaling/compositionality study.
other_metrics_reported: Linear decodability (R2) of task constituents from the input task encoding (input decoder); Pearson correlations between task-decoder R2 and compositional generalization with p-values
notes: Comp. gen. R2=1.00 +/-0.000 (SEM, 3 seeds); task decoder R2=0.95 +/-0.012; input decoder R2=1.00 +/-0.000; hyperteacher M=16 K=3

title: Learning to Compose Representations of Different Encoder Layers towards Improving Compositional Generalization
authors: Lei Lin; Shuangtao Li; Yafang Zheng; Biao Fu; Shan Liu; Yidong Chen; Xiaodong Shi
task_custom_name: CoGnition (Chinese-English MT, CG-test set; not in task vocabulary)
arch_detail: COMPOSITION: adds a composed layer between encoder and decoder that learns to compose different encoder layers' representations into keys/values per decoder layer (dynamic per-task); built on Fairseq seq2seq Transformer; CFQ variant uses RoBERTa encoder + randomly initialized Transformer decoder (following Zheng and Lapata 2022a)
train_data_note: CFQ MCD splits: training set 95,743, validation set, test set 11,968 per split; GPT2-BPE preprocessing
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; CTER reductions (-8.0% inst, -10.9% aggr on CoGnition) are error-rate deltas, not effect sizes
schema_coherence_notes: Paper hypothesizes syntactic/semantic representation entanglement but measures task-level CTER/exact-match, not a representation-level coherence proxy
repr_analysis_finding: Analyzes learned composition weights: bottom encoder layers contribute more syntactic information and top layers more semantic information; weight matrices show which encoder layers feed keys/values of each decoder layer (bottom encoder layer weights keys of upper decoder layers, Fig 4)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure (sigma-trap) on CFQ MCD splits, attributing it to entangled encoder representations and improving MCD exact-match from 17.9 (Transformer) to 59.4 mean via composed layer representations.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a representation-learning method for compositional generalization.
other_metrics_reported: CoGnition CG-test CTER: COMPOSITION 20.4% inst / 52.0% aggr vs Transformer 28.4% / 62.9% (6 runs); BLEU also reported (values not in excerpt)
notes: Exact-match accuracy on CFQ MCD1; averaged over 3 random runs; no IID results in excerpt

title: Systematic Generalization on gSCAN with Language Conditioned Embedding
authors: Tong Gao; Qi Huang; Raymond J. Mooney
arch_detail: Language-conditioned contextualized object embeddings via dynamic message passing (GNN-style) over objects, end-to-end trainable, with LSTM sequence decoder for action generation; ablation removes message passing module
train_data_note: gSCAN grounded language navigation dataset; 7 test splits (A random, B novel direction, C relativity, D red squares, E yellow squares, F adverb-to-verb, G class inference)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; mean +/- SD over multiple runs only
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Attention visualization shows baseline attends to correct target position but cannot handle novel direction navigation (split B) and picks similar training-seen objects over novel color-shape targets (split D); full model handles novel combinations via contextualized embeddings
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets systematic (compositional) generalization on gSCAN with seven OOD test splits, showing a language-conditioned message-passing model that matches or beats prior state of the art on most splits, including a documented failure mode on novel-direction navigation - core sigma-trap territory.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a compositional generalization method and evaluation paper.
limitations_text: Fails on Split B (novel direction): LSTM decoder cannot generalize action tokens for unseen directions; model generates action sequence from static scene, not modeling agent movement; high variance across runs on splits C, D, F.
open_questions_text: Introduce clues informing the model of view changes as it takes actions; transform novel navigation tasks into familiar ones via perspective change, conditioning on previous actions.
other_metrics_reported: Exact match accuracy per split (7 splits); attention-score visualizations; ablation (no message passing) results
notes: ID split (random, no systematic difference); exact match 98.6 +/- 0.95

arch_detail: Language-conditioned contextualized object embeddings via dynamic message passing (GNN-style) over objects, end-to-end trainable, with LSTM sequence decoder for action generation; ablation removes message passing module
train_data_note: gSCAN grounded language navigation dataset; 7 test splits (A random, B novel direction, C relativity, D red squares, E yellow squares, F adverb-to-verb, G class inference)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; mean +/- SD over multiple runs only
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Attention visualization shows baseline attends to correct target position but cannot handle novel direction navigation (split B) and picks similar training-seen objects over novel color-shape targets (split D); full model handles novel combinations via contextualized embeddings
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets systematic (compositional) generalization on gSCAN with seven OOD test splits, showing a language-conditioned message-passing model that matches or beats prior state of the art on most splits, including a documented failure mode on novel-direction navigation - core sigma-trap territory.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a compositional generalization method and evaluation paper.
limitations_text: Fails on Split B (novel direction): LSTM decoder cannot generalize action tokens for unseen directions; model generates action sequence from static scene, not modeling agent movement; high variance across runs on splits C, D, F.
open_questions_text: Introduce clues informing the model of view changes as it takes actions; transform novel navigation tasks into familiar ones via perspective change, conditioning on previous actions.
other_metrics_reported: Exact match accuracy per split (7 splits); attention-score visualizations; ablation (no message passing) results
notes: Class inference (push size-3 square, heavy concept); 99.33 +/- 0.46
experiment_label: gSCAN Split G (class inference); full model

title: On a Built-in Conflict between Deep Learning and Systematic Generalization
authors: Yuanpeng Li
task_custom_name: Synthetic two-output classification over partitioned input spaces (unseen factor combinations); equally-difficult-factors version uses two CIFAR-10 datasets concatenated by channel (6-channel input)
arch_detail: Fully-connected DNN and CNN reported in tables; also studies residual networks, LSTMs, and (Vision) Transformers; shared vs individual network depths varied 0-7
train_data_note: Synthetic tasks where some factor combinations (e.g. Y1<5 or Y2<5 for tile; Y1<9 or Y2<1 for one-shot) are excluded from training; equally-difficult version concatenates two CIFAR-10 datasets by channel
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly theorizes a mechanism (internal function sharing preferring boundary reuse) for why standard deep learning models fail at out-of-distribution/systematic generalization, and demonstrates accuracy collapse on unseen factor combinations across MLP, CNN, ResNet, LSTM, and Transformer.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; purely an account of systematic generalization failure mechanisms in deep learning.
notes: Individual network (no sharing); ID=Random Set Acc 31.2+/-2.5, OOD=Test Sample Acc 24.6+/-0.9; Test Set Acc 33.3+/-1.3

title: What Do You Need for Compositional Generalization in Diffusion Planning?
authors: Quentin Clark; Florian Shkurti
task_custom_name: Diffusion planning for navigation/manipulation (goal-conditioned Maze and didactic environments designed to require stitching)
arch_detail: Diffusion planners trained via generative behavioural cloning (no DP/TD); compared Didactic model, U-Net, DiT, and Eq-Net (shift-equivariant architecture with local receptive fields); inpainting-based goal guidance
train_data_note: Navigation and manipulation tasks; training data scaling studied as a factor; details in appendix
effect_size_notes: Paper reports completion rates (83.8 vs 11.16 vs 0.44 vs 0 in Maze) without formal effect sizes
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies compositional generalization (stitching) of diffusion planners on held-out start-goal pairs, identifying shift equivariance, local receptive fields, and inference choices as enablers, and showing replanning/augmentation/data-scaling alternatives. Reports a concrete OOD completion gap (Eq-Net 83.8% vs 0.44-13.4% for baselines), though limited to carefully designed stitching environments.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; contribution is architectural and empirical analysis of composition in diffusion planners for robotics.
limitations_text: Only considers environments carefully designed to require stitching; guidance strategy limited to inpainting, less useful for abstract goals (language-conditioned, multi-modal) or multi-task/multi-embodiment robotics datasets.
open_questions_text: Evaluate findings in multi-task or multi-embodiment robotics datasets; incorporate other guidance strategies such as classifier-based or free guidance into high-compositionality diffusion planners.
other_metrics_reported: unique successful trajectories (count); denoising steps vs completion rates
notes: Goal-conditioned Maze, held-out start-goal pairs; completion 83.8 +/- 6.4%, unique paths 116.8; roughly 7.5x higher than local-receptive-field-only model (Table I)

title: D3: Data Diversity Design for Systematic Generalization in Visual Question Answering
authors: Amir Rahimi; Vanessa D'Amario; Moyuru Yamada; Kentaro Takemoto; Tomotake Sasaki; Xavier Boix
task_custom_name: VQA: CLEVR 2-Hop/3-Hop OOD splits, GQA length generalization, TallyQA-Nouns/Cars
arch_detail: GPT-2 style transformer trained from scratch with fixed ResNet-101 vision encoder; also MAC (Memory-Attention-Control), FiLM, VectorNMN (with/without ground-truth program generator), MiniGPT-v2 (ViT + Llama-2 7B)
train_data_note: GQA length-generalization sets: 450k questions (30% of base replaced by short/long questions); CLEVR 2-Hop experiments scale 100k-600k questions; TallyQA-Nouns/Cars splits
augmentation_type: D3: data diversity design - adding diverse simple questions to training sets
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; results as accuracy percentages and change-in-accuracy deltas from D3 intervention
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; analysis is behavioral (test accuracy across training distributions)
relevance_sigma_justification: Studies systematic generalization failure in VQA across five architectures (MAC, FiLM, VectorNMN, GPT-2, MiniGPT-v2): OOD novel-composition and length splits fail (GPT-2 2-Hop OOD 23.7% vs 45.2% on 3-Hop A) and D3 data-diversity design mitigates (59.7%), squarely the sigma-trap, though framed as data curation rather than training dynamics.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a data-design study for VQA systematic generalization.
other_metrics_reported: Change-in-accuracy deltas (GQA length generalization: +1.94/+0.2 MAC, +1.35/+1.63 GPT-2; MiniGPT-v2 1-Hop Full +12.8); accuracy matrices across question-complexity distributions (Figs 6/8)
notes: ID = trained/tested on 2Nouns (40.67); OOD = trained on 2Nouns, tested on 3+Nouns (22.88); MAC arch (other)

task_custom_name: VQA systematic generalization: CLEVR-CoGenT, CLOSURE, GQA-SGL
arch_detail: TMN (Transformer Module Network): NMN composing Transformer-encoder modules per question program, TMN-Stack and TMN-Tree variants; baselines: standard Transformer, Transformer w/ PR (ground-truth programs), Vector-NMN, MDETR, LXMERT
train_data_note: Trained on CLEVR-CoGenT condition A and tested on condition B; CLEVR for CLOSURE tests; GQA balanced split for GQA-SGL; ResNet-101 object detector (regional features) or grid features as input
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; paper reports mean accuracy and SD across at least three repetitions
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality score; attention-map behaviour of modules analysed instead
repr_analysis_finding: Module attention maps show sub-task specialization: filter_shape(sphere)/filter_color(yellow) modules attend to sphere/yellow regions respectively; region queries attend to attribute keys and update region representations accordingly
repr_analysis_layer: within Transformer modules; attention scores averaged across all attention heads
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets systematic generalization (novel compositions of known concepts) in VQA on CLEVR-CoGenT, CLOSURE, and GQA-SGL: shows standard Transformers fail on novel sub-task compositions and that Transformer Module Networks improve over 30% on CLOSURE, directly addressing compositional generalization failure (sigma-trap) and how modularity mitigates it.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architecture and evaluation paper on systematic generalization for VQA.
limitations_text: GQA comparison models use different pre-training datasets (VG/COCO/Flickr30k/GQAu), so they cannot be compared in a fair manner; module libraries must be predefined; standard Transformer attention maps attended to relevant regions in-distribution only.
notes: Overall accuracy on validation condition B, grid features, mean+/-SD across at least 3 reps; regional features 80.9+/-0.25

title: Learning Algebraic Representation for Systematic Generalization in Abstract Reasoning
authors: Chi Zhang; Sirui Xie; Baoxiong Jia; Ying Nian Wu; Song-Chun Zhu; Yixin Zhu
task_custom_name: RAVEN / I-RAVEN (Raven's Progressive Matrices abstract spatial-temporal reasoning)
arch_detail: ALANS (ALgebra-Aware Neuro-Semi-Symbolic) learner: neural visual perception frontend producing object-based representations + algebraic abstract reasoning backend that induces the hidden operator on the fly and executes it; ALANS-V variant with perfect perception
train_data_note: RAVEN (Zhang et al.) and I-RAVEN (Hu et al.) datasets; systematicity/productivity/localism generalization splits plus regular I.I.D. splits
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests reported; component-level and end-to-end accuracies only
schema_coherence_notes: No measured representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; algebraic structure is an architectural design, not a measured proxy
repr_analysis_finding: Learned algebraic representation is generative: the hidden operator and attribute value can be decoded by isomorphism to generate a full answer panel when paired with a rendering engine
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly tackles systematic (compositional) generalization in abstract reasoning with a neuro-symbolic learner, evaluated on systematicity/productivity/localism splits of RAVEN and I-RAVEN, and dissects where perception uncertainty limits reasoning - squarely in sigma-trap territory.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a reasoning-capability and systematic generalization paper.
limitations_text: Despite accurate perception, near-perfect reasoning is never guaranteed; perception uncertainty marginalized by expectation introduces noise into reasoning; sampling via REINFORCE would add credit-assignment and gradient-variance complications.
open_questions_text: Sample from the perception module and optimize via REINFORCE to reduce uncertainty-induced reasoning noise, pending credit-assignment and variance challenges.
other_metrics_reported: Perception accuracy per attribute (objectiveness/type/size/color); reasoning accuracy per attribute and per generalization aspect - systematicity avg 72.04% RAVEN / 69.96% I-RAVEN, productivity avg 85.20% / 83.33%, localism avg 71.75% / 69.37%; per-configuration I.I.D. accuracies
notes: RAVEN regular I.I.D. average 74.9% (table of RAVEN{I-RAVEN pairs); on par with SCL, below shortcut-exploiting MXGNet/CoPINet

task_custom_name: Synthetic compositional string-transformation tasks: 24 atomic skills (Yuan et al., 2025) plus 10 novel atomic routing mechanisms; compositions of depth L=1..8

title: Systematic Generalization: What Is Required and Can It Be Learned?
authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau; Shikhar Murty; Michael Noukhovitch; Thien Huu Nguyen; Harm de Vries; Aaron Courville
task_custom_name: Synthetic VQA (SQOOP with #rhs/lhs splits)
arch_detail: Neural Module Networks: NMN-Tree (hardcoded layout/parametrization), N2NMN with Stochastic layout induction (Residual and Find modules), Attention N2NMN (learned parametrization); MAC baseline
train_data_note: Synthetic VQA; training on small subset of object pairs with #rhs/lhs in {1, 2, 18}; 200K training iterations
effect_size_notes: Paper reports test error rates with SDs; significance assessed via Fisher exact test on success counts (p=0.001), no formal effect sizes
repr_analysis_finding: Attention quality kappa defined on module attention over object/relation words: for #rhs/lhs=1 generalization strongly associated with high kappa (modules 1-2 focus on distinct object words, module 3 on relation); for #rhs/lhs=2 generalization achievable with blurry attention (kappa approx 0.6)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies compositional (systematic) generalization failure in synthetic VQA: generic models latch onto spurious regularities, N2NMN layout induction often converges to wrong layouts (p(tree) low) causing large OOD error, and end-to-end learned parametrizations fail on the difficult #rhs/lhs=1 split. Proposes attention-quality metric linking representation structure to generalization, a core sigma-trap concern.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; focused on architectural modularity and systematic generalization in grounded language understanding.
other_metrics_reported: test loss; p200K(tree) layout probability; attention quality kappa
notes: Table 1: test error 31.89 +/- 0.75% (error->accuracy); layout not learned (p200K(tree)=0.08 +/- 0.01)

title: Learning by Analogy: A Causal Framework for Composition Generalization
authors: Lingjing Kong; Shaoan Xie; Yang Jiao; Yetian Chen; Yanhui Guo; Simone Shao; Yan Gao; Guangyi Chen; Kun Zhang
task_custom_name: Text-to-image generation with compositional prompts (DPG-Bench)
arch_detail: HierDiff: fine-tuned from Stable Diffusion v1.5 (U-Net) with frozen FLAN-T5-xl text encoder, time-dependent conditioning and sparsity regularization on attention maps; extended to 4.8B diffusion transformer (HierDiff-DiT)
train_data_note: Fine-tuned on public LayoutSAM dataset (high-level text y + local descriptions); QWEN-v2.5 generates local descriptions at test time; DPG-Bench = 1,065 prompts; M=3 local concepts, lambda=1e-4
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; DPG-Bench composite and sub-metric scores with SDs over 3 seeds
schema_coherence_proxy_other: cross-attention spatial overlap (sparsity surrogate for latent concept graph)
schema_coherence_notes: Sparsity regularization Ln penalizes spatial overlap of cross-attention maps as a surrogate for a sparse latent graph; qualitative evidence only (Fig 6/7 show reduced overlap), no quantitative coherence values
repr_analysis_finding: Cross-attention maps over diffusion steps: without sparsity constraint attention lumps objects together; with sparsity, overlapping areas reduce; time-dependent conditioning shifts attention from dispersed global to focused local across steps
relevance_sigma_justification: Formalizes compositional generalization via causal modularity and minimal changes with an identifiability proof, operationalized as HierDiff, a T2I diffusion model whose hierarchical time-dependent conditioning and sparsity regularization improve composition on DPG-Bench (HierDiff 79.28 vs SD v1.5 63.18) - squarely addressing compositional failure (sigma-trap) from the generative-process side with theory grounding.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a causal-modularity theory and T2I generation method.
limitations_text: Condition 3.3-iii assumes no direct causal influences among variables at each hierarchical level, which may restrict representative power; mitigation via additional hierarchical levels or more involved conditions.
other_metrics_reported: DPG-Bench sub-metrics (Global/Entity/Attribute/Relation/Other); ablations w/o TD Global 85.15+/-2.26, w/o SR Global 83.09+/-2.49; Table 3 DPG scores for large DiT models (HierDiff-DiT 84.9)
notes: DPG composite 79.28; sub-metrics Global 85.77+/-1.21, Entity 85.15+/-0.66, Attribute 86.98+/-0.09, Relation 86.82+/-0.86, Other 87.77+/-1.45; 3 seeds; sparsity regularization + time-dependent conditioning | DPG composite 79.28

arch_detail: Model-based RL agent: causal transition model estimated via causal structure estimation + Bayesian network estimation (independence tests, intersection of environment graphs), planning oracle on the learned model; no neural architectures involved

title: Impact of Pretraining Word Co-occurrence on Compositional Generalization in Multimodal Models
authors: Helen Qu; Sang Michael Xie
task_custom_name: zero-shot ImageNet classification under concept-pair composition (GenPairs, ImageNet-Paste); VQA transfer (TextVQA, VQAv2)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: pointwise mutual information (PMI) of concept pairs in pretraining captions
arch_detail: CLIP ViT-B/32 pretrained on LAION-400M (primary); scaling: ViT-B/16+240, ViT-L/14, EVA01-g/14; LMMs built on CLIP for VQA transfer; images generated with Flux.1-dev (diffusion) and Llama 3.1 8B captions
train_data_note: CLIP pretrained on LAION-400M (400M image-text pairs); fine-tuning on ImageNet classification with on-the-fly PMI-based edit augmentation
augmentation_type: on-the-fly concept-pair pasting (PMI-based image edits) during CLIP fine-tuning
effect_size_notes: Correlation between concept-pair PMI and CLIP zero-shot accuracy: r=0.97 (key concept pair) and r=0.99 (average PMI) on GenPairs; r=0.75 on ImageNet-Paste; r=0.70 TextVQA, r=0.62 VQAv2 for LMMs
schema_coherence_notes: PMI is a data-level co-occurrence statistic, not a representation-level coherence proxy
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly characterizes compositional generalization failure in multimodal models: shows CLIP zero-shot accuracy is governed by pretraining concept co-occurrence (PMI) rather than composition ability, quantifies the accuracy gap (18%/14% on synthetic, 10% on natural images), and shows PMI-based augmentation fine-tuning nearly eliminates it.
relevance_alignment_justification: No AI safety, alignment, or goal-misgeneralization content; the paper is a pretraining-data analysis for understanding and improving compositional generalization in CLIP/LMMs.
other_metrics_reported: zero-shot top-1/top-5 accuracy; correlation r between PMI and accuracy; accuracy gap between top and bottom 5% PMI; VQA accuracy on TextVQA and VQAv2
notes: r=0.99 correlation (avg PMI) with 18% accuracy gap; key concept pair pmiD: r=0.97, gap 14%

title: Systematic Generalization in Neural Networks-based Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Models
authors: Hritik Bansal; Gantavya Bhatt; Pankaj Malhotra; Prathosh A. P
task_custom_name: multivariate time series forecasting (NARMA toy + PMSM electric motor)
arch_detail: Latent-dynamics forecasting model with MLP transition model; proposed modular variant with separate encoders for independent control variables and factored per-state latent transition model (Ours); baselines: standard NN (MLP TM) and Baseline+SC (separate control encoders)
train_data_note: PMSM electric motor: 80k data points, 4k temporal segments (T=10) for training, controls ud, uq and states id, iq; NARMA synthetic scenarios 1-4; OOD = control combinations from quadrants 2/4 of control joint distribution, held out during training
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level proxy; paper uses behavioral intervention testing (perturbing non-causal control variables) and argues separate decoders induce disentangled latent states, but no internal-representation metric is computed
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies systematic (compositional) generalization - forecasting under unseen combinations of control variables - and shows that a modular, factored latent transition model provides an inductive bias that substantially improves OOD forecasting relative to standard NNs.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architecture-inductive-bias study for time-series forecasting models.
other_metrics_reported: Intervention testing (MSE of state variables under additive Gaussian noise on non-causal controls); OOD loss vs forecasting horizon; relative error (OOD-IID)/IID
notes: MSE IID 0.89, OOD 27 (x1e-5), relative error 29.24; single-step forecasts

title: Latent Compositional Representations Improve Systematic Generalization in Grounded Question Answering
authors: Ben Bogin; Sanjay Subramanian; Matt Gardner; Jonathan Berant
task_custom_name: CLOSURE (grounded QA systematic generalization), CLEVR, CLEVR-Humans, synthetic arithmetic expressions (none in task vocabulary)
arch_detail: GLT: CKY-style bottom-up parser computing representation and denotation for every question span, inducing latent trees from end-to-end (answer-only) supervision; modules include a VISUAL module; baselines: LSTM and Transformer seq2seq models
train_data_note: CLOSURE systematic generalization benchmark for grounded QA over CLEVR-style scenes; arithmetic expressions setup also used
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparison is qualitative (96.1% on CLOSURE vs prior models near-perfect on random ID split)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy (probing/CKA/compositionality score); tree structure is architectural, not measured as a coherence metric
repr_analysis_finding: Evaluates induced latent trees: constituent recall 81.6% (CLEVR) / 83.1% (CLOSURE), average object F1 95.9% (CLEVR) / 94.7% (CLOSURE); missed constituents mostly differed by an extra prefix (e.g., 'any tiny green objects' instead of 'tiny green objects'); human forward-prediction test shows denotation trees help humans predict correctness (p<0.05)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses systematic (compositional) generalization failure in grounded QA: prior models near-perfect on random ID splits collapse on CLOSURE OOD compositions, while the latent-tree GLT reaches 96.1%, tying the sigma-trap to shortcut learning and global representations.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; interpretability analysis targets human understanding of model predictions, not safety.
limitations_extractor: No explicit limitations section in excerpt; conclusion notes the model is restricted to compositional computation
open_questions_text: Investigate the structures revealed by the model in other grounded QA setups; allow the model freedom to incorporate non-compositional signals, which go hand in hand with compositional computation in natural language.
other_metrics_reported: Intermediate-output metrics: constituent recall and average object F1 (see repr_analysis_finding); CLEVR (random split) accuracy 99.1%; arithmetic expressions benchmark setup; human forward-prediction study (20 participants, group A vs B)
notes: CLOSURE systematic generalization; 96.1% vs prior models that almost perfectly solve the random in-distribution split; no SD/seeds reported

title: Measuring Systematic Generalization in Neural Proof Generation with Transformers
authors: Nicolas Gontier; Koustuv Sinha; Siva Reddy; Christopher Pal
task_custom_name: CLUTRR (logical reasoning over entity relations; natural language proof generation)
arch_detail: Small TLM: 5 layers, 192 embedding dim, 768 mlp hidden, 3 attention heads, ~3M params, max length 1024; large TLM ~145M (20 layers, 768 emb, 12 heads); GPT2 ~125M from-scratch and fine-tuned; encoder-decoder 5+5 layers 5.22M params
train_data_note: CLUTRR dataset; models trained on levels 2, 4, 6 only, evaluated on levels 2-10; stories in facts template (amt template for GPT2); proof settings: no-proof, short-proof, short-proof-reversed, long-proof, long-proof-reversed
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes or significance tests; all accuracy results reported only in figures
schema_coherence_notes: Generated proofs are tested for logical consistency (proof validity), reported in figures only; proof validity measured alongside answer accuracy
relevance_sigma_justification: Measures systematic generalization in neural proof generation, showing length-generalization failure on longer-than-trained proof sequences, backward-chaining superiority, and better generalization without proof training - direct evidence on when and why compositional generalization fails in Transformers.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; focuses on measuring systematic generalization in proof generation with Transformer language models.
limitations_text: TLMs fail to generalize to unseen facts due to the combinatorially large entity-fact space in CLUTRR; encoder-decoder models are sensitive to training sequence length, failing in both extrapolation (levels 7-10) and interpolation (levels 3, 5); model size improves generalization only marginally.
open_questions_text: Deeper inspection of TLMs' underlying internal reasoning strategies, which appear efficient but harder to interpret.
other_metrics_reported: Proof validity (logical consistency) of generated proofs; answer accuracy per difficulty level 2-10 across proof settings (np, sp, spr, lp, lpr) and models (2.5M, 145M, GPT2 125M from-scratch/fine-tuned, s2s 5.22M)
notes: No quantitative results in excerpt (figures only). Small TLM trained on levels 2/4/6; reversed short-proof and no-proof settings generalize best

title: Systematic Generalization on gSCAN: What is Nearly Solved and What is Next?
authors: Linlu Qiu; Hexiang Hu; Bowen Zhang; Peter Shaw; Fei Sha
arch_detail: General-purpose Transformer-based seq2seq with cross-modal attention; ablations -V (remove decoder visual attention), -T (remove decoder textual), -X (remove encoder cross-modal attention)
train_data_note: Original gSCAN 360,000 training examples; new spatial-relation task ~260,000 generated examples from 18 templates (~32,000 unique instructions); smaller primitive-reduced splits 110,000 (compositional) and 74,000 (spatial relation) examples
relevance_sigma_justification: Analyzes which gSCAN compositional-generalization splits are nearly solved by a general-purpose cross-modal Transformer and identifies unsolved challenges (spatial relation splits V/VI, 64.4/62.4 vs 94+ on other splits), directly mapping where compositional generalization failure persists.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a benchmark analysis and new-task proposal for grounded language understanding.
open_questions_text: Use regularization to improve the cross-modal attention model on V/VI splits; explore architectural priors to improve data efficiency; evaluate sample complexity as future work (performance drops below ~40% of training data; no-cross-modal model drops below ~70%).
other_metrics_reported: In-domain exact match on seen relations: cross-modal model 95.52 (V) / 95.43 (VI); without cross-modal 93.14 / 93.90; data-efficiency curves vs % of training data

title: ClassicLogic: A Knowledge-Driven Benchmark of Classic Puzzle Games for Evaluating Compositional Generalization
authors: Mahnoor Shahid; Hannes Rothe
task_custom_name: logic puzzle games (Sudoku, KenKen, Kakuro, Futoshiki)
arch_detail: SATNet (differentiable satisfiability), NMN (neural module networks), LNN (logical neural networks); trained on Sudoku for entity/relational composition with zero-shot transfer to KenKen, Kakuro, Futoshiki; procedural composition via curriculum on Easy/Moderate puzzles tested on Hard puzzles
train_data_note: Procedurally generated puzzles; hierarchical knowledge base where complex strategies are compositions of atomic rules (e.g., naked_pair = naked_single + constraint_propagation); training only on Sudoku for zero-shot transfer; Easy/Moderate curriculum for procedural composition
relevance_sigma_justification: Dedicated benchmark for compositional generalization across three explicit facets (entity, relational, procedural composition) on logic puzzles; documents that SATNet, NMN, and LNN collapse to below 25% success on Hard puzzles requiring novel strategy compositions, directly exposing compositional generalization failure in neuro-symbolic systems.
relevance_alignment_justification: No alignment or safety framing beyond an aspirational closing remark about building 'robust, trustworthy' AI; the paper is a benchmark and capability-diagnosis contribution.
limitations_text: Only four puzzle families (no graph-coloring, temporal, or common-sense puzzles); the hierarchical knowledge base is curated from documented human strategies and is not claimed to be exhaustive.
open_questions_text: Community contributions are welcomed to expand the benchmark's scope to additional puzzle families.
other_metrics_reported: Illegal move rate (%) for relational composition; success rate on Hard puzzles for procedural composition (all models below 25%, LNN 20-24%)
notes: Table 3 entity parsing accuracy: Sudoku 79.7, KenKen 70.6, Kakuro 74.7, Futoshiki 70.5 (mean 71.93); illegal move rate 6.8/17.8/25.0/9.5

title: HICO-DET-SG and V-COCO-SG: New Data Splits for Evaluating the Systematic Generalization Performance of Human-Object Interaction Detection Models
authors: Kentaro Takemoto; Moyuru Yamada; Tomotake Sasaki; Hisanao Akima
task_custom_name: HOI detection with systematic-generalization splits (HICO-DET-SG; V-COCO-SG)
arch_detail: Four HOI detection models evaluated: HOTR, QPIC (DETR-style transformers), STIP (action-unit transformer), FGAHOI; optional encoder/decoder pretraining from DETR trained on COCO
train_data_note: HICO-DET-SG train covers 540 of 600 object-interaction combinations; V-COCO-SG train covers 160 of 228; split algorithm (seeded SELECT + VERIFY) ensures all object/interaction classes appear in train with multiple pairings and test scenes contain only held-out combinations
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; gap described qualitatively (test mAP much lower on SG splits than original splits)

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety or alignment; motivated by real-world HOI applications (e.g., self-driving, surveillance) but purely an evaluation and benchmark study.
open_questions_text: Authors identify four possible future research directions for improving systematic generalization performance in HOI detection, based on analysis of the evaluation results.
other_metrics_reported: train-data mAP (reference); test mAP per split (split1/2/3 and average); original-split mAP from literature (bracketed values)

title: Rule Extrapolation in Language Models: A Study of Compositional Generalization on OOD Prompts
authors: Anna Mészáros; Szilvia Ujváry; Wieland Brendel; Patrik Reizinger; Ferenc Huszár
task_custom_name: rule extrapolation on formal languages (L1-L6 regular/context-free/context-sensitive grammars)
arch_detail: Autoregressive LMs trained on formal languages defined by intersections of rules; architectures compared: Linear, LSTM, Mamba (state space model), Transformer (decoder-only), xLSTM; rule-following accuracy for ID and OOD (rule-violating) prompts
train_data_note: Formal languages L1-L6 (e.g., anbn, Dyck, anbncn) generated by rule intersections; OOD prompts violate at least one rule (zero probability under training distribution); rule extrapolation = staying consistent with remaining rules
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; study is behavioral (rule-following accuracy under OOD rule violations) plus normative theory (Solomonoff-inspired prior)
relevance_sigma_justification: Core sigma-trap study: defines rule extrapolation - OOD compositional generalization on formal languages where prompts violate rules - empirically compares five architectures across grammar classes and proposes a Solomonoff-inspired normative theory of when rule extrapolation is rational.
relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment framing, but analyzes when LM OOD rule-following behavior is desirable/rational, which bears on reliability and specification-following of deployed language models; primary relevance remains compositional generalization.
limitations_text: Human-machine comparison is only a small pilot study that provides intuition rather than a rigorous evaluation of human performance; authors emphasize this caveat for the human baseline results.
open_questions_text: Rigorous evaluation of human performance on rule extrapolation is left for future work; normative theory is an uncomputable ideal (Solomonoff-style) intended as a guide for practical models.
other_metrics_reported: Test loss (cross-entropy); ID and OOD rule-following accuracies for rules R1 and R2 separately; chance-level accuracy for each rule; pilot human study
notes: R1 rule-following accuracy; ID R1 0.200, OOD R1 0.275; R2: 1.000 both; chance R1 0.105, chance OOD R1 0.154; Table 4 parse inferred
