title: The Devil is in the Detail: Simple Tricks Improve Systematic Generalization of Transformers
authors: Róbert Csordás; Kazuki Irie; Jürgen Schmidhuber
task_custom_name: Mathematics dataset (MW) also used, not in vocab
arch_detail: Seq2seq Transformers and Universal Transformer variants; relative vs absolute positional embeddings; embedding scaling schemes TEU / no-scaling / PED; OpenNMT-style baselines
train_data_note: COGS trained for fixed 50k steps without early stopping; PCFG productivity split 300k steps; SCAN length split with cutoff at 26; five runs per model
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; IID accuracy ~100% across datasets while generalization accuracy varies (0.47-1.0) depending on config
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; analyses focus on loss-accuracy relationship, early stopping, and embedding scaling
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional/systematic generalization failure (the sigma-trap) across SCAN, COGS, CFQ, and PCFG, demonstrating that Transformer training configuration details (embedding scaling, early stopping, relative position) drastically change OOD performance while IID accuracy stays ~100%.
relevance_alignment_justification: Improves systematic generalization, a capability relevant to reliable out-of-distribution deployment, but does not discuss AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization.
open_questions_text: Calls for future systematic-generalization datasets to include validation and test sets for both IID and generalization splits, with harder generalization test sets, so model development can be measured without overfitting the generalization test set.
other_metrics_reported: Generalization accuracy vs loss correlation (loss not predictive of gen accuracy); epoch-wise double descent on PCFG; catastrophic failure analysis where accuracy drops to 0 and never recovers
notes: COGS generalization split, 50k steps, no early stopping; Position Embedding Downscaling (PED); IID validation 1.00 +/- 0.00, gen test 0.80 +/- 0.00 (Table 2)

title: A Minimalist Dataset for Systematic Generalization of Perception, Syntax, and Semantics
authors: Qing Li; Siyuan Huang; Yining Hong; Yixin Zhu; Ying Nian Wu; Song-Chun Zhu

title: Scale Up Strategically: Learning Compositional Generalization via Bias-Aware Evaluation and Data Collection for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Yu Qi; Zhang Ye; Xinyi Xu; Yuxuan Lu; Amitoj Sandhu; Boce Hu; Haojie Huang; Jonathan Tremblay; Lawson L. S. Wong
task_custom_name: Robotic manipulation instruction following with factorized instructions (color, verb, object, size, spatial); ManiSkill simulation and real robot
arch_detail: Six vision-language-action (VLA) foundation policies post-trained on demonstrations: pi0.5, pi0, OpenVLA-oft, GR00T-N1.7, XVLA, Genie-Envisioner; each model's default training config, trained until convergence
train_data_note: 200 demonstrations by default per training run; factorized scenes (target + up to 3 distractors) on Panda arm in ManiSkill; strategies Complete/Random/L/ V; real robot uses half the demonstrations
train_regime_other: Post-training / fine-tuning of pretrained foundation policy checkpoints on collected demonstrations
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons are raw success-rate differences across data-collection strategies at factor-change budget f=18
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured; analysis is behavioral (which instruction factors are grounded) via FDR/FDH
repr_analysis_finding: Factor Dominance Rate (FDR) and Factor Dominance Hierarchy (FDH) quantify instruction-factor bias: color >= object >= spatial >= verb >= size is consistent across six foundation policies (tau=5% and 10%), with color dominant and verb/size most under-grounded
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies compositional generalization failure in instruction-following robot policies: quantifies shortcut/instruction-factor bias with FDR/FDH, localizes under-grounded factors, and proposes bias-aware data collection that outperforms baselines, i.e., an empirical attack on one core sigma-trap phenomenon.
relevance_alignment_justification: Shortcut-taking policies that ignore the verb are a concrete goal-misgeneralization risk in deployed robots; the paper diagnoses and mitigates this bias, though it does not frame results in alignment or safety terms.
other_metrics_reported: LLM judge agreement with human annotations 88.7% overall (90.0 success / 83.0 overfit-f1 / 93.0 overfit-f2); Copeland FDH rankings per model; factor-change collection cost analysis
notes: Simulation OOD success, Spatial x Size factor pair, bias-aware (V) strategy at factor-change budget f=18; 48.1% (vs L 33.9%, Random 28.7%)
experiment_label: GR00T-N1.7 Spatial x Size; V @ f=18

title: ORCHARD: A Benchmark For Measuring Systematic Generalization of Multi-Hierarchical Reasoning
authors: Bill Tuck Weng Pung; Alvin Chan
task_custom_name: ORCHARD (multi-hierarchical arithmetic reasoning, seq2seq)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: tree depth (n) and cross-tree referencing level (easy/medium/hard via COPY operators)
arch_detail: Transformer 44.3M params vs bi-directional attentional LSTM 6.2M params; Fairseq seq2seq, character-level output classification via beam search; batch 128 on 4x RTX 2080, 500 epochs, FP16
train_data_note: ORCHARD: sequences of values 0-9 and operators {FIRST, LAST, MIN, MAX, COPY} over two nested trees; trained on tree depths 3-6, tested on unseen depths up to 12; six variants (MIN-MAX/FIRST-LAST x easy/medium/hard)
effect_size_notes: No effect size computed; results reported as point accuracies from figures
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy measured; analysis is behavioral (per-tree classification accuracy)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures systematic (compositional) generalization failure: both Transformer and LSTM fail to generalize to unseen tree depths in multi-hierarchical reasoning, with Transformer dropping to random chance (10%) at depth 12; but the paper is behavioral, without training dynamics or representation-level analysis.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a diagnostic generalization benchmark paper.
other_metrics_reported: Per-tree classification accuracy (first tree, second tree, both trees) across tree depths 3-12
notes: First-tree classification at depth 12 (OOD); at depth 12 the Transformer's both-trees performance degrades to random chance (10%); Figure 5

title: Compositional Generalization in Spoken Language Understanding

relevance_alignment_justification: Improves robustness of voice-assistant intent/slot understanding under cold-start compositional settings, which bears on reliable deployment of interactive agents, but the paper has no safety or alignment framing.
open_questions_text: In future work the authors want to further explore the impact of OOV slot values on compositionality.

notes: ID = standard split slot F1 98.42 +/- 0.09, intent acc 98.2 +/- 0.02; daggers = significant improvement (p<0.05, t-test) over BERT SLU; Table 3

id_metric_other: hacking metrics (sycophancy rate, response length in tokens, code gaming rate); detection AUC

title: Probing the Probes: Methods and Metrics for Concept Alignment
authors: Jacob Lysnæs-Larsen; Marte Eggen; Inga Strümke
task_custom_name: Concept Activation Vector (CAV) probing of CNN vision models; concept classification on image concepts (horses, dogs, primates, buildings)
arch_detail: CNN vision models (specific architecture unspecified); probing methods: Classifier-CAVs, Segmentation-CAVs, Combination-CAVs, Pattern-CAVs, translation-invariant (GAP) CAV variants; spatial linear attribution concept localization
train_data_note: Concept datasets for CAV training (e.g., horse, dog, primate, building concepts); concept training data size varied to study alignment scaling; hard-accuracy test set replaces backgrounds with concept-free random images
schema_coherence_notes: Paper's core is concept alignment via CAV linear probes; argues probe accuracy alone is an unreliable alignment measure (probes exploit spurious correlations); hard (worst-group) accuracy, segmentation score, and augmentation robustness proposed as alignment metrics; no numeric values in excerpt
repr_analysis_finding: Probe classification accuracy is an unreliable measure of concept alignment; deliberately misaligned probes exploiting spurious correlations reach accuracy close to standard probes; translation-invariant (GAP) CAVs increase alignment; TCAV scores are highly dependent on the probed layer, with some late layers lacking spikes for dog classes
relevance_sigma_justification: Tangentially relevant: probe accuracy can be inflated by spurious correlations, and the paper introduces hard accuracy (worst-group accuracy on background-randomized images) as an OOD-like robustness metric; however, the object of study is explainability probes rather than model compositional or OOD generalization.
relevance_alignment_justification: Relevant to AI safety through interpretability: concept alignment of CAVs/TCAV is a mechanistic-interpretability tool used for model auditing, bias mitigation, and adversarial detection; the paper shows probe accuracy is an unreliable audit metric and proposes alignment-based evaluation, but does not connect to goal misgeneralization or safety.
open_questions_text: Future work should investigate the extent to which CNNs encode the absolute position of features (concepts may be encoded at the channel level, in superposition, or using absolute positions), and tailor probes to both model architecture and concept nature.
notes: No quantitative results in excerpt; methods paper on CAV concept alignment

title: Neural Collapse Inspired Feature Alignment for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Chen, Z.; Zhang, M.; Cui, S.; Li, H.; Niu, G.; Gong, M.; Zhang, C.; Zhang, K.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
task_custom_name: Spurious-correlation OOD classification (ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces, NICO)
arch_detail: Backbone architectures not specified in excerpt; method learns per-environment local models and applies semantic masks to inputs at pixel or feature level
train_data_note: Three toy datasets (ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces) and one real dataset (NICO); samples partitioned into environments either by known labels or by learned local models with maximum-likelihood assignment
schema_coherence_notes: Method enforces neural collapse to a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF) on semantic-mask features as a training objective, but the excerpt reports no empirical measurement of a representation-level coherence proxy
relevance_sigma_justification: Addresses OOD generalization failure under spurious correlation via environment partitioning and neural-collapse-based feature alignment, improving OOD accuracy on four benchmarks; relevant to distribution-shift robustness but not to compositional generalization or schema coherence, and it does not analyze training-dynamics geometry beyond imposing the ETF constraint.
relevance_alignment_justification: OOD robustness is an indirect safety-relevant capability, but the paper does not address goal misgeneralization, alignment, or value learning; its connection to AI alignment is only via improved distribution-shift robustness.
open_questions_text: Investigate more effective and efficient environment partitioning techniques; apply the method to other domains such as segmentation and few-shot spurious correlation issues.
notes: Table 1: OOD accuracy 66.4 +/- 0.2
